questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
The police had accumulated reliable information that a man operated a large cocaine-distribution network, that he and his accomplices often resorted to violence, and that they kept a small arsenal of weapons in his home.
One day, the police received reliable information that a large brown suitcase with leather straps containing a supply of cocaine had been delivered to the man's home and that it would be moved to a distribution point the next morning. The police obtained a valid search warrant to search for and seize the brown suitcase and the cocaine, and they went to the man's house.
The police knocked on the man's door and called out, "Police. Open up. We have a search warrant." After a few seconds with no response, the police forced the door open and entered. Hearing noises in the basement, the police ran down there and found the man with a large brown suitcase with leather straps. They seized the suitcase and put handcuffs on the man. A search of his person revealed a .45-caliber pistol. The man cursed the police and said, "You never would have caught me with the stuff if it hadn't been for that lousy snitch!"
The police then fanned out through the house, looking in every room and closet. They found no one else, but one officer found an Uzi automatic weapon in a box on a closet shelf in the man's bedroom.
In addition to charges relating to the cocaine in the suitcase, the man is charged with unlawful possession of weapons. The man moves pretrial to suppress the use as evidence of the weapons seized by the police and of the statement he made.
As to the Uzi automatic weapon, should the court grant the man's motion to suppress?

choices.A: No, because the police were lawfully in the bedroom and the weapon was immediately identifiable as being subject to seizure.
choices.B: No, because the police were lawfully in the house and had probable cause to believe that weapons were in the house.
choices.C: Yes, because once the object of the warrant—the brown suitcase—had been found and seized, no further search of the house was permitted.
choices.D: Yes, because the search exceeded the scope needed to find out if other persons were present.

questions.explanation:
A court should suppress evidence taken during a Fourth Amendment search or seizure conducted without a warrant or an exception to the warrant requirement. A protective sweep—ie, a quick, warrantless search of the premises made incident to an arrest—is reasonable if:

  • police have a reasonable suspicion (ie, a belief based on specific and articulable facts) that there is someone who poses a threat in the area being swept and
  • the sweep is limited to a cursery inspection of places in which a person could hide (eg, closet, laundry room).

Evidence or contraband found in plain view during a protective sweep may be seized without a warrant and admitted against the defendant at trial.

Here, the man was known to have violent accomplices, so the police had a reasonable suspicion that there was someone who posed a threat in the home. This authorized the protective sweep after the suitcase was seized and the man was arrested (Choice C). But that sweep should have been limited to places where persons could hide—not a box on a closet shelf. Therefore, the Uzi found in that box should be suppressed.

(Choice A) The police were lawfully in the bedroom and the Uzi was immediately identifiable as contraband once the box in the closet was opened. But they wrongfully opened that box since a person could not hide there. Therefore, the Uzi found in the box should not be admitted as evidence at trial.

(Choice B) Although the police were lawfully in the house to execute the search warrant for the suitcase and cocaine, the warrant did not authorize the seizure of weapons. And although the police had probable cause to believe that there were weapons in the house, this did not permit their continued search of the home once the suitcase and cocaine were seized.

📌 Educational Objective

Police may conduct a protective sweep—a quick, warrantless search of the premises made incident to an arrest— if (1) they have a reasonable suspicion that there is a dangerous person in the area to be swept and (2) the search is limited to a cursory inspection of places where a person could hide.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Maryland v. Buie, 494 U.S. 325, 334–36 (1990) (explaining that officers may conduct a protective sweep if they have reasonable suspicion that a dangerous person is in the area swept).
questions.zh-question:
警方已掌握可靠情报，一名男子经营着一个庞大的可卡因分销网络，他和他的同伙经常诉诸暴力，并在其家中存放了少量武器。

一天，警方接到可靠情报，一个装有可卡因的带皮带的棕色大手提箱已被送到该男子家中，并将在第二天早上被转移到一个分销点。警方获得了一份有效的搜查令，以搜查并扣押该棕色手提箱和可卡因，然后他们前往该男子的住所。

警察敲了敲该男子的门，并喊道：“警察。开门。我们有搜查令。”几秒钟后无人回应，警察便强行破门而入。听到地下室有噪音，警察跑下楼，发现该男子和一个带皮带的棕色大手提箱。他们扣押了手提箱，并给该男子戴上手铐。对其进行人身搜查时，发现了一把.45口径的手枪。该男子咒骂警察说：“要不是那个该死的告密者，你们根本抓不到我的人赃俱获！”

随后，警察在整栋房子里散开，搜查了每个房间和壁橱。他们没有发现其他人，但一名警官在该男子卧室的一个壁橱架子上的盒子里发现了一把Uzi自动武器。

除了与手提箱中的可卡因有关的指控外，该男子还被控非法持有武器。该男子在审前提出动议，要求排除警方缴获的武器及其所作陈述作为证据使用。

关于那把Uzi自动武器，法院是否应批准该男子的排除动议？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为警察合法地身处卧室，并且该武器可立即被辨认为应予扣押的物品。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为警察合法地身处该房屋内，并有合理根据相信房屋内有武器。
zh-choices.C: 是的，因为一旦搜查令的目标——那个棕色手提箱——被找到并扣押，就不再允许对房屋进行进一步搜查。
zh-choices.D: 是的，因为搜查超出了查明是否有其他人在场所需的范围。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Search and seizure

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：警察执行逮捕后的 保护性搜查（protective sweep），能不能把箱子外的盒子也翻开。

三秒认题路径：

有逮捕 → 查保护性搜查 → 只能看能藏人处 → 盒子不是藏人处 → 证据压掉

核心法律规则

搜查逮捕附带的 保护性搜查（protective sweep），前提是警方有具体、可陈述事实支持的合理怀疑，认为现场还有会带来危险的人；而且搜查只能是快速、简略地扫过 places where a person could hide。

所以，警察可以看床下、衣柜、洗衣房这类能藏人的地方，但不能借这个名义去翻不能藏人的盒子、抽屉内盒或包裹。明视（plain view） 只救合法进入后的偶然发现，不救越界开的地方。

核心判例： Maryland v. Buie - 它把本题锁死在两步：先有危险怀疑，再只扫能藏人的地方。

思维导图

先问：这是不是为了找“会躲人的地方”？
是有逮捕 + 现场可能还有同伙
能做快速扫过衣柜、床底、洗衣房
卡死点：只能看“人藏得下”的地方
否去翻盒子、包裹、架子上的小物箱
直接越界：这不是保护性搜查范围
本题触发链：发现枪支网络 + 可能有暴力同伙 → 逮捕后搜屋 → 打开壁橱架上的盒子 → 盒子不能藏人 → Uzi 该压掉

考点陷阱

你可能会想：警察已经合法进屋，又是在找武器，所以看到 Uzi 就能收走。

但考试真正问的是：他们开盒子那一步有没有超出 保护性搜查（protective sweep） 的范围。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里警方在楼里“looking in every room and closet”之后又去开楼上壁橱里的盒子，这一步已经不只是找人；盒子里不能藏人，所以 Uzi 要压掉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 现行可见误认

✕ A: 把“合法在场 + 现行可见”套过头了，plain view 不是先越界开盒再补救。

❌ 法律适用 | 概括授权误判

✕ B: 以为“屋里可能有武器”就能继续搜全屋，错把怀疑当成一般搜查许可。

❌ 事实误判 | 找到即停偷换

✕ C: 把找到手提箱后“整屋都得停”说得太绝对，警察仍可做限于藏人处的保护性搜查。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是逮捕附带搜查，再只盯“能不能藏人”这条线，别被“屋里有武器”带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：保护性搜查（protective sweep） 只能扫“人能藏”的地方，不能借找人名义翻盒子。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 这类口诀是讲中间上诉例外；本题不是上诉题，直接记 Buie 的两步规则就够了。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
A police officer stopped a driver who had run a red light. Upon approaching the car, the officer noticed a strong odor of alcohol and immediately asked whether the driver had been drinking. The driver admitted having had several alcoholic drinks that evening.
The driver, charged with driving while intoxicated, moved to suppress the officer's testimony regarding the driver's statement about his drinking. The driver argued that the officer had elicited the statement without providing the requisite Miranda warnings. The prosecutor has responded that the statement should be allowed in the prosecution's case-in-chief or, at a minimum, should be allowed as impeachment in the event the driver testifies and denies drinking.
How should the court rule regarding the driver's statement admitting his drinking?

choices.A: The statement should be allowed, because although the driver was in custody, the officer's spontaneous utterance upon smelling alcohol did not rise to the level of interrogation.
choices.B: The statement should be allowed, because the driver was not in custody for Miranda purposes when the admission was made.
choices.C: The statement should be suppressed both in the prosecution's case-in-chief and as impeachment evidence, even if the driver testifies.
choices.D: The statement should be suppressed in the prosecution's case-in-chief, but it may be used as impeachment evidence if the driver testifies.

questions.explanation:
A defendant's motion to suppress an incriminating statement should be granted if law enforcement failed to provide Miranda warnings prior to a custodial interrogation. A custodial interrogation occurs when a person is:

  • in custody – placed under formal arrest or restrained in his/her freedom of movement to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to terminate the encounter and leave and
  • subjected to interrogation – express questions, words, or actions directed at a suspect that an officer knows or should know are likely to elicit an incriminating response.

Although traffic stops restrain freedom of movement, drivers are generally not in custody for Miranda purposes because those police encounters are typically brief.

Here, the officer stopped the driver for a red-light violation (traffic stop). The officer noticed a strong odor of alcohol and immediately asked the driver if he had been drinking (interrogation). However, the officer was not required to give Miranda warnings before doing so because the driver was not in custody for Miranda purposes. Therefore, the driver's statement admitting his drinking should be allowed in the prosecution's case-in-chief.

(Choice A) The officer's question about drinking was directed at the driver and reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response; therefore, it was an interrogation. But since the driver was not in custody, his statement should be admitted.

(Choices C & D) Since the officer was not required to provide Miranda warnings, the prosecution should be allowed to use the driver's admission in its case-in-chief. But even if that admission was suppressed, it could be used as impeachment evidence if the driver later testifies.

📌 Educational Objective

Miranda warnings protect persons from self-incrimination when they are in custody and subjected to interrogation (custodial interrogations). Since drivers are generally not in custody during traffic stops, Miranda warnings need not be provided before brief police questioning.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 468–70 (1966) (listing Miranda warnings).
  • Berkemer v. McCarty, 468 U.S. 420, 440 (1984) (recognizing that a person is not in custody during an investigatory detention).
questions.zh-question:
一名警察拦下了一名闯红灯的司机。在靠近车辆时，警察闻到一股浓烈的酒味，并立即询问司机是否饮酒。司机承认当晚喝了几杯含酒精的饮料。

该司机被控酒后驾车，并动议排除警察就司机关于其饮酒的陈述所作的证词。司机辩称，警察在未提供必要的米兰达警告的情况下诱使其作出陈述。检察官则回应称，该陈述应被允许在控方主案中采纳，或者至少在司机作证并否认饮酒时，应被允许用作弹劾证据。

法院应如何就司机承认其饮酒的陈述作出裁决？

zh-choices.A: 该陈述应被采纳，因为尽管司机处于被羁押状态，但警察在闻到酒味后的自发询问并未达到审讯的程度。
zh-choices.B: 该陈述应被采纳，因为在作出承认时，司机并未因米兰达规则之目的而处于被羁押状态。
zh-choices.C: 无论司机是否作证，该陈述在控方主案中和作为弹劾证据都应被排除。
zh-choices.D: 该陈述在控方主案中应被排除，但如果司机作证，则可被用作弹劾证据。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：Miranda 警告（Miranda warnings）要不要给，关键看是不是羁押性讯问（custodial interrogation）；单纯交通拦停通常还不算“羁押”。

三秒认题路径：

交通拦停 → 先问喝酒 → 要不要警告 → 先看是否羁押 → 本题否

核心法律规则

只抓这一条就够了

Miranda 警告（Miranda warnings）只在政府把人放进羁押（custody），并进行讯问（interrogation）时才需要给。这里的custody考场意思：不是“警察有接触”就算，而是人已经被正式逮捕，或被限制到理性人不会觉得自己能离开的程度。

交通拦停虽然会限制行动，但一般仍是短暂的调查性扣留（investigatory detention），所以通常不算 Miranda 的羁押。interrogation考场意思：警察的提问确实是在引发自证其罪，但前提是先得“羁押”成立。

核心判例： Berkemer v. McCarty —— 交通拦停通常不构成 Miranda 下的羁押，所以简短盘问前一般不用先给警告。

思维导图

先问：有没有 Miranda 触发？
1. 是不是 羁押（custody）？
本题卡在这里：只是红灯拦停 + 问一句喝没喝酒，还没到“正式逮捕/无法离开”。
→
交通拦停通常只是短暂扣留，不是 Miranda 羁押。
2. 有没有 讯问（interrogation）？
有：警察直接问“你喝酒了吗”，这是会诱发不利回答的提问。
3. 两个都成立才要警告
只要“羁押”不成立，后面就不用继续卡 Miranda。
结论： 这句认罪式回答可进 case-in-chief。
正确答案：B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：警察已经闻到酒味，还直接发问，这明显是在“套话”，所以一定要先给 Miranda。

但考试真正问的是：先看有没有羁押（custody），不是先看警察有没有“想问出不利答案”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干红灯交通拦停仍属短暂调查性扣留，不是 Miranda 羁押，所以警察先问一句是否饮酒，口头承认可以进检方主证。

❌ 概念混淆 | 讯问当作羁押

✕ A: 把 interrogation 当成自动触发点了，但没先过羁押这关。

❌ 法律适用 | 过度排除证据

✕ C: 误以为只要没警告就全都不能用，连本案的非羁押盘问都一起打掉。

❌ 事实误判 | 先假设已被压制

✕ D: 把“若被压制后还能弹劾”搬进来，但这里压根没到先排除的前提。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是不是 traffic stop，再问有没有真正进入 Miranda 的羁押门槛。

考场速记

记忆口诀：Miranda 先看“custody + interrogation”两把锁，少一把就不触发；traffic stop 常常卡在第一把锁外面。

再记一句：Berkemer v. McCarty = 交通拦停通常不算 Miranda 羁押。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A state enacted a statute "to regulate administratively the conduct of motor vehicle junkyard businesses in order to deter motor vehicle theft and trafficking in stolen motor vehicles or parts thereof." The statute requires a junkyard owner or operator "to permit representatives of the Department of Motor Vehicles or of any law enforcement agency upon request during normal business hours to take physical inventory of motor vehicles and parts thereof on the premises." The statute also states that a failure to comply with any of its requirements constitutes a felony.
In a large city located in this state, two police officers assigned to the automobile crimes unit periodically visited all motor vehicle junkyards in the city to make the inspections permitted by the statute. A woman owned such a business. One summer day, the officers asked to inspect the vehicles on her lot. The woman asked, "Do I have a choice?" The officers told her she did not. The officers then conducted their inspection and discovered three stolen automobiles.
The woman is charged with receiving stolen property. She moves pretrial to suppress the evidence relating to the three automobiles on the ground that the inspection was unconstitutional.
How should the court rule on her motion to suppress this evidence?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because administrative searches of commercial establishments do not require warrants.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the statute deals reasonably with a highly regulated industry.
choices.C: Sustain the motion, because the stated regulatory purpose of the statute is a pretext to circumvent the warrant requirement in conducting criminal investigations.
choices.D: Sustain the motion, because the statute grants unbridled discretion to law enforcement officers to make warrantless searches.

questions.explanation:
Administrative or regulatory searches
Ordinary industries Warrant based on less stringent probable cause standard—ie:
  • search meets reasonable & neutral administrative standard or
  • public interest justifies search
Highly regulated
industries		 No warrant required if:
  • statute/regulatory scheme involves substantial government interest
  • warrantless search necessary to further interest and
  • statute provides constitutionally adequate substitute for warrant

A court should suppress evidence obtained from an unreasonable Fourth Amendment search. A search is generally unreasonable if it is conducted without a warrant based on probable cause. But an administrative search of a highly regulated industry is an exception to the warrant requirement since it furthers administrative objectives (eg, to protect the public welfare)—not traditional law enforcement objectives (eg, to gather evidence for criminal prosecution). Therefore, a statute can permit warrantless administrative searches of highly regulated industries if three requirements are met:

  • The statute's purpose involves a substantial government interest—eg, improving public health and safety.
  • Warrantless searches are necessary to further the statute's purpose—ie, unannounced searches are needed to properly inspect the industry.
  • The statute provides a constitutionally adequate substitute for a warrant—ie, it (1) notifies the property owner that searches are authorized and (2) limits the inspecting officers' discretion concerning the time, place, and scope of the search.

Here, the court should deny the woman's motion to suppress and admit the evidence from the officers' warrantless administrative search of her motor vehicle junkyard (highly regulated industry). The Fourth Amendment was not violated since the statute authorizing their search, according to New York v. Burger, met all three requirements:

  • The statute's purpose—to deter motor vehicle theft and trafficking in stolen vehicles and parts— involves a substantial government interest.
  • Warrantless inspections of motor vehicle junkyards are necessary to further the statute's purpose.
  • The statute is a constitutionally adequate substitute for a warrant because it (1) notifies junkyard owners that the inspections are authorized and (2) limits police discretion by only permitting them to inventory vehicles and parts on the premises during normal business hours.

(Choice A) Administrative searches of most commercial establishments do require a warrant (eg, health inspection of a restaurant). However, no warrant is required for administrative searches of highly regulated industries (as seen here).

(Choice B) The statute's purpose—to deter motor vehicle theft and trafficking in stolen vehicles and parts—involves a substantial government interest.

(Choice C) The statute's stated purpose is to deter motor vehicle theft and trafficking in stolen vehicles and parts. There is no evidence that the stated purpose was a pretext to circumvent the general warrant requirement (or that officers used it to conduct unlawful searches). Therefore, the statute validly authorized the officers' search.

(Choice D) The statute does not grant law enforcement officers unbridled discretion to make warrantless searches. It restricts officers to taking physical inventory of vehicles and parts in motor vehicle junkyards during normal business hours. Therefore, evidence obtained from the officers' search is admissible at trial.

📌 Educational Objective

A statute permitting warrantless administrative searches of highly regulated industries is valid if: (1) its purpose concerns a substantial government interest, (2) warrantless searches are necessary to further that purpose, and (3) it is a constitutionally adequate substitute for a warrant (ie, gives notice of right to search and limits officer discretion).

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • New York v. Burger, 482 U.S. 691, 702–04 (1987) (listing the requirements for a reasonable administrative search of a highly regulated industry).
questions.zh-question:
某州颁布了一项法规，“旨在对机动车废品场业务的经营进行行政管理，以遏制机动车盗窃以及被盗机动车或其零部件的贩运。”该法规要求废品场所有者或经营者，“应请求在正常营业时间内，允许机动车管理局或任何执法机构的代表对其经营场所内的机动车及其零部件进行实物盘点。”该法规还规定，不遵守其任何要求的行为均构成重罪。

在该州的一个大城市，两名被派往汽车犯罪部门的警官定期走访市内所有的机动车废品场，以进行法规所允许的检查。一名女性拥有一家此类企业。夏日某天，警官要求检查她场地上的车辆。该女性问道：“我有选择的余地吗？”警官告诉她没有。警官随后进行了检查，并发现了三辆被盗汽车。

该女性被控收受赃物罪。她在审前提出动议，以检查违宪为由，请求排除与这三辆汽车相关的证据。

法院应如何裁定她排除此证据的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为对商业机构的行政搜查不需要搜查令。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为该法规对一个受到高度管制的行业进行了合理的规制。
zh-choices.C: 支持动议，因为该法规所述的监管目的，是在进行刑事侦查时规避搜查令要求的借口。
zh-choices.D: 支持动议，因为该法规授予执法人员进行无证搜查的不受限制的裁量权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Search and seizure

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：高度监管行业（highly regulated industry）的行政搜查（administrative search），能不能在没有普通令状的情况下直接进行。

三秒认题路径：

行政搜查 → 高监管行业 → Burger 三要件 → 令状例外 → 选 B

核心法律规则

这类题先看例外，不要先想普通刑搜

行政搜查（administrative search）考场意思：不是为了抓这次案子的证据，而是为了管行业秩序；高度监管行业（highly regulated industry）考场意思：像汽车拆车场这种行业，法律本来就预期会被查。

如果州法满足三件事，就可以不先拿普通令状：第一，监管目的有重大公共利益（substantial government interest）；第二，无令状搜查（warrantless search）对实现目的确有必要；第三，法条给了令状的合宪替代（constitutionally adequate substitute for a warrant），也就是提前通知、并限制查的人什么时候查、查哪里、查多大范围。

核心判例： New York v. Burger — 这案子把高度监管行业无令状搜查的三要件钉死了；本题的拆车场法条正好符合。

思维导图

先问：这是不是普通刑事搜查？
不是。 这是州法授权的行政搜查（administrative search）。
再问：行业是不是高度监管？
是。 汽车拆车场直接落入高度监管行业（highly regulated industry）。
再过三关：重大利益？必要性？合宪替代？
卡死点：这里不是看“会不会有伤害”，而是看终局前后还能不能补救。
1. 目的：打击盗车和赃车流通 → 重大公共利益。
2. 必要性：不预先通知、直接抽查，才能防止提前藏车。
3. 替代：法条已通知会查，并且只限正常营业时间、只查场内车辆和零件。
结论： 令状例外成立，证据保留，选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想： 只要是没有令状的商业搜查，就一定要压掉证据。

但考试真正问的是： 这是不是高度监管行业（highly regulated industry）里的合宪行政搜查（administrative search）；一旦满足 Burger 三要件，就不需要普通令状。

别被“像刑事侦查”骗走： 这里法条目的虽然后面也能帮警方抓赃车，但题目看的是州法授权的行业监管机制，不是单纯的犯罪取证。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的拆车场属于高度监管行业，州法又限定了营业时间、检查范围和事先通知，所以无令状搜查可成立，证据不压。

❌ 概念混淆 | 普通商业搜查

✕ A: 把普通商业场所的令状要求套到highly regulated行业上了。

❌ 事实误判 | 预文本意错读

✕ C: 题干没有把法条写成借口性pretext搜查，别凭感觉补事实。

❌ 法律适用 | 自由裁量误读

✕ D: 法条已限缩到正常营业时间和特定检查范围，不是无边界unbridled discretion。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判断是不是普通刑搜，再套 Burger 三要件；看到高监管行业时，先找例外而不是先背令状规则。

考场速记

记忆口诀：New York v. Burger = 重大公共利益 + 无令状有必要 + 法条像令状替代。

再记一句：普通商业场所先看令状，高度监管行业先看例外；查得越像“行业监管”，越可能不用普通令状。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
The police obtained reliable information from an anonymous informant that a man with a reputation for violence operated a large cocaine-distribution network and kept an arsenal of weapons in his home.
One day, the informant told the police that a supply of cocaine had been delivered to the man's home and that it would be moved to a distribution point the next morning. The police obtained a valid search warrant to search for and seize the cocaine, and they went to the man's house.
The police knocked on the man's door and called out, "Police. Open up. We have a search warrant." After a few seconds with no response, the police forced the door open and entered. Hearing noises in the basement, the police ran down there and found the man holding a package of cocaine. They seized the package and put the man in handcuffs. The man cursed the police and said, "You never would have caught me with the stuff if it hadn't been for that lousy snitch!"
The man is charged with unlawful possession of cocaine. He moves pretrial to suppress the use as evidence of the statement he made.
How is the court likely to rule on the man's motion to suppress?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the statement was the product of a lawful public safety search.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the statement was volunteered.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the entry by forcing open the door was not reasonable.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the police failed to read the man his Miranda rights.

questions.explanation:
Incriminating statements
Elicited statement
Volunteered statement
Custody + Interrogation
=
Miranda required
Custody + No interrogation
=
No Miranda required

According to Miranda v. Arizona, a defendant's motion to suppress an incriminating statement should be granted if that statement was made when the suspect was in custody and interrogated without receiving Miranda warnings:

  • The suspect has the right to remain silent.
  • Anything said can be used against the suspect in court.
  • The suspect has the right to counsel prior to and during questioning.
  • The suspect has the right to an appointed attorney if he/she cannot afford one.

An interrogation occurs when police direct questions, words, or actions at a suspect that they know or should know are reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response. Since volunteered statements (ie, spontaneous or unprompted remarks) are freely offered, they are not elicited by an interrogation. Therefore, volunteered statements are admissible even if the speaker had not been Mirandized.

Here, the man was in custody when the police apprehended and handcuffed him in his home. But his statement is admissible since he was not being interrogated when he spontaneously shouted, "You never would have caught me with the stuff if it hadn't been for that lousy snitch." Therefore, the police did not need Mirandize him and his motion to suppress the statement will likely be denied (Choice D).

(Choice A) Under the public safety exception, police do not need to Mirandize a suspect before an interrogation that is reasonably prompted by a public safety concern. Since the man's statement was not the product of an interrogation, this exception does not apply.

(Choice C) Forcible entry into a home to execute a warrant is reasonable if police first announce their presence and give the occupant a reasonable opportunity to open the door (knock and announce rule). However, police need not follow that rule if there is a credible threat of physical violence (eg, the man's violent reputation and weapons arsenal). Additionally, suppression is not a remedy for a violation of this rule.

📌 Educational Objective

Volunteered (ie, spontaneous or unprompted) statements are not protected by Miranda and are admissible at trial because they are freely offered by the suspect—not elicited by police interrogation.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 444–45 (1966) (listing the warnings required before custodial interrogation).

警方从一名匿名线人处获得可靠情报，称一名有暴力名声的男子经营着一个大型可卡因分销网络，并在其家中藏有大量武器。

一天，线人告知警方，一批可卡因已运抵该男子家中，并将在次日早晨被转移至一个分销点。警方获得了一份有效的搜查令，以搜查并扣押可卡因，随后他们前往该男子的住所。

警方敲了该男子的门并喊道：“警察。开门。我们有搜查令。”几秒钟没有回应后，警方强行破门而入。听到地下室有动静，警察跑下楼，发现该男子正持有一包可卡因。他们扣押了包裹，并给该男子戴上了手铐。该男子咒骂警察并说道：“要不是那个该死的告密者，你们根本抓不到我的人赃俱获！”

该男子被指控非法持有可卡因。他在审前动议，要求排除他所作陈述的证据资格。

法院很可能如何裁决该男子的排除动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为该陈述是合法公共安全搜查的产物。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为该陈述是自愿作出的。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为强行破门进入不具合理性。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为警方未能向该男子宣读其 Miranda 权利。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：拘押审讯（custodial interrogation）里，只有被警察“逼出来”的话才需要 Miranda；自发陈述（volunteered statement）不需要。

三秒认题路径：

先看是否拘押 → 再看有无审讯 → 没逼问就不保 Miranda → 自发喊话可采 → 选 B

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则

Miranda 警告（Miranda warnings）只管拘押（custody）加审讯（interrogation）。考场意思：人被控制住只是第一关，警察还得有问话或等同于逼供的动作，才会触发告知义务。

审讯（interrogation）是警察明知或应知会引出自证其罪回答的提问、言词或动作；自发陈述（volunteered statement）是嫌疑人自己突然说出口，所以可采。

本题里，男人虽然已被戴上手铐，属于拘押，但这句话是他自己对着警察脱口而出，不是被问出来的，所以不受 Miranda 排除。

核心判例： Miranda v. Arizona — 只有在拘押审讯（custodial interrogation）时才要先读权利；本题没有审讯，所以不能抑制这句话。

思维导图

1. 先问：这是拘押（custody）吗？
是男人已被按住并上铐，进入 Miranda 可能范围。
2. 再问：有审讯（interrogation）吗？
没有警察只是执行搜查、抓人，没对他发问。
卡死点：没有“逼出话”的审讯，就没有 Miranda 违规可抑制。
3. 这句话是什么类型？
自发陈述他自己骂出“you never would have caught me...”，属于主动脱口而出。
结论可采，运动 to suppress 应被驳回，答案选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：人都被抓住了，又没读 Miranda，应该直接压掉这句话。

但考试真正问的是：警察有没有审讯（interrogation），不是人当时有没有被控制住。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另一个坑是把搜查进门、破门方式和这句口供混在一起；这题抑制对象只有陈述本身，不是在打门是否合理。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里这句是他在被铐住后自己脱口而出，属于volunteered statement；没有审讯，就不触发 Miranda，故应驳回抑制动议。

❌ 概念混淆 | 公共安全误判

✕ A: 把public safety搬来，但这里根本没先问出答案的审讯。

❌ 事实误判 | 破门救济偷换

✕ C: 把破门是否合理当成口供抑制理由，偷换了争点。

❌ 法律适用 | 读权利套错

✕ D: 看到没读Miranda rights就直接判错，忽略了自发陈述不需要先警告。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定是否“拘押+审讯”，再判断是不是嫌疑人自己脱口而出。

考场速记

记住一句：拘押不等于一定要排除，真正触发点是拘押审讯（custodial interrogation）。自发陈述（volunteered statement）通常直接可采。

口决：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是给中间上诉用的；这题不是上诉题，别乱套。对 Miranda 题，最稳的速记是：“先看有没有问，没问就别抑制。”

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was a suspect in a series of murders. Detectives convinced the man's neighbor to sneak into the man's home and remove a cigarette butt so that the man's DNA could be compared to DNA found at the scene of one of the murders. The DNA was a match and the man was arrested.
Upon discovering that the prosecutor intended to present the DNA-comparison evidence to the grand jury, the man's lawyer filed a motion to suppress arguing that the evidence was illegally acquired.
How should the court rule on the man's motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the cigarette butt was seized by a private citizen instead of a police officer.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the grand jury cannot consider evidence obtained without probable cause.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the neighbor was acting as a police agent when he seized the cigarette butt without a warrant.

questions.explanation:
Rights & privileges that may be invoked at grand jury proceedings
Constitutional
rights
  • Privilege against self-incrimination (Fifth Amendment)
  • Equal protection (Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment)
  • Congressmen's privilege not to be questioned about legislative activities (speech
    or debate clause)
Privileges
  • Attorney-client privilege
  • Spousal privilege
  • Marital communications privilege
  • Psychotherapist-patient privilege

The exclusionary rule requires the suppression of illegally acquired evidence at trial. But this rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings because a grand jury only has the investigatory power to charge a person with a crime—not the judicial power to convict. The man's motion to suppress the DNA-comparison evidence was therefore premature and should be denied. However, the man can file a motion to suppress again at trial.

(Choices A & D) The exclusionary rule applies to misconduct by any government agent—ie, government employees and non-employees working on the government's behalf. Here, the neighbor was acting as a government agent because police convinced him to seize the cigarette butt for their benefit. This seizure violated the Fourth Amendment because it was made without a warrant and no exception applies. But since the exclusionary rule is inapplicable to grand jury proceedings, the man's motion should be denied.

(Choice C) A grand jury can consider any evidence relevant to deciding whether to charge an individual with a crime—including evidence obtained without a warrant based on probable cause. Therefore, the grand jury can consider the DNA evidence even if it was collected without probable cause.

📌 Educational Objective

The exclusionary rule does not apply during grand jury proceedings since the grand jury is an investigatory body—not a judicial body with the power to convict.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (unreasonable search and seizure).
  • United States v. Calandra, 414 U.S. 338, 351–52 (1974) (holding that the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子是一系列谋杀案的嫌疑人。侦探说服该男子的邻居潜入其家中，取走一个烟头，以便将其DNA与在其中一宗谋杀案现场发现的DNA进行比对。DNA比对结果相符，该男子因此被捕。

当该男子的律师发现检察官打算向大陪审团呈交DNA比对证据时，他提出了一项排除动议，主张该证据系非法获取。

法院应如何裁定该男子的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议，因为烟头是由一名普通公民而非警官获取的。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该动议，因为证据排除规则不适用于大陪审团程序。
zh-choices.C: 批准该动议，因为大陪审团不能采纳在没有“合理依据”（probable cause）的情况下获得的证据。
zh-choices.D: 批准该动议，因为邻居在没有搜查令的情况下获取烟头时，是作为警方代理人行事的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - General Fourth Amendment principles

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：大陪审团程序（grand jury proceedings）里，排除规则（exclusionary rule）通常不能让被告立刻压掉非法取得的证据。

三秒认题路径：

大陪审团 → 想压证据 → 先想排除规则 → grand jury 例外 → 不能立刻上诉/排除

核心法律规则

排除规则（exclusionary rule）的考场意思：它主要管审判（trial），不是管大陪审团先不要不要收这份材料。

大陪审团（grand jury）只是调查、决定要不要起诉的机关，不是负责定罪的法庭，所以它通常可以先看进去，即使证据日后在审判中可能被排除。

所以这题的动作不是“现在就把证据从世界上消失”，而是“等到审判阶段再谈能不能用”。这就是 United States v. Calandra 的核心结论。

核心判例： United States v. Calandra — 说明非法取得的证据通常仍可在大陪审团程序中被考虑，排除规则不在这里先启动。

思维导图

先问：这是终局判决（final judgment）吗？
NO只是大陪审团要不要起诉前的程序动作。
再问：有法定中间上诉吗？
NO题干没有 injunction / certification / class action 这类法定入口。
最后才看附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）
要件里最容易死掉的是：现在不立即上诉，之后仍能有效救济（effectively reviewable）
这题就算现在让大陪审团先看，之后在审判阶段仍可主张压制、重审，甚至排除使用。
结论：不满足“立即上诉”门槛 → B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：证据是“非法搜来的”，那就应该马上压掉。

但考试真正问的是：现在这个程序能不能先排除；不是问这份证据将来在审判里会不会被打掉。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以“无令状（without a warrant）”和“警方代理人（police agent）”只是在告诉你第四修正案可能被碰到，但还没有把这题变成“现在就能在大陪审团阶段排除”的题。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键触发点是 grand jury，所以即使 DNA 证据有第四修正案问题，排除规则（exclusionary rule）也通常不在这里先用。

❌ 概念混淆 | 私人行为误判

✕ A: 把 private citizen 当成自动无效，忽略了邻居其实是替警方办事。

❌ 法律适用 | 无因果件套错

✕ C: 看到没 probable cause 就想直接“全删”，但大陪审团阶段本来就不按这一步先排除。

❌ 事实误判 | 代理人细节偷换

✕ D: 盯着 government agent 只会看到第四修正案，没看到这是大陪审团程序。

这题建议用什么方法？

程序姿态优先：先看是不是大陪审团，再决定排除规则要不要当场启动。

考场速记

记忆口诀：大陪审团先看，审判时再拦。一看到 grand jury，先想 Calandra：通常不能立刻靠排除规则挡住证据。

如果题目再出现中间上诉线索，顺手记住：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely，对应 injunction、certification、class action 等法定例外。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
State troopers lawfully stopped a car driver on a turnpike for exceeding the speed limit by four miles per hour. One trooper approached the car to warn the driver to drive within the speed limit. The other trooper remained in the patrol car and ran a computer check of the car's license number. The computer check indicated that there was an outstanding warrant for the driver's arrest for unpaid traffic tickets. The troopers then arrested the driver based on the warrant, and they proceeded to search the driver. During the search, they discovered a package of heroin in one of the driver's pockets. Later, it was learned that the driver had paid the outstanding traffic tickets 10 days earlier and that the warrant had been quashed, but the clerk of the court had failed to update the computer, which continued to list the warrant as outstanding.
The driver was charged with unlawful possession of heroin. Her attorney has filed a motion to suppress the use of the heroin as evidence.
Should the motion be granted?

choices.A: No, because the troopers could reasonably rely on the computer report and the search was incident to arrest.
choices.B: No, because troopers may lawfully search a driver incident to a valid traffic stop.
choices.C: Yes, because there was no arrest for the traffic violation and no lawful arrest could be made on the basis of the warrant.
choices.D: Yes, because there was no probable cause or reasonable suspicion to believe that the driver possessed drugs.

questions.explanation:
Exceptions to exclusionary rule
Exception Definition Examples
Good faith Reasonable belief that actions leading to discovery of evidence were lawful
  • Executing later-invalidated warrant
  • Following law subsequently deemed unconstitutional
Independent source Evidence later obtained independent of initial illegality
  • Police return to site of illegal search with valid warrant based on other information
Inevitable discovery Evidence would have been discovered through other untainted means
  • Incriminating evidence would have been discovered during search despite Miranda violation
Attenuation Break in causal connection between illegal police conduct & discovery of evidence
  • Suspect released after invalid arrest later confesses
  • Substantial passage of time between illegal conduct & discovery of evidence

The exclusionary rule seeks to deter police misconduct by prohibiting the government from using evidence obtained in violation of a defendant's constitutional rights at trial. But under the good faith exception, illegally obtained evidence is admissible if the prosecution proves by a preponderance of the evidence that:

• police relied in good faith on (1) a facially valid warrant later deemed invalid or (2) an existing law later declared unconstitutional and

• their reliance was objectively reasonable.

Here, state troopers stopped the driver for speeding and arrested her after a computer check indicated that she had an outstanding arrest warrant. Although the computer report was wrong, the troopers did not know that the facially valid warrant had been quashed. Therefore, they reasonably relied on that report in arresting the driver and searching her incident to that arrest. As a result, the heroin found in her pocket was obtained in good faith, and the motion to suppress should be denied.

(Choice B) Under the search-incident-to-arrest exception, a warrantless search is lawful when a person (and the area within his/her immediate reach) is searched incident to a valid arrest—not a valid traffic stop.

(Choice C) Although there was no arrest for the traffic violation and no lawful arrest could be made based on the warrant, the troopers could reasonably rely on the computer check showing the outstanding warrant. Therefore, the heroin found during the subsequent search is admissible under the good faith exception.

(Choice D) The troopers did not have probable cause or reasonable suspicion to believe that the driver possessed drugs. But since the troopers arrested and then searched the driver in good faith, the heroin discovered during that search is admissible.

📌 Educational Objective

The good faith exception to the exclusionary rule allows unlawfully obtained evidence to be admitted when (1) police relied in good faith on a facially valid warrant later deemed invalid OR an existing law later declared unconstitutional and (2) their reliance was objectively reasonable.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Leon, 468 U.S. 897, 919 (1984) (establishing the good faith exception to the exclusionary rule).
  • Herring v. United States, 555 U.S. 135, 137 (2009) (applying the good faith exception to an arrest based upon an invalid warrant).

州警在收费公路上合法地拦下了一名超速四英里/小时的汽车司机。一名州警走近车辆，警告司机在限速内驾驶。另一名州警留在巡逻车内，对该车的车牌号进行了电脑查询。电脑查询显示，该司机因未付交通罚单而有一张未执行的逮捕令。州警随后根据该逮捕令逮捕了司机，并对其进行了搜查。在搜查过程中，他们在司机的一个口袋里发现了一包海洛因。后来得知，司机在10天前已经支付了未付的交通罚单，逮捕令也已被撤销，但法院书记员未能更新电脑系统，导致该逮捕令仍被列为未执行状态。

该司机被指控非法持有海洛因。她的律师已提出动议，要求排除将该海洛因用作证据。

该动议是否应被批准？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为州警可以合理信赖电脑报告，并且该搜查是附带逮捕的搜查。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为州警可以在一次有效的交通拦截中合法地对司机进行附带搜查。
zh-choices.C: 应该批准，因为没有因交通违法行为而进行逮捕，并且基于该逮捕令也无法进行合法逮捕。
zh-choices.D: 应该批准，因为没有相当理由或合理怀疑来相信司机持有毒品。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Search and seizure

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：警方依据看似有效、但后来发现已被撤销的逮捕令实施逮捕后，能否适用善意例外（good faith exception）保住搜到的毒品证据。

三秒认题路径：

电脑误报令状 → 先逮捕 → 附带搜身 → 善意例外 → 不压制

核心法律规则

第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）通常排除违法搜查得到的证据，但善意例外（good faith exception）会救回证据：如果警察对表面有效的令状（facially valid warrant）作出了客观上合理的依赖，即使后来发现令状其实已失效，证据也可能可以使用。

这里的关键不是“后来证明令状错了”，而是“当时警察能不能合理相信它是真的”。所以在这题里，objectively reasonable 的重点已经满足，逮捕后的附带搜查（search incident to arrest）也就跟着站得住。

核心判例： United States v. Leon 与 Herring v. United States - 令状后来失效不等于证据必排，只要警方当时是善意、客观合理地依赖电脑报告或令状信息。

思维导图

先问：这是不是终局判决后的普通证据问题？不是。这里先看逮捕令与例外。
事实起点：超速拦停 traffic stop，不是为了毒品搜查。
关键关卡：电脑显示有未缴罚单的逮捕令，警员当场逮捕。
规则连接：令状看起来有效，警员没理由知道它已被撤销，属于善意依赖。
卡死点：即使事后发现令状已过期，仍可通过善意例外保留证据。
最终结论：逮捕合法化后，搜身发现海洛因可作为证据使用，选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然真正的逮捕令后来被撤销，那搜到的海洛因就该一起排除。

但考试真正问的是：警察当时是否合理相信令状有效，而不是事后能不能证明记录系统出了错。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另外，search incident to arrest 不是“只要刚好有交通拦停就能搜”，而是要先有一个有效逮捕；本题有效逮捕来自电脑报告下的善意依赖。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 computer check 显示有未撤销的逮捕令，警员据此逮捕并搜身，属于善意例外，海洛因不压制。

❌ 概念混淆 | 交通拦停误认

✕ B: 把 traffic stop 当成可直接搜身的理由了。

❌ 法律适用 | 令状无效误套

✕ C: 只盯着令状后来失效，漏掉了警方当时的善意依赖。

❌ 事实误判 | 毒品线索偷换

✕ D: 题目不要求先有毒品嫌疑，逮捕后的搜身本来就够了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看警方是否善意依赖令状，再决定搜身证据能不能留。

考场速记

记住一句：令状后来错了，不等于当场就错；只要警员依赖客观合理，good faith 往往能保住证据。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was charged with and tried for murder. At trial, the defendant testified that he had acted in self-defense.
The trial court instructed the jury that the defendant had the burden of proving by a preponderance of the evidence that he had acted in self-defense. The defendant objected, arguing that this instruction violated the constitutional requirement that the prosecution prove the offense beyond a reasonable doubt.
Did the trial court's instruction violate the defendant's federal constitutional rights?

choices.A: No, because due process does not preclude requiring a defendant to prove self-defense by a preponderance of the evidence.
choices.B: No, because due process does not regulate the burdens of proof in criminal cases.
choices.C: Yes, because due process precludes placing any evidentiary burden on a criminal defendant.
choices.D: Yes, because due process precludes requiring a criminal defendant to bear the burden on an issue that would make an act lawful.

questions.explanation:
Due process seeks to prevent wrongful convictions by requiring the government to prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt (a high evidentiary burden). However, a legislature can place any burden of proof on the defendant to establish an affirmative defense—an assertion that, if proven, will justify or excuse a criminal defendant's actions and defeat the prosecution's claim (Choice C).

Here, the trial court instructed the jury that the defendant had the burden of proving that he acted in self-defense by a preponderance of the evidence. Since self-defense is an affirmative defense—not an element of the charged crime (murder)—this instruction placed a proper burden of proof on the defendant and did not violate due process.

(Choice B) Although due process does not regulate the burden of proof for affirmative defenses in criminal cases (eg, self-defense, insanity), it does regulate the burden of proof for criminal offenses (eg, murder, rape).

(Choice D) Due process precludes requiring a criminal defendant to bear the burden on an issue necessary to prove an element of a crime (eg, for murder, that the defendant caused the death of another)—not an issue that would make an act lawful. Therefore, a defendant can be required to prove an affirmative defense that would justify or excuse his/her actions and make the act lawful (eg, that the defendant killed another in self-defense).

📌 Educational Objective

Due process requires the prosecution to prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. But the defendant can be required to prove an affirmative defense (eg, self-defense, insanity) by any degree of proof.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (due process clause applicable to the federal government).
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV § 1 (due process clause applicable to the states).
  • Martin v. Ohio, 480 U.S. 228, 233 (1987) (holding that a state can place the burden of proof for self-defense on a defendant).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Due process

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：正当程序（due process）并不禁止把积极抗辩（affirmative defense）的举证责任放在被告身上，只要控方仍要证明犯罪构成要件。

三秒认题路径：

控方证要件 → 被告提自卫 → 这是抗辩 → 只要非要件 → 可由被告证

核心法律规则

正当程序（due process）要求控方把犯罪的每个构成要件（element）都用排除合理怀疑（beyond a reasonable doubt）证明到位，考场意思：你不能让被告去替国家证明“人确实被杀了、被告确实致死”这种定罪核心事实。

但对积极抗辩（affirmative defense），例如正当防卫（self-defense），法律可以让被告承担举证责任，考场意思：这不是在帮控方补犯罪要件，而是在让被告证明一个“即使事实成立也能免责/正当化”的理由。

所以本题里，被告要证明自己是正当防卫，州法院要求其以优势证据标准（preponderance of the evidence）举证，通常不违反联邦宪法。

核心判例：Martin v. Ohio —— 法院确认州可以把正当防卫的举证责任放在被告身上。

思维导图

先看：州是不是把“定罪要件”交给被告证明？
YES如果是构成犯罪的事实（例如杀人要件），就撞上 必须由控方证明到排除合理怀疑。
NO如果是积极抗辩（affirmative defense），比如正当防卫（self-defense），就继续往下看。
再看：这个问题是不是只是在给“免责理由”分配举证责任？
是州可以要求被告用优势证据标准（preponderance of the evidence）证明。
不是如果题目把被告逼去证明犯罪要件本身，才会碰到 正当程序问题。
本题结论
正当防卫不是 murder 的要件，故 A 选项。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然是刑事案件，控方就得把所有东西都证明完，被告不能再背任何举证责任。

但考试真正问的是：这个事实是在证明犯罪要件，还是在证明一个积极抗辩。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的关键点是self-defense属于积极抗辩，不是 murder 的构成要件，所以州可以要求被告用优势证据标准证明。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则范围误判

✕ B: 把正当程序误看成对burden of proof一律不管。

❌ 事实误判 | 要件偷换

✕ C: 以为任何辩解都不能让被告举证，偷换成“所有事实都归控方”。

❌ 法律适用 | 要件混淆误判

✕ D: 把make an act lawful当成犯罪要件，其实那是免责抗辩。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是“构成要件”还是“积极抗辩”，再决定举证责任能不能落到被告身上。

考场速记

记忆口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉例外的记忆法；本题则记成一句话：要件归控方，抗辩可给被告。

reason.en: The constitutional standard that regulates burdens of proof in criminal cases.
reason.zh: 规制刑事案件中证明责任的宪法标准。

label.zh: 被告对积极抗辩的证明责任

reason.en: Correctly states that due process allows requiring the defendant to prove this defense.
reason.zh: 正确指出正当程序允许要求被告证明该抗辩。

B.text: does not regulate the burdens of proof

label.zh: 误述正当程序规制范围

reason.en: Incorrectly claims that due process plays no role in criminal proof burdens.
reason.zh: 错误地声称正当程序在刑事证明责任中不起任何作用。

label.zh: 过度宽泛的证明责任限制

reason.en: Incorrectly states that the defendant can never carry any burden of proof.
reason.zh: 错误地声称被告绝对不能承担任何证明责任。

D.text: precludes requiring a criminal defendant to bear the burden on an issue that would make an act lawful

label.zh: 对违法阻却事由证明责任的误解

reason.en: The specific instruction assigning the burden of proof to the defendant that is under review.
reason.zh: 将证明责任分配给被告的受审查的特定陪审团指示。

highlights.text: prosecution prove the offense beyond a reasonable doubt

reason.en: The constitutional benchmark that the defense argues was violated by the instruction.
reason.zh: 辩方认为该指示所违反的宪法基准。

highlights.text: violate the defendant's federal constitutional rights

reason.en: The core legal question of whether the instruction violates federal due process.

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
The police had, over time, accumulated reliable information that a man operated a large cocaine-distribution network, that he and his accomplices often resorted to violence, and that they kept a small arsenal of weapons in his home.
One day, the police received reliable information that a large brown suitcase with leather straps containing a supply of cocaine had been delivered to the man's home and that it would be moved to a distribution point the next morning. The police obtained a valid search warrant to search for and seize the brown suitcase and the cocaine, and they went to the man's house.
The police knocked on the man's door and called out, "Police. Open up. We have a search warrant." After a few seconds with no response, the police forced the door open and entered. Hearing noises in the basement, the police ran down there and found the man with a large brown suitcase with leather straps. They seized the suitcase and put handcuffs on the man. A search of his person revealed a switchblade knife and a .45-caliber pistol. The man cursed the police and said, "You never would have caught me with the stuff if it hadn't been for that lousy snitch!"
The police then fanned out through the house, looking in every room and closet. They found no one else, but one officer found an Uzi automatic weapon in a box on a closet shelf in the man's bedroom.
In addition to charges relating to the cocaine in the suitcase, the man is charged with unlawful possession of weapons. The man moves pretrial to suppress the use as evidence of the weapons seized by the police and of the statement he made.
As to the switchblade knife and the .45-caliber pistol, how is the court likely to rule?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the police had reasonable grounds to believe that there were weapons in the house.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the search and seizure were incident to a lawful arrest.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the police did not inform the man that he was under arrest and did not read him his Miranda rights.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the search and seizure were the result of illegal police conduct in executing the search warrant.

questions.explanation:
Admissibility of evidence obtained by Fourth Amendment violation

Did government conduct search?
  • Physical trespass: intrusion of constitutionally protected area
    OR
  • Reasonable expectation of privacy: invasion of subjectively and objectively reasonable privacy expectation
Yes
↓
Was search unreasonable?
  • No warrant
  • AND
  • No applicable exception
    ◦ Search incident to valid arrest
    ◦ Administrative search of highly regulated industry
    ◦ Stop and frisk
    ◦ Plain view doctrine
    ◦ Automobile exception
    ◦ Consent
    ◦ Exigent circumstance
    ◦ Special government purpose
  • Mnemonic: SAD SPACES
Yes
↓
Inadmissible

The Fourth Amendment generally requires that officers obtain a warrant before conducting a search. However, a warrant is not required to conduct a search incident to a lawful arrest because an immediate search is necessary for officer safety and to prevent the arrestee from destroying nearby evidence. This exception allows police to conduct a warrantless search of:

  • the person who has been lawfully arrested and
  • the areas within that person's immediate reach.

Here, the police obtained a warrant to search for and seize the brown suitcase and cocaine believed to be in the man's home. The police then entered his home, found him with the suitcase, and lawfully placed him in handcuffs. They conducted a warrantless search of the man's person incident to that arrest and found a switchblade knife and .45-caliber pistol. As a result, the man's motion to suppress that evidence should be denied.

(Choice A) Since the police had reasonable grounds (probable cause) to believe that there were weapons in the house, they could have obtained a warrant to search the home—but not persons in the home—for those weapons. But probable cause alone does not authorize a warrantless search.

(Choice C) Police need not inform suspects that they are under arrest, and Miranda warnings are only required if police intend to interrogate suspects while they are in custody. Since the man was not interrogated, Miranda warnings were not required. And even if they were, the court would suppress the man's self-incriminating statement—not the knife and pistol.

(Choice D) When executing a warrant, police must announce their presence and give the occupant a reasonable opportunity to answer before forcibly entering the home (knock and announce rule). However, an unannounced or expedited entry is permitted when there is a credible threat of violence or destruction of evidence (eg, the man's violent reputation and weapons arsenal).

📌 Educational Objective

Police do not need a warrant to conduct a search incident to a lawful arrest. However, that search is limited to (1) the person arrested and (2) the areas within his/her immediate reach.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Chimel v. California, 395 U.S. 752, 763 (1969) (recognizing that search incident to lawful arrest extends to areas within the suspect's immediate control).
questions.zh-question:
警方长期以来积累了可靠的情报，得知一名男子经营着一个庞大的可卡因分销网络，他与同伙经常诉诸暴力，并且在家中存放着一个小型武器库。

一天，警方接到可靠情报，一个装有可卡因的带皮带的大号棕色手提箱已被送到该男子家中，并将在第二天早上被转移到一个分销点。警方获得了一份有效的搜查令，以搜查并扣押该棕色手提箱和可卡因，然后他们前往该男子的住宅。

警方敲响了该男子的门，并喊道：“警察。开门。我们有搜查令。”几秒钟后无人应答，警方强行破门而入。听到地下室有响动，警方冲下楼，发现该男子正拿着一个带皮带的大号棕色手提箱。他们扣押了手提箱，并给该男子戴上了手铐。对其人身进行搜查后，发现了一把弹簧刀和一把.45口径的手枪。该男子咒骂警察说：“要不是那个该死的告密者，你们永远也抓不到我拿着这些东西！”

随后，警方分散到整个房屋，搜查了每个房间和壁橱。他们没有发现其他人，但一名警官在该男子卧室的壁橱架子上的一个盒子里发现了一把 Uzi 自动武器。

除了与手提箱中的可卡因有关的指控外，该男子还被控非法持有武器。该男子提出审前动议，要求排除警方所缴获的武器及其所作陈述作为证据使用。

关于弹簧刀和.45口径手枪，法院可能会如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议，因为警方有合理理由相信房屋内有武器。
zh-choices.B: 驳回该动议，因为该搜查与扣押是合法逮捕附带的。
zh-choices.C: 批准该动议，因为警方未告知该男子他已被逮捕，也未向他宣读其 Miranda 权利。
zh-choices.D: 批准该动议，因为该搜查与扣押是警方在执行搜查令过程中非法行为的结果。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Search and seizure

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：警察在合法逮捕后，能不能对被逮捕人的身体做附带搜查（search incident to lawful arrest），从而把身上搜到的刀和手枪拿来当证据。

三秒认题路径：

合法搜查令 → 现场抓人 → 人身搜查 → 逮捕附带 → 可采证据

核心法律规则

第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）一般要求搜查先拿令，但合法逮捕附带搜查（search incident to lawful arrest）是经典例外，考场意思：人已经合法被抓，警察可以马上搜他本人和他伸手能碰到的范围。

即时安全（officer safety）和防止销毁证据是这个规则的核心理由，考场意思：不是因为警察“怀疑那里有武器”就能随便搜，而是因为逮捕本身打开了对被捕人身体的无令搜查窗口。

这题里警察先在屋里抓到男人，再搜他的身体，拿到刀和手枪，所以关键不是屋里有没有武器线索，而是搜查是否紧贴着合法逮捕（lawful arrest）发生。

核心判例： Chimel v. California — 逮捕附带搜查只到被捕人本人和其立即可及范围。

思维导图

先问：这是不是要直接拦下证据？
1.警察先有有效搜查令，进入住宅找箱子和毒品。
2.他们在屋内当场抓到男人，并把他戴上手铐。
3.随后搜他本人，拿到switchblade knife和.45-caliber pistol。
卡死点：争议不是“屋里能不能搜武器”，而是“逮捕后能不能搜人身”。
规则锁定：合法逮捕附带搜查 → 可搜被捕人本人 → 发现刀和枪可采。
结论：这不是要压掉证据，而是要判断逮捕附带例外是否成立。
答案走向：否决排除动议。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：警察虽然有搜查令，但没有另外拿到搜武器的令，所以刀和枪应该被排除。

但考试真正问的是：他们搜的是被合法逮捕的人身，不是单纯在屋里四处找证据；这个场景直接落进search incident to lawful arrest。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里要抓的是例外是否存在，不是嫌疑人家里有没有武器背景。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干里男人是在屋内被合法控制后，警察才搜他本人并找到switchblade knife和.45-caliber pistol，这正是附带搜查（search incident to lawful arrest）。

❌ 概念混淆 | 令状理由误判

✕ A: 把probable cause当成能直接搜人，错把搜屋理由当搜身理由。

❌ 法律适用 | 米兰达错套

✕ C: 只盯着Miranda rights，但这里争的是刀枪能不能进证据，不是口供能不能用。

❌ 事实误判 | 执行瑕疵夸大

✕ D: 把knock and announce说成会自动毒化后续搜身，事实和结论都偷换了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先定搜查对象，再看是否已发生合法逮捕；一旦是人身附带搜查，就先想 Chimel。

考场速记

记住一句：合法逮捕一发生，警察就能搜被捕人本人和立即可及范围；这题的刀和枪就是这样进来的。

速记口诀：search incident to lawful arrest，先看“人是否已被合法抓住”，再看“搜的是不是他的身体或伸手范围”。

reason.zh: 指对被逮捕人的人身搜查，这在合法逮捕后是自动允许的。

C.text: did not read him his Miranda rights

D.text: illegal police conduct in executing the search warrant

label.zh: 非法证据排除规则范围不匹配

reason.zh: 违反敲门并宣布身份规则并不会导致搜查中发现的实物证据被排除。

highlights.text: obtained a valid search warrant

reason.en: Confirms the initial police presence in the house was lawful.
reason.zh: 确认警察最初在房屋内的活动是合法的。

highlights.text: kept a small arsenal of weapons in his home

reason.en: Justifies forcing open the door due to threat of violence, defeating knock-and-announce violation claims.
reason.zh: 因存在暴力威胁而证明强行开门合理，击败了违反敲门宣布规则的主张。

highlights.text: put handcuffs on the man

reason.en: Shows the defendant was arrested, which triggers the exception to search the person.
reason.zh: 表明被告已被逮捕，这触发了搜查人身的例外规则。

highlights.text: A search of his person revealed a switchblade knife and a .45-caliber pistol

label.en: scope of search incident to arrest

reason.en: The specific search and evidence targeted by the suppression motion.
reason.zh: 排除动议针对的特定搜查行为和扣押证据。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A store owner whose jewelry store had recently been robbed was shown by a police detective a photograph of the defendant, who previously had committed other similar crimes. The store owner examined the photograph and then asked the detective whether the police believed that the man pictured was the robber. After the detective said, "We're pretty sure," the store owner stated that the man in the photograph was the one who had robbed her.
The defendant was indicted for the robbery. His counsel moved to suppress any trial testimony by the store owner identifying the defendant as the robber.
Should the court grant the motion and suppress the store owner's trial testimony identifying the defendant as the robber?

choices.A: No, because suppression of in-court testimony is not a proper remedy, even though the out-of-court identification was improper.
choices.B: No, because the out-of-court identification was not improper.
choices.C: Yes, because the improper out-of-court identification has necessarily tainted any in-court identification.
choices.D: Yes, unless the prosecution demonstrates that the in-court identification is reliable.

questions.explanation:
Admissibility of in-court identification testimony
Was there an unnecessarily suggestive
out-of-court identification procedure?
  • Arranged by police
  • Unnecessarily & highly suggestive—eg, defendant looks different from others in lineup
No Admit
in-court
testimony
Did the out-of-court identification procedure create
a substantial likelihood of misidentification?
Court will consider:
  • Witness's opportunity to view perpetrator & level of attention during crime
  • Accuracy of witness's description before suggestive identification & certainty during identification
  • Time between crime & suggestive identification
No Admit
in-court
testimony
(reliable)
Suppress in-court testimony
(unreliable)

Due process requires the suppression of unreliable testimony identifying the defendant as the perpetrator of the charged crime (ie, identification testimony) since it may inhibit the defendant's right to a fair trial. In-court identification testimony may be unreliable if it stems from unnecessarily suggestive out-of-court identification procedures arranged by police. Therefore, such in-court identification testimony is only admissible if the prosecution demonstrates that it is sufficiently reliable and poses no substantial likelihood of misidentification.

Here, the police detective showed the store owner a photograph of the defendant and explained that the police were "pretty sure" that the defendant was the robber. After this unnecessarily suggestive out-of-court identification procedure, the store owner identified the defendant as the robber (Choice B). As a result, the court should suppress the store owner's in-court testimony identifying the defendant as the robber unless the prosecution proves that her testimony is reliable despite the improper identification procedure.

(Choice A) Suppression of in-court identification testimony is a proper remedy if (1) that testimony stems from an unnecessarily suggestive out-of-court identification procedure and (2) the prosecution cannot prove that the in-court testimony is reliable.

(Choice C) An improper out-of-court identification does not always taint an in-court identification—eg, a witness's in-court testimony may be reliable despite a suggestive identification procedure if he/she could accurately describe the perpetrator before that procedure. Therefore, in-court identification testimony will only be suppressed if it is rendered unreliable by an improper out-of-court identification.

📌 Educational Objective

Due process requires the suppression of in-court identification testimony that was rendered unreliable (ie, substantially likely to result in misidentification) by an unnecessarily suggestive out-of-court identification procedure.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amends. V & XIV (due process).
  • Neil v. Biggers, 409 U.S. 188, 197 (1972) (holding that unnecessarily suggestive identification procedures violate due process if they create a substantial likelihood of misidentification).
  • Perry v. New Hampshire, 565 U.S. 228, 240–244 (2012) (stating that the reliability of identification testimony stemming from improper identification procedures must be assessed before admitting that testimony at trial).
questions.zh-question:
一名警探向一名珠宝店最近被抢劫的店主出示了被告的照片，该被告此前曾犯下其他类似罪行。店主查看了照片，然后询问警探警方是否认为照片中的男子就是抢劫犯。在警探说“我们很确定”之后，店主陈述照片中的男子就是抢劫她的人。

被告因抢劫罪被起诉。其律师申请排除店主在庭审中指认被告为抢劫犯的任何证词。

法院是否应批准该动议，并排除店主指认被告为抢劫犯的庭审证词？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为排除庭审证词并非适当的救济措施，即使庭外指认不当。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为庭外指认并无不当。
zh-choices.C: 应批准，因为不当的庭外指认必然污染了任何庭审中的指认。
zh-choices.D: 应批准，除非控方证明庭审中的指认是可靠的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Due process

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：警察安排的过度暗示性辨认（unnecessarily suggestive identification）会不会把后面的庭审辨认（in-court identification）也带歪，答题关键是看它还能不能被证明足够可靠。

三秒认题路径：

警察暗示 → 先前辨认 → 会不会错认 → 还能否可靠 → 选 D

核心法律规则

如果警察（police）安排了过度暗示性辨认程序（unnecessarily suggestive identification procedure），而且这会让认人结果有明显错认风险（substantial likelihood of misidentification），due process 就要把这类不可靠的辨认证言挡在庭审外。

但这不是“一有问题就全废”；考试真正看的是，庭审辨认（in-court identification）是不是仍然可靠。如果检方还能证明它没被前面的暗示搞歪，证言还是能进。

核心判例： Neil v. Biggers / Perry v. New Hampshire - 先看是否是警察制造的暗示，再看是否造成明显错认；能证明可靠，就不必当然排除。

思维导图

1. 先问：这是不是警察安排的过度暗示性辨认？
NO 直接可采：庭审辨认通常不因这条规则被压掉
YES
2. 再问：它有没有制造明显错认风险？
看三件事
看见机会
目击时有没有认真看清嫌犯。
先前描述
正式暗示前，描述准不准。
时间间隔
案发到辨认隔太久，可靠性会掉。
卡死点：只要检方能证明庭审辨认仍可靠，就不必排除；本题这里被警察一句“pretty sure”明显推向暗示性错误，所以结论转到 D。
3. 结论：不可靠 → 排除；可靠 → 允许进入庭审

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然前面的照片辨认已经被警察带节奏了，那后面的庭审辨认就一定不能用。

但考试真正问的是：后面的庭审辨认有没有被证明仍然可靠，不是前面一出错就自动全盘报废。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干里警察先给了带暗示的照片，还说“pretty sure”，这正是警察制造的过度暗示；所以庭审辨认只有在检方证明它仍然可靠时才可采。

❌ 概念混淆 | 绝对排除误判

✕ A: 把“有瑕疵”直接当成“永远不能用”，suppression 不是无条件。

❌ 事实误判 | 暗示来源漏读

✕ B: 题干明明写了警察说“pretty sure”，不是普通自发辨认。

❌ 法律适用 | 必然污染套错

✕ C: 把前面的错误说成当然毁掉一切，忽略了后面还可单独证明可靠。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“警察是否制造暗示”，再查“庭审辨认是否仍可靠”，别被“看起来很像”带跑。

考场速记

记住这句：先问有没有警察制造的过度暗示，再问会不会造成明显错认；能证明可靠，就还能上庭。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 这题虽不是上诉题，但同样是“先看门槛，再看例外/可靠性”的 MBE 走法。

question_analysis.skill_tested: evaluating admissibility of in-court identification

reason.en: Indicates a suggestive identification procedure using a single photograph rather than a photographic lineup.
reason.zh: 表明使用了单张照片而非照片组的暗示性辨认程序。

reason.en: The procedural vehicle used by defense counsel to challenge the admissibility of the identification.
reason.zh: 辩护律师用来质疑辨认证据可采性的程序手段。

reason.en: The evidence that the defendant wants excluded because of the prior suggestive procedure.
reason.zh: 被告因先前存在暗示性程序而要求排除的证据。

A.text: suppression of in-court testimony is not a proper remedy

label.zh: 对证据排除救济的错误限制

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was charged with murder. Several witnesses testified that the crime was committed by a person of the man's general description who walked with a severe limp. The man in fact walks with a severe limp. He objected to a prosecution request that the court order him to walk across the courtroom in order to display his limp to the jury to assist it in determining whether the man was the person that the witnesses had seen.
How should the court respond to the man's objection?

choices.A: Overrule the objection, because a criminal defendant has no legitimate expectation of privacy.
choices.B: Overrule the objection, because the order sought by the prosecution is a legitimate part of a proper courtroom identification process.
choices.C: Sustain the objection, because the order sought by the prosecution would constitute an illegal search and seizure.
choices.D: Sustain the objection, because the order sought by the prosecution would violate the man's privilege against self-incrimination.

questions.explanation:
Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination
Testimonial communications(privileged)
  • Oral testimony
  • Act of producing documents
Real or physical evidence(not privileged)
  • Fingerprints
  • Handwriting samples
  • Voice tests
  • Photographs
  • Physical characteristics & clothing
  • Movements or gestures
  • Blood, DNA, urine samples

The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination protects defendants from being compelled to provide incriminating evidence—evidence that could be used, or lead to other evidence that might be used, against a person in a criminal prosecution. However, this privilege only applies to testimonial communications (eg, oral testimony, act of producing documents)—not real or physical evidence (eg, movements, gestures, blood test).

Here, several witnesses testified that the murderer walked with a severe limp (same as the man), so the prosecution requested that the court order him to walk across the courtroom to show the jury his limp. Since the privilege against self-incrimination does not apply to physical evidence (eg, a limp), the order sought is a legitimate part of a proper courtroom identification process (Choice D). Therefore, the man's objection should be overruled.

(Choices A & C) The Fourth Amendment protects a person's legitimate expectation of privacy by prohibiting unreasonable searches and seizures. However, a person has no legitimate expectation of privacy in his/her physical characteristics because they are exposed to the public. Therefore, an order compelling the man to display his limp would not constitute an illegal search and seizure or otherwise violate the Fourth Amendment.

📌 Educational Objective

The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination prohibits the government from compelling a defendant to provide incriminating testimonial communications—not real or physical evidence.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Schmerber v. California, 384 U.S. 757, 764 (1966) (recognizing that self-incrimination does not apply to real or physical evidence).
  • Missouri v. Proctor, 535 S.W.2d 141, 144–45 (Mo. Ct. App. 1976) (holding that a compelled walk in the courtroom does not violate privilege against self-incrimination).

zh-choices.A: 驳回反对意见，因为刑事被告没有合法的隐私期待。
zh-choices.B: 驳回反对意见，因为检方所请求的命令是正当的法庭身份识别程序的合法组成部分。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - The Privilege Against Compulsory Self-Incrimination

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第五修正案的 反自证其罪特权（privilege against self-incrimination） 只挡 证言性沟通（testimonial communication），不挡 身体性证据（physical evidence），所以法院可以命令被告走路展示跛行。

三秒认题路径：

强制走路 → 看特权 → 证言性？ → 不是 → 可命令

核心法律规则

第五修正案的 反自证其罪特权（privilege against self-incrimination），考场意思：政府不能逼你说话、写字、交出“会表达你脑子里内容”的东西。它保护的是 证言性沟通（testimonial communication），比如口头证言和交文件的行为。它不保护 身体性证据（real or physical evidence），比如走路姿势、手写样本、指纹、血液、DNA。

核心判例： Schmerber v. California - 说明自证其罪特权不管身体性证据；本题里命令被告走过法庭，只是让陪审团看他的跛行，不是逼他“作证”。

思维导图

题目先看：法院要他做的是“说话”还是“展示身体特征”?
YES 证言性沟通：口头证言 / 交文件内容 / 逼你表达想法 → 可能触发第五修正案。
如果被逼的是“脑子里的信息”，就可能是特权范围。
NO 身体性证据：走路、跛行、指纹、照片、血样、声音、手写样本 → 不在特权内。
本题命令他走过法庭，只是在看 跛行，所以不是自证其罪。
结论：法院可命令展示跛行，帮助陪审团做身份辨认 → 选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告一走路，等于被强迫拿自己的缺陷来认罪，听起来很像自证其罪。

但考试真正问的是：这是不是 证言性沟通（testimonial communication）；答案不是。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

真正卡点是：这里没有逼他说“我就是凶手”，只是让陪审团看他有没有和证人描述一致的跛行。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 walk across the courtroom 只是展示跛行，属于身份辨认流程，不是逼供或逼他表达内心内容，所以第五修正案不挡。

❌ 概念混淆 | 隐私权误套

✕ A: 把 privacy 当成本题核心，但这里问的是自证其罪，不是第四修正案。

❌ 法律适用 | 搜查扣押误套

✕ C: 看到身体被命令展示就想到 search and seizure，但这不是搜查扣押。

❌ 事实误判 | 证言性偷换

✕ D: 把 self-incrimination 扩到所有不利证据，漏掉了“身体性证据不保护”。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“说出来的内容”还是“身体本身”，再决定第五修正案能不能挡。

考场速记

记住一句：第五修正案 只挡 证言性沟通（testimonial communication），不挡 身体性证据（physical evidence）。看到“走路、指纹、手写、血样、声音”先判断为物理证据，通常直接排除特权。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Federal agents had a hunch that a local man was engaged in illegal gambling activities. An agent decided to enter the man's house while he was not at home and see what he could find. The agent discovered an envelope containing $5,000 in cash and an executive's business card. Returning the envelope to its place, the agent located and interviewed the executive, who admitted that he had paid the man $5,000 to settle a gambling debt; the executive also disclosed that the man regularly took illegal bets from the executive and several of his acquaintances. The agent then interviewed the acquaintances, who confirmed what the executive had told him. The agent then arranged to be introduced to the man at a local bar. After a few drinks, the man, unaware of the agent's identity, boasted that he was one of the biggest bookmakers in the state.
The agent testified to all of his investigation's discoveries before a grand jury, which returned an indictment against the man for illegal gambling activities, based solely on the agent's testimony. The man's attorney then filed a motion to dismiss the indictment, claiming that it rested on violations of the man's constitutional rights.
Should the court grant the motion?

choices.A: No, because dismissal of the indictment is not the appropriate remedy.
choices.B: Yes, because much of the agent's testimony before the grand jury was inadmissible hearsay.
choices.C: Yes, because of the agent's unlawful search of the man's home.
choices.D: Yes, because of the agent's violation of the man's right to counsel.

questions.explanation:
Grounds for dismissing indictment
Deficient indictment
  • Fails to charge actual crime
  • Omits elements of crime
  • Statute of limitations has run
  • Improper venue or jurisdiction
Defective grand jury proceedings
  • Admission of unqualified grand juror
  • Exclusion of grand juror based on race/gender
  • Prosecutorial misconduct
Constitutional violation
  • Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause
  • Sixth Amendment right to speedy trial
  • Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment due process clauses

Grand jury proceedings are investigatory in nature since they are used to determine whether probable cause exists to bring a criminal charge (ie, issue an indictment) against an individual. To help the grand jury in its investigation, the prosecutor can present any evidence that may be relevant to the grand jury's decision—even if that evidence was obtained in violation of the Fourth Amendment. And since these are not traditional judicial proceedings, the exclusionary rule (used to suppress illegally obtained evidence at trial) does not apply.

Here, the man filed a motion to dismiss the indictment, claiming that it was based on violations of his constitutional rights. Although the man's Fourth Amendment rights were violated when the agent conducted a warrantless search of the man's home, the agent's testimony regarding that search was relevant to the man's illegal gambling charge. Therefore, that testimony was properly presented to the grand jury, so the indictment should not be dismissed. Instead, the appropriate remedy will be to suppress any evidence obtained from the unlawful search at trial.

(Choice B) Hearsay is an out-of-court statement offered into evidence to prove the truth of the matter asserted. Although hearsay is generally inadmissible at trial, it can be presented at a grand jury proceeding where the rules of evidence do not apply. Therefore, though much of the agent's testimony would be inadmissible hearsay if offered at trial, it was properly considered by the grand jury.

(Choice C) A Fourth Amendment search is unlawful when it is conducted without a warrant and no exception to the warrant requirement applies (as seen here). But the exclusionary rule only prohibits the use of illegally obtained evidence at trial—not at a grand jury proceeding. Therefore, since the evidence from the unlawful search was relevant to the grand jury's probable cause determination, it was properly presented to the grand jury.

(Choice D) The Fifth Amendment right to counsel is not triggered unless the defendant is subjected to a custodial interrogation. And the Sixth Amendment right to counsel does not attach until judicial proceedings have commenced (eg, indictment issued). But neither right was violated here because the man met with the agent voluntarily (no custody) and was interviewed before judicial proceedings began.

📌 Educational Objective

The exclusionary rule prohibits the use of illegally obtained evidence at trial—not grand jury proceedings. Therefore, evidence from an unlawful Fourth Amendment search can be presented to the grand jury if that evidence may be relevant to the grand jury's probable cause determination.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Calandra, 414 U.S. 338, 351–52 (1974) (explaining that the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings).

法院应否批准该动议？

zh-choices.B: 应批准，因为探员在大陪审团面前的大部分证词是不可采纳的传闻证据。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Search and seizure

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：非法搜查（unlawful search）得到的证据，能不能拿去支持大陪审团（grand jury）起诉。

三秒认题路径：

无令搜查 → 大陪审团 → 证据可用 → 不排除 → 不撤销起诉

核心法律规则

排除规则（exclusionary rule）主要管的是审判（trial），不是大陪审团的调查过程。考试里你要记住：只要证据和可能原因（probable cause）有关，检察官通常可以拿去给大陪审团看，即使这证据最初来自违反第四修正案的搜查。

大陪审团（grand jury）是为了决定要不要起诉，不是为了当庭定罪；所以这里不走“先把证据全排掉再说”的思路。真正能做的是：到审判阶段再主张排除，而不是直接要求撤销起诉书。

核心判例：United States v. Calandra - 说明排除规则一般不适用于大陪审团程序，所以非法搜查得到的相关证据仍可用于起诉决定。

思维导图

题干先看：证据是拿去给 grand jury 用，还是拿去 trial 用？
第一关：这是起诉阶段，不是审判阶段。
第二关：证据是不是和 probable cause 有关？
卡死点：exclusionary rule 主要不挡 grand jury。
所以即使搜查可能违法，相关证据仍可交给大陪审团。
结论：不撤销起诉；到审判时再争取排除。
命题人最爱骗你：把“证据违法”直接等于“起诉无效”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然警察是warrantless search，那整件案子都该作废。

但考试真正问的是：这份证据能不能支撑grand jury的probable cause判断，而不是它在审判时能不能直接用。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的关键事实是：被污染的是给grand jury看的材料，不是审判中的证据；排除规则（exclusionary rule）通常不能据此要求直接撤销起诉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 传闻规则误判

✕ B: 把 hearsay 当成大陪审团的硬禁令了。

❌ 法律适用 | 排除规则搬错场景

✕ C: 只盯着 unlawful search，却忘了这里还在起诉前。

❌ 事实误判 | 律师权利偷换

✕ D: 把 right to counsel 硬塞进了本题，但题干没到那一步。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看程序姿态：先分清是大陪审团还是审判，再决定排除规则能不能上场。

考场速记

记住一句：非法搜查证据不一定能挡住起诉，但常常还能在审判时继续打。

这题的口诀是：“先问是不是 grand jury，再问 exclusionary rule 管不管。”

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A public defender was appointed by the court to represent an indigent defendant on trial for felony theft. The defendant was offended when the public defender suggested that the defendant consider pleading guilty in light of the evidence against her and the generous plea bargain offered by the prosecution. As a result, the defendant asked the court to appoint another attorney. The court refused but explained that the defendant had the right to dismiss the public defender and proceed pro se. The defendant chose to continue being represented by the public defender. The defendant was subsequently convicted and received a one-year prison sentence that was suspended in full.
Has the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel been violated?

choices.A: No, because a defendant has no right to counsel when a sentence of imprisonment is not actually imposed.
choices.B: No, because the court complied with the defendant's right to the appointment of counsel.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant was entitled to counsel of her own choosing.
choices.D: Yes, because the defendant's conviction shows that she was denied competent counsel.

questions.explanation:
Sixth Amendment right to counsel
(choice of counsel)
General rule Non-indigent* criminal defendant is entitled to counsel of choice
Limitations Court may deny choice of counsel if:
  • defendant is unable to pay desired attorney
  • attorney declines representation
  • attorney has conflict of interest
  • advocate is not an attorney
*Indigent criminal defendant entitled to effective advocate but not counsel of choice.

The Sixth Amendment provides the right to counsel in any case in which a defendant is sentenced to imprisonment, even if that sentence is suspended (Choice A). A defendant who can afford a lawyer is generally entitled to the counsel of her own choosing, but a defendant who is indigent is not.

Here, the court complied with the Sixth Amendment when it appointed a public defender to represent the indigent defendant. And though the defendant was offended by the public defender's suggestion that she consider pleading guilty, the defendant was not entitled to choose her own counsel (Choice C). Therefore, the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel was not violated when the court refused her request for a different attorney.

(Choice D) The right to counsel encompasses the right to be assisted by a reasonably competent attorney. But a conviction will be reversed based on ineffective counsel only if (1) counsel's representation fell below an objective standard of reasonableness and (2) counsel's deficient performance prejudiced the defendant, resulting in the reasonable probability that the outcome would have been different if not for the ineffective assistance. Here, the public defender's suggestion that the defendant plead guilty does not meet these requirements.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant who is indigent has a Sixth Amendment right to counsel in any case in which the defendant is sentenced to imprisonment but—unlike a defendant who can afford a lawyer—is not entitled to counsel of her own choosing.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to counsel).
  • Wheat v. United States, 486 U.S. 153, 159 (1988) (holding that defendant has the right to an effective advocate, not to an attorney preferred by defendant).

zh-choices.A: 否，因为当未实际判处监禁时，被告无权获得律师。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为法院遵守了被告获得指定律师的权利。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为被告有权选择自己的律师。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Right to counsel

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：贫困被告（indigent defendant）有权获派律师，但没有权利自己挑律师；法院只要已经依法指派有效辩护人，拒绝换人一般不构成第六修正案违反。

三秒认题路径：

贫困被告 → 法院指派 → 想换律师 → 无权挑选 → 不违宪

核心法律规则

第六修正案（Sixth Amendment）保障的是“有律师”，不是“想要哪位律师就一定给哪位”。对贫困被告（indigent defendant），法院只需提供称职的辩护人；只有非贫困被告才通常享有律师选择权（counsel of choice）。

考试里看到法院已经给了公设辩护人，就先问一句：这题是在考“有没有律师”，还是在考“能不能指定自己喜欢的人”。这题只要法院完成了指派义务，被告就不能因为不喜欢辩护建议而要求另换律师。

核心判例： Wheat v. United States - 强调被告有权获得有效辩护人，但没有权利挑自己偏好的律师。

思维导图

先看被告身份：她是贫困被告（indigent defendant）吗？
是：法院只要指派律师（appointed counsel），就先满足第六修正案的基本要求。
再问：她主张的是“换成我喜欢的律师”还是“根本没有律师”？
卡死点：counsel of choice 不是贫困被告的默认权利。
本题事实：法院已经给了公设辩护人，被告只是对其认罪建议不满。
结论：没有第六修正案违反，答案选 B。
反向误区：“被判刑一年”不等于“没收回自由就没右边”；但本题真正争点不是刑期长短，而是能不能自己选律师。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然她对公设辩护人的建议很反感，那法院拒绝换人一定不公平。

但考试真正问的是：法院有没有满足任命律师（appointment of counsel）的义务，而不是被告能不能按喜好换成自己想要的人。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的不满有没有发生」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干 法院已经指派公设辩护人，对贫困被告来说这已满足第六修正案；她没有律师选择权（counsel of choice）。

❌ 事实误判 | 刑期状态偷换

✕ A: 把sentence is not actually imposed当成关键，但题干是“已被判刑，只是 suspended”。

❌ 概念混淆 | 自选律师误读

✕ C: 以为counsel of her own choosing对贫困被告也当然成立，错把富人规则套到穷被告身上。

❌ 法律适用 | 无效辩护跳步

✕ D: 只看到辩护人建议认罪，就直接跳到incompetent counsel，但题干没有无效辩护的两步门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“有无指派律师”和“能否挑律师”，再排除无效辩护这条旁支。

考场速记

记住一句：贫困被告（indigent defendant）有律师，不一定有自己挑律师的权利。看到法院已派公设辩护人，就先别把“不满意”误当成“宪法违背”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
An elementary school teacher detained a student after school. A state prosecutor, alleging that the detention was improper, filed an information charging the teacher with false imprisonment. At trial, the jury rendered a not-guilty verdict.
The student later revealed that on the day of the incident, the teacher had hidden the student in a closet to prevent him from being found. The state prosecutor then filed an information charging the teacher with kidnapping, which requires all of the elements required to establish false imprisonment as well as the movement or hiding of the victim. The teacher, contending that his constitutional rights were violated, has filed a motion to dismiss the charge.
Should the court grant this motion?

choices.A: No, because kidnapping requires proof of an additional element that false imprisonment does not.
choices.B: No, because the teacher was not previously subject to punishment for his behavior.
choices.C: Yes, because both crimes are based on the teacher's conduct at a single event.
choices.D: Yes, because the teacher was previously found not guilty of false imprisonment.
