(attaches
automatically)

A court should exclude (i.e., suppress) any statement that was taken in violation of a defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel. This right:

• automatically attaches once judicial proceedings have commenced (e.g., when the defendant is indicted) and

• guarantees a defendant access to an attorney at every critical stage of the proceedings.

A critical stage is an event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial, including interrogations by law enforcement officers and police informants. For Sixth Amendment purposes, an undercover police informant interrogates a defendant by directly asking questions or engaging in conduct designed to deliberately elicit an incriminating response.*

(Choice B) Here, the man was indicted for bank robbery (judicial proceedings commenced). After he was jailed pending trial, the prosecutor put an undercover informant in his cell to get information about the crime. To do this, the informant constantly boasted about his own crimes—i.e., acted to deliberately elicit an incriminating response from the man (interrogation) (Choice B). Because an interrogation is a critical stage requiring access to counsel and no attorney was provided, the man's statement was obtained in violation of the Sixth Amendment and will likely be excluded.

*However, no Sixth Amendment violation occurs when an undercover informant is placed in a defendant's cell simply to listen to and report statements made in the absence of counsel.

(Choices A and C) The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination requires police to give Miranda warnings before custodial interrogation. But Miranda warnings are not required if a suspect is unaware that the interrogator is a police officer or informant.** Here, the man boasted to an undercover informant, so Miranda warnings were not required and no Fifth Amendment violation occurred. And though police initially Mirandized the man when arrested, these warnings do not absolve the Sixth Amendment violation.

**Unlike the Fifth Amendment, the Sixth Amendment protects incriminating statements made in the absence of counsel when the defendant does not know the interrogator is a police officer or informant.

📌 Educational Objective

The Sixth Amendment right to counsel automatically attaches once judicial proceedings commence and guarantees access to an attorney during all critical stages of the prosecution—including interrogations. An interrogation occurs when, for example, an undercover police informant engages in conduct deliberately designed to elicit incriminating information.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to counsel).
  • United States v. Henry, 447 U.S. 264, 271–74 (1980) (finding a violation of the Sixth Amendment right to counsel when a cellmate, acting under government instruction, actively engaged the defendant in conversation that elicited incriminating statements about the crime for which the defendant was indicted and in custody).
  • Illinois v. Perkins, 496 U.S. 292, 296–98 (1990) (holding that only known law enforcement must give Miranda warnings prior to custodial interrogation).
  • Kuhlmann v. Wilson, 477 U.S. 436, 459 (1986) (holding that the Sixth Amendment right to counsel is not violated when an incriminating statement is made to a jailhouse informant who is put in "close proximity" to the defendant but takes no action designed to elicit the statement).

zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为该男子未受到线人的讯问。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Right to counsel

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告已经被起诉后，政府安排的狱中线人如果主动设法引出认罪内容，会不会违反第六修正案的律师在场权（right to counsel）。

三秒认题路径：

已起诉 → 关押中 → 线人诱供 → 第六修正案（Sixth Amendment） → 排除

核心法律规则

只记这一条就够做题

第六修正案（Sixth Amendment）的律师在场权（right to counsel）会在司法程序开始后自动生效，像起诉书已经回来这一步，考试上就算“开始算”。

一旦进入这个阶段，政府在关键阶段（critical stage）不能绕开律师去“挖”被告的认罪；deliberately elicit 的意思就是故意引出对自己不利的话。

如果线人只是安静听，被动记录，通常不一定违规；但这里线人是被安排去套话，还用炫耀犯罪的方式逼出供述，所以会压中第六修正案。

核心判例： United States v. Henry — 政府安排的狱中线人主动诱出被告供述，属于违反第六修正案的取证。

思维导图

先问：这题是不是已经进入司法程序？
是已经起诉（indicted），所以第六修正案自动附着。
再问：线人是在“听”，还是在“诱”口供？
听只是贴近旁听，通常不违法。
诱用炫耀犯罪、套话等方式让被告说出案情，就是interrogation。
卡死点：effectively reviewable 不适用这里；本题卡在“是否故意引出供述”这一关。
结论：既然已起诉 + 线人诱供 + 没有律师在场 → 排除供述。
答案选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他先被读过Miranda warnings，而且线人又没直接问问题，那是不是就没问题。

但考试真正问的是：第六修正案下，政府能不能在已起诉后用狱中线人故意引出供述。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。这里不是在比谁先开口，而是在看政府有没有绕过律师去做诱供。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的indicted 加上狱中线人被指示去套话，说明这是第六修正案的关键阶段诱供；供述应被排除。

❌ 概念混淆 | 米兰达误套

✕ A: 把 Miranda 当成万能通行证。

❌ 法律适用 | 只看没发问

✕ B: 只看 not interrogated，漏掉“故意引出”也算。

❌ 事实误判 | 自证其罪偷换

✕ C: 把 privilege 当成本题主轴，忽略真正冲突是右辩护权。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“是否已起诉”，再看线人有没有主动诱供，最后直接对照第六修正案。

考场速记

记忆口诀：已起诉 + 关键阶段 + 故意引出，就先想到第六修正案；线人只是“旁听”未必有事，线人一旦开始“套”，就很危险。

顺手记一句：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉口诀，但这题不是上诉题，别跑偏。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
Police detectives suspected that a man was involved in a homicide committed during a robbery of a convenience store but did not have enough evidence to obtain an arrest warrant. One morning, the detectives telephoned the man and asked if he would mind coming to the police station to talk. The man agreed and met the detectives that afternoon.
Ten minutes into the interview, the detectives told the man that he was identified as a "person of interest" in the convenience store robbery and homicide and asked the man if investigators would find his fingerprints on the cash register. Suddenly, the man confessed to the detectives that he had committed the robbery but added that the store clerk's death was accidental and occurred when his gun "just went off."
The man was indicted for felony murder.
If the man files a motion to suppress the introduction of his statement into evidence, how will the court likely rule?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the man failed to invoke his right to remain silent during the interview with the detectives.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the man freely and voluntarily made the statement and was not entitled to Miranda warnings.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the custodial interrogation violated the man's rights to counsel and due process.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the man was effectively in custody and entitled to Miranda warnings once he was identified as a suspect.

Question

Statements taken in violation of a defendant's Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination should be excluded from evidence at the defendant's trial. To comply with this privilege, police need only administer Miranda warnings before a custodial interrogation—ie, when a person is in custody and subjected to interrogation. A person is in custody when:

  • the person is placed under formal arrest (eg, arrest pursuant to a warrant or based on probable cause) or
  • the person's freedom of movement is restrained to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to terminate the encounter (eg, physical restraint during questioning, told by officers not free to leave).

Here, the man went to the police station voluntarily (not under arrest) and could have terminated the encounter (no restraint). Therefore, he was not in custody, and being told by the detectives that he was a suspect in the robbery-homicide would not change that fact (Choice D). As a result, he was not entitled to Miranda warnings. Accordingly, the man's voluntary admission that he committed the robbery was not taken in violation of the Fifth Amendment, and his motion to suppress will likely be denied.

(Choices A & C) Under the Fifth Amendment, a person may invoke the right to silence and the right to counsel when subjected to custodial interrogation. Here, the man was not in custody, so these rights were never implicated. Additionally, introducing his statement into evidence would not violate his due process right to a fair trial since the confession was given voluntarily—not by coercion.

📌 Educational Objective

Miranda warnings are only required when a suspect is in custody and subjected to interrogation. A suspect is in custody when formally arrested or when the suspect's freedom of movement is so restricted that a reasonable person would not feel free to terminate the encounter.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 469–72 (1966) (listing the warnings required prior to custodial interrogations).
  • Oregon v. Mathiason, 429 U.S. 492, 495–96 (1977) (explaining that custody requires a restriction on a person's freedom, not merely questioning at police station).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：米兰达警告（Miranda warnings）只在羁押性讯问（custodial interrogation）时才要给；单纯被请去警局聊天、还可自由离开，不会自动触发排除。

三秒认题路径：

自愿到场 → 还可离开 → 不是羁押 → 不触发Miranda → 不能压制

核心法律规则

把规则说成人话

第五修正案（Fifth Amendment）防的是被迫自证其罪，所以只有在羁押性讯问（custodial interrogation）里，警方才必须先读 Miranda warnings。

羁押（custody）的考场意思：要么已经正式逮捕，要么一个合理人会觉得自己不能结束谈话、不能离开现场；仅仅在警局接受提问，本身不等于羁押。

本题里，男子是自己答应去警局、也没有被限制离开，所以即使警探后来告诉他“你是嫌疑人”，也还没把场景变成必须读警告的羁押讯问。

核心判例： Oregon v. Mathiason — 只是在警局被问话，不会因为“被当作嫌疑人”就自动变成羁押。

思维导图

先问：有没有 羁押（custody）？
YES正式逮捕 / 合理人不能离开
再问：是不是 讯问（interrogation）？
YES警方话语在诱发自证其罪
结论：先读 Miranda warnings
没读却继续问 → 口供可压制
NO自愿到场 / 可结束谈话 / 可离开
门槛没过，Miranda 不启动
本题卡死点：只是在警局聊天，不等于羁押
最终答案：驳回压制动议（B）

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他一被说成“person of interest”就成了嫌疑人，所以口供一定要排除。

但考试真正问的是：有没有羁押，不是警方有没有在心里把他当坏人。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干最关键的事实是他自愿去警局、没有被限制离开，所以不是 羁押性讯问（custodial interrogation），不需要先读 Miranda，口供可用。

❌ 概念混淆 | 权利触发误判

✕ A: 把“没主动说不”当成门槛，remain silent 还没到触发点。

❌ 法律适用 | 特权扩张误判

✕ C: 把 due process 和自白自愿性混成一题，这里没有胁迫。

❌ 事实误判 | 嫌疑状态偷换

✕ D: 只看到“被当成嫌疑人”，却漏掉他仍然能走，effectively in custody 还没成立。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看程序姿态：先判羁押，再看是否讯问，最后才谈 Miranda 和压制。

考场速记

记住一句：Miranda 只管羁押性讯问，不是“在警局说话”就自动触发。

口诀：Miranda only if custody + interrogation；自愿到场、可离开、未被控制，通常就选不压制。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
The legislature of State X is debating reforms in the law governing insanity. Two reforms have been proposed. Proposal A would eliminate the insanity defense altogether. Proposal B would retain the defense but place on the defendant the burden of proving insanity by a preponderance of the evidence. Opponents of the reforms argue that the proposals would be unconstitutional under the due process clause of the United States Constitution.
Which of the proposed reforms would be unconstitutional?

choices.A: Neither proposal.
choices.B: Proposal A only.
choices.C: Proposal B only.
choices.D: Both proposals.

questions.explanation:
Affirmative defenses
  • Duress
  • Insanity
  • Necessity
  • Entrapment
  • Defense of persons/property
Mnemonic:  DINED

The Fourteenth Amendment due process clause (applicable to the states) requires the prosecution to prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. Since an affirmative defense does not challenge any elements of a crime—it instead provides a justification or excuse for criminal conduct—the due process clause does not apply. Therefore, state law can place any burden of proof on either party (prosecution or defense) to establish or negate an affirmative defense. Additionally, states can freely modify or eliminate such defenses.

Insanity is an affirmative defense because it does not challenge any element of a crime and instead provides an excuse for the defendant's criminal behavior. Since due process does not regulate affirmative defenses, Proposal B can require a defendant to prove this defense by a preponderance of the evidence (Choices C & D). And Proposal A can completely eliminate insanity as an affirmative defense without violating due process (Choices B & D). Therefore, both proposals are constitutional.

Educational objective:
Due process does not apply to affirmative defenses (eg, insanity), so state law can require the defendant to prove an affirmative defense by any standard. Additionally, a legislature can freely modify or eliminate these defenses.

References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV § 1 (due process clause).
  • Leland v. Oregon, 343 U.S. 790, 799 (1952) (recognizing that states can place any burden of proof on the defendant to establish an insanity defense).
  • Clark v. Arizona, 548 U.S. 735, 752–53 (2006) (holding that a state can narrow its insanity defense).
questions.zh-question: 哪项提案是违宪的？

zh-choices.A: 两项提案均不违宪。
zh-choices.B: 仅提案A违宪。
zh-choices.C: 仅提案B违宪。
zh-choices.D: 两项提案均违宪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Due process

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：精神失常抗辩（insanity defense）是不是必须受 正当程序（due process） 保护，以及州能不能把举证责任放给被告，甚至直接取消这个抗辩。

三秒认题路径：

抗辩非要件 → 正当程序不管 → 州可分配举证 → 也可删掉 → 两项都合宪

核心法律规则

四teenth Amendment 的 正当程序条款（due process clause） 要求控方证明犯罪 构成要件（elements） 到 beyond a reasonable doubt，但这条规则主要管的是“罪有没有成立”，不管“被告能不能拿某个 积极抗辩（affirmative defense） 来脱责”。

像 精神失常（insanity） 这种抗辩，本质上不是在否认犯罪要件，而是在说“我虽然做了，但法律上应当免责”，所以州可以把举证责任放给被告，标准也可以提高到 preponderance of the evidence。

同理，州立法也可以把这个抗辩缩小，甚至直接取消；对 MBE 来说，答案关键不是“这会不会让人觉得不公平”，而是“正当程序有没有管到这个抗辩”。

核心判例： Leland v. Oregon 认可州可要求被告证明精神失常抗辩；Clark v. Arizona 说明州甚至可以缩小该抗辩范围。

思维导图

题干先问：州能不能改 insanity defense？
第一关：这是不是犯罪 构成要件？
不是。它是 积极抗辩，不是控方必须证明的犯罪要素。
第二关：due process 会不会锁死州的安排？
不会。州可规定被告来证明精神失常，甚至可把这个抗辩直接删掉。
第三关：题目里的两项改革分别怎么过关？
Proposal A：取消抗辩 仍可行；Proposal B：被告负担证明 也可行。
结论：没有哪一项违反正当程序，答案选 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然精神失常关系到“能不能免责”，那州把举证责任丢给被告，或者直接取消它，好像很不公平。

但考试真正问的是：due process 有没有要求州必须保留这个抗辩、并且必须由控方证明。答案没有这么强。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的关键点是 insanity 属于 affirmative defense，不受正当程序强制保护，所以州既能改举证标准，也能直接取消它。

❌ 概念混淆 | 要件抗辩混淆

✕ B: 把精神失常当成控方要证明的要件，才会以为 dismiss 一定违宪。

❌ 法律适用 | 举证标准误套

✕ C: 只看到 preponderance 就慌，但州对抗辩提高标准本来就能做。

❌ 事实误判 | 取消范围偷换

✕ D: 题干没有说州只能保留抗辩不能删，直接假设“可删”违宪是在偷换条件。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看它是不是 affirmative defense，再判断正当程序有没有把州的立法手脚绑住。

考场速记

DINED 记忆：Duress、Insanity、Necessity、Entrapment、Defense of persons/property 常见为 affirmative defenses。这类抗辩通常不被 due process 绑死，州可以分配举证责任，甚至缩小或取消。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Police received information from an undercover police officer that she had just seen two men (whom she described) in a red pickup truck selling marijuana to schoolchildren near the city's largest high school. A few minutes later, two police officers saw a pickup truck fitting the description a half block from the high school. The driver of the truck matched the description of one of the men described by the undercover officer.
The only passenger was a young woman who was in the back of the truck. The police saw her get out and stand at a nearby bus stop. They stopped the truck and searched the driver. In the pocket of the driver's jacket, the police found a small bottle of pills that they recognized as narcotics. They then broke open a locked toolbox attached to the flatbed of the truck and found a small sealed envelope inside. They opened it and found marijuana. They also found a quantity of cocaine in the glove compartment.
After completing their search of the driver and the truck, the police went over to the young woman and searched her purse. In her purse, they found a small quantity of heroin. Both the driver and the young woman were arrested and charged with unlawful possession of narcotics.
If the young woman moves to suppress the use of the heroin as evidence, how should the court rule on her motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because she had been a passenger in the truck and the police had probable cause to search the truck.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because she was planning to leave the scene by bus and so exigent circumstances existed.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because she did not fit the description given by the undercover officer and her mere presence does not justify the search.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the police should have seized her purse and then obtained a warrant to search it.

The exclusionary rule prevents the introduction of evidence found during an illegal Fourth Amendment search—ie, a search conducted without a warrant or an exception to the warrant requirement. Under the search incident to lawful arrest exception, police can conduct a warrantless search that is:

  • limited to a person's body and areas in his/her immediate reach and
  • conducted immediately before or after a valid arrest.

An arrest is valid when it is based on probable cause, a reasonable belief (greater than mere suspicion) that the person arrested committed a crime. But a person's mere presence with a criminal—or in a vehicle believed to contain evidence of a crime—is insufficient to create such a belief.

Here, the police saw the young woman exit a truck that matched the officer's description. They approached the woman, searched her purse without a warrant, and arrested her. But her arrest was not supported by probable cause (ie, it was invalid) since:

  • she did not fit the description of the suspected drug dealers and
  • her mere presence in the truck was insufficient grounds to believe that she had committed a crime (Choice A).

And since the arrest was invalid, the warrantless search of the woman's purse conducted immediately before that arrest was also invalid (Choice D). Therefore, the heroin found during that search should be suppressed.

(Choice B) Under the exigent circumstance exception, police can conduct a warrantless search if they reasonably believe that prompt action is necessary to prevent a suspect's escape or the destruction of evidence. Here, the woman's plan to leave the scene by bus did not create an exigent circumstance because police had no reason to believe that she was a suspect in, or had evidence of, a crime (since the undercover officer described two men).

📌 Educational Objective

Police can conduct a warrantless search of a person's body or areas in his/her immediate reach if the search is conducted immediately before or after a lawful arrest. But a passenger's mere presence with a criminal or in a suspicious vehicle is not enough to establish probable cause.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Di Re, 332 U.S. 581, 587 (1948) (explaining that a person's mere presence in a suspected vehicle does not forfeit his/her right to be free from unreasonable searches).

警方从一名卧底警官处获得信息，称她刚看到两名男子（她描述了他们的特征）驾驶一辆红色皮卡车，在该市最大的高中附近向学童出售大麻。几分钟后，两名警官在离高中半个街区的地方看到一辆符合描述的皮卡车。卡车司机符合卧底警官描述的两名男子之一的特征。唯一的乘客是一名年轻女子，她当时在卡车后部。警方看到她下车，站在附近的一个公交车站。他们拦下卡车并搜查了司机。在司机夹克口袋里，警方发现了一小瓶他们认为是麻醉品的药丸。随后，他们撬开了一个固定在卡车平板上的上锁工具箱，并在里面发现了一个密封的小信封。他们打开信封，发现了大麻。他们还在储物箱里发现了一定数量的可卡因。完成对司机和卡车的搜查后，警方走向该年轻女子并搜查了她的手提包。在她的手提包里，他们发现了一小包海洛因。司机和该年轻女子均被逮捕，并被控非法持有麻醉品。
如果该年轻女子提出动议，要求排除海洛因作为证据的使用，法院应如何裁决她的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为她曾是卡车的乘客，且警方有 probable cause 搜查卡车。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为她正计划乘公交车离开现场，因此存在 exigent circumstances（紧急情况）。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为她不符合卧底警官提供的描述，且她仅仅在场并不能证明搜查的合理性。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为警方应该扣押她的手提包，然后获得 warrant（搜查令）才能搜查。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Search and seizure

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：警察对这名女子有没有逮捕依据的 probable cause，以及随后搜她包是不是search incident to lawful arrest 的合法附带搜查。

三秒认题路径：

只见别人可疑 → 先搜了车 → 再搜女子包 → 女子非嫌疑人 → 证据应排除

核心法律规则

第四修正案（Fourth Amendment） 里，没搜查令的搜查通常要靠例外才合法。附带逮捕搜查（search incident to lawful arrest） 只允许在有效逮捕（lawful arrest） 前后、并且针对被逮捕者身体和立即可及范围内的区域。

关键先看逮捕有没有probable cause：要有足够事实让警察合理相信这个人自己犯了罪。mere presence（只是和可疑人物同在现场）不够，坐在可疑车里也不自动变成嫌疑人。

所以本题里，女子既不符合卧底描述，又只是从车里下来站在公交站，警察没有足够理由把她当成涉毒者；她包里的搜查就不能借search incident to arrest 洗白。

核心判例： United States v. Di Re - 只是在可疑车辆或和嫌疑人同场，不会自动给警察对你成立 probable cause。

思维导图

先问：警察对女子本人有没有 probable cause？
NO 她不是卧底描述的两名男子之一
↓
只是在车里出现 / 下车等公交，不等于她自己有犯罪嫌疑
↓
不能先把她当成可搜身对象
再问：搜她的包能否靠 search incident to arrest？
NO 前提是合法逮捕
↓
没有对她的 probable cause，附带搜查就失去支点
↓
答案：排除 heroin 证据

考点陷阱

你可能会想：她坐在可疑卡车里，又刚好想搭公交离开，警察是不是可以顺手把她也查了。

但考试真正问的是：警察有没有能指向她本人的 probable cause，而不是这辆车里“有人看起来像坏人”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

换句话说，车可疑，不等于乘客自动可搜；“想走”也不等于已经形成exigent circumstances。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干关键事实是：卧底只描述了两名男子，这名女子不在描述中，只是从车里下来站在公交站；对她本人没有 probable cause，所以搜她的包得到的 heroin 要排除。

❌ 概念混淆 | 车搜人乱套

✕ A: 把车上有 probable cause 直接扩成能搜她本人，passenger 不是自动嫌疑人。

❌ 法律适用 | 紧急例外误套

✕ B: 她想坐公交离开，不等于警方对她已有马上失证风险。

❌ 事实误判 | 先后顺序偷换

✕ D: 想把她的包包装成先扣押再申请令状，题干里警察根本没有先对她成立合法扣押基础。

这题建议用什么方法？

先盯住“逮捕她本人有没有 probable cause”，再看附带搜查能不能站住。

考场速记

记住一句：有车可疑，不等于人可疑；先看警察能不能对“这个人”说出 probable cause，再谈搜包、搜身、附带逮捕搜查。

以后遇到这类题，先默念：mere presence 不够，Di Re 先挡住“连坐式搜查”。

reason.en: Highlights that the woman was a passenger who did not match the description of the two men.
reason.zh: 强调该女性是乘客，且不符合两名男子的描述。

reason.zh: 表明她在搜查发生前已与车辆分离，使得车辆搜查规则不适用于其皮包。

highlights.text: went over to the young woman and searched her purse

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A state prosecutor filed an information charging a man with first-degree arson and first-degree murder. In the applicable jurisdiction, first-degree arson is defined as "the willful and malicious setting fire to and burning of a dwelling."
After the presentation of the prosecution's case, the man's counsel moved for a dismissal of the arson charge because the prosecution had failed to prove that the burned structure was a dwelling. The court granted the motion. However, because the evidence presented by the prosecution established second-degree arson, the court permitted the prosecution to amend the information to charge the man with second-degree arson.
The man then took the stand and, while testifying, admitted that the structure was a dwelling. The court permitted the prosecution to again amend the information to charge the man with first-degree arson. The jury subsequently convicted the man of first-degree arson.
Can the man successfully challenge his conviction on constitutional grounds?

choices.A: No, because the man's own testimony caused the reinstatement of the first-degree arson charge.
choices.B: No, because the trial was not terminated by the dismissal of the first-degree arson charge.
choices.C: Yes, because the court dismissed the first-degree arson charge against the man.
choices.D: Yes, because the man was not charged with arson through an indictment.

questions.explanation:
Double jeopardy
(second prosecution for same offense)
Did jeopardy attach in first prosecution?
  • Jury impaneled and sworn
  • Judge begins to hear evidence
→
Allowed
Yes
Did first prosecution end with:
  • Conviction
  • Acquittal
  • Mistrial (with no manifest necessity)
→
Allowed
Yes
Does second prosecution involve
the same offense?
  • Identical elements
  • All elements of one crime are elements
    of the other
→
Allowed
Yes
Prohibited

Double jeopardy protects criminal defendants from undue harassment and expense by prohibiting:

  • multiple punishments for the same offense
  • a second prosecution for the same offense after a conviction (i.e., a guilty judgment) and
  • a second prosecution for the same offense after an acquittal (i.e., a not-guilty judgment based on the defendant's innocence or the prosecution's failure to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt).

A grant of a motion to dismiss in favor of the accused based on the prosecution's failure to prove the elements of a crime at the close of the state's case is equivalent to an acquittal.

Here, the man was effectively acquitted of first-degree arson when the charge was dismissed after the prosecution presented its case. Therefore, the man can successfully challenge his subsequent conviction of first-degree arson as a violation of the double jeopardy clause.

(Choice A) Once a charge has been dismissed on substantive grounds at trial, double jeopardy protections prohibit that charge from being reinstated—even if the defendant subsequently admits that he committed the crime or an element thereof.

(Choice B) The dismissal of a charge against a defendant on substantive grounds after the trial has begun constitutes an acquittal with respect to that charge—even if the trial continues because the defendant is facing other charges.

(Choice D) A state is not constitutionally required to use the grand jury process (i.e., indictment) when charging a defendant because the Fifth Amendment grand jury clause has not been incorporated by the Fourteenth Amendment.

📌 Educational Objective

The double jeopardy clause prohibits a second prosecution for the same offense after an acquittal. A dismissal based on the prosecution's failure to prove the elements of a crime is equivalent to an acquittal.

📚 References
  • Smalis v. Pennsylvania, 476 U.S. 140, 145–46 (1986) (holding that the prosecution could not reinstate a charge that was dismissed in the same trial court for lack of evidence).
questions.zh-question: 一名州检察官提起一份信息（information），指控一名男子犯有一级纵火罪（first-degree arson）和一级谋杀罪（first-degree murder）。在适用司法管辖区，一级纵火罪被定义为“故意恶意地放火焚烧住宅”。控方举证结束后，该男子的律师动议驳回纵火罪指控，理由是控方未能证明被烧毁的建筑物是住宅。法院批准了该动议。然而，由于控方提交的证据确立了二级纵火罪（second-degree arson），法院允许控方修改信息，指控该男子犯有二级纵火罪。该男子随后出庭作证，作证时承认该建筑物是住宅。法院允许控方再次修改信息，指控该男子犯有一级纵火罪。陪审团随后裁定该男子犯有一级纵火罪。该男子能否成功基于宪法理由质疑其定罪？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为该男子自己的证词导致了一级纵火罪指控的恢复。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为审判并未因一级纵火罪指控被驳回而终止。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为法院驳回了针对该男子的一级纵火罪指控。
zh-choices.D: 能，因为该男子并非通过大陪审团起诉书（indictment）被指控纵火罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Double jeopardy

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：庭审中因证据不足被法官驳回的第一度纵火指控，是否等同于无罪判决，从而触发双重危险禁止再次恢复同一指控。

三秒认题路径：

证据不足驳回 → 视同无罪 → 同一罪名再提 → 双重危险 → 禁止

核心法律规则

拿分规则

双重危险（double jeopardy）考场意思：同一罪名一旦已经出现实质性无罪结论，检方通常不能再把这项指控捡回来重提。

无罪裁定（acquittal）考场意思：只要法官因为证据不足（insufficiency of the evidence）而结束该项指控，就算程序上还在审别的罪，也已经挡住对这项罪的再次追诉。

实体性驳回（dismissal on substantive grounds）考场意思：不是纯程序瑕疵，而是检方没证明构成要件，所以后面即使被告自己承认事实，也不能把已经“输掉”的同一指控再救回来。

核心判例： Smalis v. Pennsylvania - 证据不足导致的驳回，等同无罪，不能在同一案件里恢复同一项指控。

思维导图

先看这是不是同一项指控被“翻案重来”？
1.陪审团已审理、证据已进入庭审，jeopardy attach。
2.法官因检方没证明“dwelling”而准许dismissal，这一步在考场上就是acquittal。
3.后面被告自己作证说是 dwelling，只是事实补洞，不是给检方重开一次第一度纵火的机会。
卡死点：已经对第一度纵火作出无罪性终结 → 不能再把同一罪名改回去 → 选 C
结果.不是“能不能证明新事实”，而是“这项罪是不是已经被判输过”。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：被告后来自己承认了“dwelling”，所以检方当然可以把第一度纵火再加回来。

但考试真正问的是：法官已经因为证据不足把这项罪名判掉了，后面就不能靠新证词把同一指控重新活过来。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「被告后来有没有把秘密说出来」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里第一度纵火已因检方没证明 dwelling而被法官驳回，这在考场上就是无罪性终结，之后再恢复同一罪名会触发双重危险。

❌ 概念混淆 | 自认补救误判

✕ A: 以为own testimony能洗回指控，但先前的无罪性驳回已经锁死了。

❌ 法律适用 | 终止要件误判

✕ B: 把“还在审别的罪”当成没终止这项罪，但双重危险看的是这项指控是否已被驳为无罪。

❌ 事实误判 | 起诉形式偷换

✕ D: indictment不是这题的输赢点，州法院也不因没用大陪审团就自动失分。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“是否已经作出无罪性终结”，再看检方能否把同一罪名恢复；别被后来的补充事实带跑。

考场速记

记住一句：证据不足的驳回 = 无罪，同一罪名不能在同一案件里被检方再捡回来。

这题的快记法：先问“是不是同一罪”，再问“前面是不是已经输过”；一旦答案都是“是”，就直接挡掉重提。

reason.zh: 法院的裁决，在双重危险判定中等同于实体上的无罪判决。

reason.en: Signals a claim under the Double Jeopardy Clause of the Fifth Amendment.
reason.zh: 暗示依据宪法第五修正案双重危险条款提出的主张。

reason.zh: 干扰项，主张随后的自认可以推翻此前无罪判决的双重危险保护。

reason.zh: 干扰项，暗示双重危险仅在整个审判结束时适用，而非针对个别指控。

C.text: court dismissed the first-degree arson charge

reason.zh: 正确指出因证据不足驳回指控构成无罪判决。

D.text: not charged with arson through an indictment

label.zh: 未经大陪审团起诉书指控

reason.en: Establishes that the dismissal is substantive and based on a failure of proof, rather than procedural.
reason.zh: 确立了该驳回是实体性的且基于证据不足，而非程序性驳回。

highlights.text: The court granted the motion.

label.zh: 准予驳回等同于无罪判决

reason.en: Triggers double jeopardy protection for the first-degree arson charge.
reason.zh: 触发了对一级纵火罪指控的双重危险保护。

highlights.text: The court permitted the prosecution to again amend the information to charge the man with first-degree arson.

label.zh: 重新恢复已被宣告无罪的指控

reason.en: Reinstating the acquitted charge during the same trial violates the double jeopardy clause.
reason.zh: 在同一审判中重新恢复已被宣告无罪的指控违反了双重危险条款。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was charged with first-degree murder. The prosecutor notified defense counsel that the state would seek the death penalty. Defense counsel filed a motion challenging the prosecution of the man on the ground that he was not mentally competent to stand trial because he has an IQ of 68. After a hearing on the motion, the court concluded that the man was mentally competent to stand trial. The man was subsequently convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to death.
When a date was set for the man's execution, defense counsel filed a habeas corpus petition claiming that the man's execution would violate the Eighth Amendment because he is mentally incompetent. A state statute defines an intellectual disability as an IQ of 65 or lower. Current medical guidelines provide that an IQ between 70 and 75 indicates a significant limitation in intellectual functioning, such that an individual within or below that range is presumptively considered to have an intellectual disability.
Should the court allow the man's execution to proceed?

choices.A: No, because the statute created an unacceptable risk of execution for a person with intellectual disabilities.
choices.B: No, because there was no finding that the man was insane or suffering from a severe mental disorder.
choices.C: Yes, because the court concluded that the man was mentally competent to stand trial.
choices.D: Yes, because the court must follow the state statute that defines intellectual disability.

questions.explanation:
Eighth Amendment cruel & unusual punishment
  • No death penalty for:
    • juveniles
    • intellectually deficient persons
    • adults convicted of nonhomicide offenses
  • No life-without-parole for juveniles convicted of nonhomicide offenses
  • No mandatory life-without-parole for juveniles convicted of homicide

The Eighth Amendment prohibits execution of an individual with an intellectual disability. In defining when an individual has an intellectual disability, a state cannot:

• ignore current medical guidelines or

• impose a strict cutoff that precludes a finding of intellectual disability if an individual has an IQ over 70.

That is because either approach creates an unacceptable risk that persons with intellectual disabilities will be executed.

Here, the man's IQ of 68 is above the state's statutory cutoff for intellectual disabilities (IQ of 65 or lower). However, current medical guidelines provide that an IQ between 70 and 75 indicates a significant limitation in intellectual functioning, so an individual within or below that range (as seen here) is presumed to have an intellectual disability. And because the Eighth Amendment prohibits states from ignoring these guidelines in defining an intellectual disability, the court should bar the man's execution.

(Choice B) The court could execute the man if there was no finding that he was insane or suffering from a severe mental disorder. Therefore, this is not a reason to halt the man's execution.

(Choice C) Even if an individual has been found mentally competent to stand trial (as seen here), he cannot be executed if he is found mentally incompetent to be executed.

(Choice D) The state statute violates the Eighth Amendment because it ignores current medical guidelines in defining an intellectual disability. Therefore, the court cannot rely on the statute to justify the man's execution.

📌 Educational Objective

The Eighth Amendment prohibits execution of an individual with an intellectual disability. In defining an intellectual disability, states must consider current medical guidelines and cannot impose a strict cutoff that precludes a finding of intellectual disability if an individual has an IQ over 70.

📚 References
  • Atkins v. Virginia, 536 U.S. 304, 321 (2002) (holding that the Eighth Amendment prohibits execution of an individual with intellectual disabilities).
  • Hall v. Florida, 572 U.S. 701, 724 (2014) (disapproving rigid IQ cutoffs for determination of intellectual disabilities for execution).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子被控一级谋杀罪。检察官通知辩护律师，州政府将寻求判处死刑。辩护律师提出动议，质疑对该男子的起诉，理由是该男子智商为68，不具备受审的精神能力（mentally competent to stand trial）。经过对该动议的听证，法院认定该男子具备受审的精神能力。该男子随后被判一级谋杀罪成立并判处死刑。
在确定该男子执行死刑的日期后，辩护律师提交了一份人身保护令（habeas corpus）请愿书，声称该男子的处决将违反第八修正案，因为他精神上无行为能力（mentally incompetent）。一项州法规将智力残疾（intellectual disability）定义为智商65或更低。当前的医学指南规定，智商在70到75之间表明智力功能存在显著限制，因此，处于或低于该范围的个体被推定为患有智力残疾。
法院是否应允许对该男子执行死刑？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为该法规对智力残疾者造成了不可接受的处决风险。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为没有认定该男子精神失常或患有严重精神障碍。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为法院认定该男子具备受审的精神能力。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为法院必须遵循定义智力残疾的州法规。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Cruel & unusual punishment

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：州不能用过死的 IQ 截线来挡掉智力障碍（intellectual disability）的认定，所以不能直接执行死刑。

三秒认题路径：

死刑执行 → IQ 68 → 州线过死 → 看医学标准 → 不能执行

核心法律规则

只抓本题需要的规则

第八修正案（Eighth Amendment）禁止对智力障碍（intellectual disability）的人执行死刑。州在定义该概念时，不能无视当前医学指南，也不能设一个硬性 IQ 截线，把 IQ over 70 的人一律排除在外。

考场意思：如果医学标准提示此人可能有智力障碍，州法再怎么写得更窄，也不能拿来直接放行死刑。这里的关键不是“能不能受审”，而是“能不能被执行”。

核心判例： Atkins v. Virginia 确认智力障碍者不得被执行；Hall v. Florida 进一步否定了僵硬的 IQ 截线。

思维导图

先看：题目是不是在问“现在能不能执行死刑”？
是走第八修正案。
州有没有把intellectual disability定得太死？
有，因为州法只认 IQ ≤ 65。
卡死点：不能忽视当前医学指南，不能把 IQ 过 70 的人一刀切排除。
题干事实：IQ 68，落在医学指南警戒区。
结论这类人仍可能被认定为智力障碍，不能执行。
答案落点：法院应阻止执行。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他已经被认定mentally competent to stand trial，所以现在当然可以执行。

但考试真正问的是：站得住庭审，不等于能被执行；这题盯的是执行时的intellectual disability，不是受审能力。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干IQ 68已落入医学指南警戒区，州却用 IQ 65 这条硬线挡住认定，属于第八修正案禁止的做法，所以不能执行。

❌ 概念混淆 | 受审能力错位

✕ B: 把 insane 当成这题标准，混淆了精神失常和智力障碍。

❌ 事实误判 | 受审结论偷换

✕ C: 受审时能站庭，不代表执行时就能被送上死刑台。

❌ 法律适用 | 州法硬线误用

✕ D: 想拿 state statute 直接盖过宪法，但州法不能排掉医学标准。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓执行时点，再看州法有没有用过死 IQ 线把医学标准挡掉。

考场速记

记忆口诀：Atkins 管“不能执行智力障碍者”，Hall 管“州不能用僵硬 IQ 截线”。看到死刑 + IQ，先问医学标准，再问州法是不是太死。

reason.en: The ultimate punishment sought by the prosecution, subject to Eighth Amendment limits.

reason.en: Distinct legal standard from the competency required for execution.

reason.zh: 禁止对智力障碍者执行死刑的宪法修正案。

label.zh: 宪法容忍的执行风险标准

reason.en: The constitutional standard under which rigid IQ cutoffs are evaluated.

B.text: insane or suffering from a severe mental disorder

label.zh: 精神失常或严重精神障碍标准

reason.en: Distractor mixing up competence to be executed with intellectual disability.
reason.zh: 混淆了可执行死刑的认知能力与智力障碍的干扰项。

reason.en: Incorrectly equates competency to stand trial with the eligibility to be executed.
reason.zh: 错误地将受审能力等同于可执行死刑的条件。

reason.en: Overlooks that federal constitutional law overrides state statutes defining intellectual disability.
reason.zh: 忽视了联邦宪法优于州关于智力障碍定义的成文法。

reason.en: Placing the defendant below the medical presumption threshold (70-75) but above the state statutory threshold (65).
reason.zh: 被告的IQ分数低于医学假定阈值（70-75），但高于州成文法阈值（65）。

highlights.text: IQ of 65 or lower

reason.en: The rigid cutoff imposed by state law that violates constitutional standards by ignoring medical guidelines.
reason.zh: 州法规定的僵硬界限，因无视医学指南而违反宪法标准。

reason.zh: 第八修正案要求各州必须考虑的医学标准。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
In a city, a number of armed bank robberies were committed near closing time by a masked man wearing a white hooded sweatshirt and blue sweatpants. Police saw a man wearing a white hooded sweatshirt and blue sweatpants pacing nervously outside one of the city's banks just before it closed. The police stopped the man and frisked the outer layers of his clothing for weapons but found none. They asked the man what he was doing outside the bank and pointed out that he was wearing clothing similar to clothing worn by the perpetrator of recent robberies. After pausing for several moments, the man confessed. The police had not provided him with any Miranda warnings.
After being charged with the bank robberies, the man moved to suppress his confession. The parties agreed, and the court properly found, that the police had reasonable suspicion, but not probable cause, at all times before the man confessed.
Should the man's motion to suppress be granted?

choices.A: No, because there was neither a Fourth Amendment violation nor a Miranda violation.
choices.B: Yes, because the confession was the fruit of a Fourth Amendment violation, even though there was no Miranda violation.
choices.C: Yes, because the confession was the fruit of a Miranda violation, even though there was no Fourth Amendment violation.
choices.D: Yes, because the confession was the fruit of both a Fourth Amendment violation and a Miranda violation.

questions.explanation:
Police-citizen encounters
Type Characteristics
Consensual
encounter
  • No suspicion required
  • Officer may approach citizen/engage in conversation
  • Citizen may:
  • respond to officer or
  • walk away
Terry stop
(stop & frisk)
  • Reasonable suspicion required
  • Officer may:
  • briefly question to confirm/dispel suspicion
  • frisk if reasonably believes person armed
  • Investigative in nature
Arrest
  • Probable cause required
  • Officer may:
  • search incident to arrest
  • interrogate after Mirandizing
  • Initiates criminal prosecution

A motion to suppress should be granted if the court finds that evidence (eg, a confession) was obtained in violation of the defendant's constitutional rights. These include the Fourth Amendment right to be free from unreasonable searches and seizures and the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination.

Under the Fourth Amendment, police may stop an individual for investigative purposes if they have a reasonable suspicion—ie, a reasonable belief, based on specific and articulable facts, that a person is (or will soon be) involved in criminal activity. During the investigatory detention (ie, Terry stop), police may:

• briefly stop and question a person to confirm or dispel their suspicions about the criminal activity and

• frisk (pat down) the person's outer garments to search for weapons if they reasonably suspect that the person may be armed and dangerous.

Under the Fifth Amendment, police must give a suspect Miranda warnings before conducting a custodial interrogation—ie, an interrogation that occurs when a suspect's freedom of movement is restricted to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to leave (eg, an arrest). Since a Terry stop is typically brief and does not substantially limit the suspect's freedom of movement (ie, no custody), Miranda warnings are not required before police questioning.

(Choices B & D) Here, police stopped and frisked the man when he was standing outside a bank before closing. However, this Terry stop did not violate the Fourth Amendment since police had reasonable suspicion that the man was (1) engaged in criminal activity and (2) armed and dangerous since he was wearing the same clothes as a man who had committed armed bank robberies near closing time (Choices B & D). And since Miranda warnings are not needed to question a suspect during a Terry stop, the man's confession is not protected by the Fifth Amendment. As a result, his motion to suppress his confession should be denied (Choices C & D).

📌 Educational Objective

During a Terry stop, police may (1) briefly stop and question a person if they reasonably suspect he/she is (or will soon be) involved in criminal activity and (2) frisk that person's outer garments if they reasonably suspect he/she is armed and dangerous. Additionally, Miranda warnings are not required to question a suspect during a Terry stop.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibiting unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • Terry v. Ohio, 392 U.S. 1, 21 (1968) (holding that investigatory detentions require reasonable suspicion).
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 468–70 (1966) (listing Miranda warnings).
  • Berkemer v. McCarty, 468 U.S. 420, 440 (1984) (recognizing that a person is not in custody during an investigatory detention).
questions.zh-question:
在一个城市，一名戴着面具、身穿白色连帽运动衫和蓝色运动裤的男子在银行临近关门时犯下了一系列持械抢劫案。警方看到一名身穿白色连帽运动衫和蓝色运动裤的男子，在城市一家银行即将关门前，在银行外紧张地踱步。警方拦住了该男子，并对其外衣进行了搜身以查找武器，但一无所获。他们询问该男子在银行外做什么，并指出他所穿的衣服与近期抢劫案罪犯所穿的衣服相似。在沉默片刻后，该男子供认了罪行。警方未向其告知任何 Miranda 警告。

在被指控犯有银行抢劫罪后，该男子动议排除其供述。各方当事人均同意，且法院也适当认定，在该男子招供前的所有时间里，警方都具有合理怀疑，但没有可成立的理由。

该男子提出的排除证据的动议是否应被批准？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为既没有违反第四修正案，也没有违反 Miranda 规则。
zh-choices.B: 应，因为该供述是违反第四修正案的产物，即使没有违反 Miranda 规则。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为该供述是违反 Miranda 规则的产物，即使没有违反第四修正案。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为该供述既是违反第四修正案的产物，也是违反 Miranda 规则的产物。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - The Privilege Against Compulsory Self-Incrimination

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：Terry stop 里警方能不能先问、再问出供述，而且还不需要 Miranda warnings（米兰达警告）。

三秒认题路径：

合理怀疑 → Terry扣留 → 非羁押 → 无需Miranda → 供述可用

核心法律规则

警方有 reasonable suspicion（合理怀疑） 时，可以做 Terry stop（临时盘问），也可以在合理相信对方可能持械且危险时做外衣拍身搜身。考场意思：这不是抓人，是短暂调查，所以通常不需要 probable cause（逮捕所需较高理由）。

Miranda warnings（米兰达警告） 只在 custodial interrogation（羁押性讯问） 前需要；Terry stop（临时盘问） 一般不算羁押。考场意思：只要人还没有被限制到“普通人觉得走不了”，先问话通常不触发 Miranda。

核心判例： Terry v. Ohio - 只要有合理怀疑，警方就能短暂拦停、问话并在必要时拍身搜身；Berkemer v. McCarty - 临时调查扣留通常不算羁押，所以不自动触发 Miranda。

思维导图

先问：这是终局羁押，还是 Terry stop？
题干事实 警察只因外观和地点相近就短暂拦停、盘问、拍身搜身；合理怀疑已够，非逮捕
第四修正案 有 reasonable suspicion（合理怀疑） + 可疑是武装危险者 → 可以停、问、拍
第五修正案 还没到 custody（羁押） → Miranda 不启动
结论 供述不是第四修正案果实，也不是 Miranda 违例果实 → 选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然警察最后问出供述，又没给 Miranda，那一定要压掉。

但考试真正问的是：当时是不是已经到了 custody（羁押）。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里只是 Terry stop，不是正式拘押，所以 Miranda 还没开。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的关键事实是只有 reasonable suspicion，警方做的是合法 Terry stop 和拍身搜身，后续问话也不属羁押性讯问，所以供述不该被压掉。

❌ 法律适用 | 果实理论误套

✕ B: 把合法临检硬说成 fruit，其实前提的第四修正案违例根本不存在。

❌ 概念混淆 | Miranda门槛误判

✕ C: 把普通 Terry stop 当成羁押讯问了。

❌ 事实误判 | 双重违例夸大

✕ D: 题干没有逮捕级别事实，别硬加 both。

这题建议用什么方法？

先判扣留层级，再看是否已经进入羁押；只要还在 Terry 阶段，先别急着套 Miranda。

考场速记

记住这句：Terry 先看合理怀疑，Miranda 先看羁押。外面只是短暂停、问几句，通常还没到必须读权利的阶段。

再加一句口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 这类口诀是处理中间上诉的；但本题不是上诉题，核心还是“Terry stop 不等于 custody”。

reason.zh: 根据第四修正案，合理怀疑支持警方进行最初的特里搜身和拦截。

A.text: neither a Fourth Amendment violation nor a Miranda violation

reason.zh: 正确指出特里拦截及后续提问并未违反第四或第五修正案。

B.text: fruit of a Fourth Amendment violation

reason.zh: 错误地认为拦截缺乏合理怀疑或超出了范围。

D.text: fruit of both a Fourth Amendment violation and a Miranda violation

reason.zh: 引发关于该提问是否属于羁押性审讯的第五修正案争点。

reason.zh: 确认提问处于简短的特里调查性拦截的范围内。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
A grand jury indicted a woman on a charge of arson, and a valid warrant was issued for her arrest. A police officer arrested the woman and informed her of what the warrant stated. However, hoping that the woman might say something incriminating, the officer did not give her Miranda warnings. He placed her in the back seat of his patrol car and was driving her to the police station when she said, "Look, I didn't mean to burn the building; it was an accident. I was just burning some papers in a wastebasket."
At the station, after being given Miranda warnings, the woman stated she wished to remain silent and made no other statements.
At trial, the woman moved to suppress the use of her statement to the police officer as evidence on two grounds: first, that the statement was acquired without giving Miranda warnings, and second, that the police officer had deliberately elicited her incriminating statement after she was indicted.
How should the court respond to the woman's motion to suppress?

choices.A: Deny the motion.
choices.B: Grant the motion only on the basis of the first ground stated.
choices.C: Grant the motion only on the basis of the second ground stated.
choices.D: Grant the motion on either ground.

questions.explanation:
Applicability of Fifth and Sixth Amendments
Woman
indicted
Woman arrested
(custody)
Volunteered
statement
Police
lineup
Police questioning
(interrogation)
Trial
No right/privilege applies
Sixth Amendment right to counsel
Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination

A court should suppress any statement taken in violation of a defendant's Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. This privilege is violated when police fail to give a suspect Miranda warnings before a custodial interrogation (suspect in custody and subjected to interrogation). Interrogation occurs when police use words or actions that they know or should know are reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response.

Here, the officer arrested the woman and placed her in his squad car (custody). As the officer was driving, the woman confessed that she accidentally started the fire. And though the officer had hoped that the woman would say something incriminating, he made no affirmative efforts to elicit her confession (no interrogation). Therefore, Miranda warnings were not required, and the court should reject the first ground of the woman's motion to suppress (Choices B & D).

A court should also suppress statements taken in violation of a defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel, which automatically attaches once judicial proceedings have commenced—eg, when the defendant is indicted. This right is violated when a defendant is denied access to an attorney during any critical stage of prosecution—including police interrogations.

Here, the woman's Sixth Amendment right to counsel attached when she was indicted for arson. But since she was not subjected to an interrogation when she confessed, her statement was not elicited during a critical stage of prosecution. As a result, she was not entitled to the assistance of counsel, and the court should also reject the second ground of her motion (Choices C & D).

📌 Educational Objective

Interrogation occurs when police use words or actions that they know or should know are reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response. Suspects must be Mirandized before a custodial interrogation and have the right to counsel if the interrogation occurs after judicial proceedings have commenced.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 478 (1966) (listing Miranda rights).
  • Rhode Island v. Innis, 446 U.S. 291, 308 (1980) (defining interrogation).
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to counsel).
  • Kuhlmann v. Wilson, 477 U.S. 436, 459 (1986) (explaining deliberate elicitation).
questions.zh-question:
一个大陪审团以纵火罪起诉了一名女子，并为逮捕她签发了有效的逮捕令。一名警官逮捕了该女子，并告知了她逮捕令的内容。然而，警官希望该女子能说出一些自证其罪的话，因此没有向她宣读 Miranda 警告。他将她安置在巡逻车的后座，在开车送她去警察局的途中，该女子说：“听着，我不是故意要烧那栋楼的；那是个意外。我只是在废纸篓里烧一些文件。”

在警察局，该女子在被告知 Miranda 警告后，表示她希望保持沉默，并且没有再做任何陈述。

在庭审中，该女子以两个理由动议排除其对警官所作的陈述作为证据：第一，该陈述是在未被告知 Miranda 警告的情况下获得的；第二，警官在她被起诉后，故意引诱她做出自证其罪的陈述。

法院应如何回应该女子的排除动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回该动议。
zh-choices.B: 仅基于陈述的第一个理由批准该动议。
zh-choices.C: 仅基于陈述的第二个理由批准该动议。
zh-choices.D: 基于任一理由批准该动议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：米兰达警告（Miranda warnings） 和 第六修正案律师权（Sixth Amendment right to counsel） 都要先看有没有真正的 讯问（interrogation）；只有被拘押还被警察用话术诱发供述时，才会触发排除。

三秒认题路径：

被捕拘押 → 有无讯问 → 是否诱供 → 米兰达 / 第六修正案 → 不能排除

核心法律规则

只看这条规则就够了

第五修正案特权（privilege against self-incrimination） 只在 拘押性讯问（custodial interrogation） 时要求先给 米兰达警告（Miranda warnings）；讯问（interrogation） 的意思是警察说的话或动作，客观上知道或应当知道会逼出自认其罪的回答。

如果只是嫌犯自己主动开口，没有警察的诱发性追问，就没有 interrogation，所以不会因为没读米兰达而排除。

第六修正案律师权（Sixth Amendment right to counsel） 在起诉、如 起诉书（indictment） 之后自动附着，但它也只管 关键阶段（critical stage）；没有被警察真正讯问时，这个权利不会因为被动听到嫌疑人自发供词就被触发。

核心判例： Rhode Island v. Innis — 这案子把 interrogation 定义成“警方知道或应当知道会引出自证其罪的问法或动作”，所以本题里警察只是没追问、不算诱供。

思维导图

先问：有没有 拘押性讯问（custodial interrogation）？
否： 只是 被捕上车，但警察没提问、没用动作诱发供述。
卡死点：没有 interrogation，米兰达不触发，排除不了。
再问： 诉讼是否已开始？（这里是 已起诉（indicted））
是： 第六修正案已附着。
但还要有 关键阶段讯问（critical-stage interrogation） 才会压到律师权；本题没有，所以照样不能排除。
结论： 自发供述可用，排除动议（motion to suppress） 应被驳回。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：人已经被抓、又已经被起诉，警察还故意想套话，所以应该一律排除。

但考试真正问的是：警察有没有做出会 引出供述（elicit a confession） 的 interrogation，不是他主观上“想不想套话”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干里警察只是把人带去警局，女人是自己在车里主动说出 accident，没有 讯问（interrogation），所以米兰达和第六修正案这两条都压不住这句供词。

❌ 概念混淆 | 米兰达误套

✕ B: 只抓住 custody，却漏掉还得先有讯问。

❌ 法律适用 | 第六权利误判

✕ C: 把 indicted 当成自动排除，忽略还要有关键阶段讯问。

❌ 事实误判 | 诱供细节偷换

✕ D: 看到警察 hoped 套话，就把主观意图当成了实际讯问。

这题建议用什么方法？

先卡住“有没有讯问”，再分别检查第五修正案和第六修正案，别被“已经被捕/已经起诉”带偏。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先看拘押，再看讯问；先有起诉，再看关键阶段。只要警察没有做出会逼出口供的 interrogation，供词通常能用。

reason.en: Triggers the attachment of the Sixth Amendment right to counsel.

reason.en: Shows the officer had subjective intent, but did not perform any objective interrogation.
reason.zh: 表明警员有主观意图，但在客观上并未进行任何讯问。

highlights.text: she said, "Look, I didn't mean to burn the building; it was an accident. I was just burning some papers in a wastebasket."

reason.en: Confirms the statement was volunteered spontaneously rather than elicited by police interrogation.
reason.zh: 确认陈述是自发作出的，而不是被警察讯问所套出的。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A wife was the prime suspect in the murder of her husband. The wife had called 911 and reported that her husband had discovered an intruder breaking into their home in the middle of the night, the husband had fought with the intruder, and the intruder had shot the husband. However, the police could find no evidence of a break-in or defensive wounds on the husband. As a result, a detective brought the wife to an interrogation room at the police station and questioned her for a number of hours. The interrogation was recorded. After claiming that she had not murdered her husband, the wife, who never received any Miranda warnings, finally voluntarily admitted that she had shot her husband. The wife was then charged with murder.
At trial, the wife took the stand and denied shooting her husband. In order to impeach the wife's credibility, the prosecution now seeks to introduce her previous statement made to the detective admitting that she had shot her husband. The wife's attorney has objected.
Is the wife's previous statement admissible?

choices.A: No, because the statement was made after the wife had been questioned for hours.
choices.B: No, because the statement was taken in violation of the wife's Miranda rights.
choices.C: Yes, because the statement was recorded.
choices.D: Yes, because the statement was voluntary.

questions.explanation:
Custodial interrogation
(Miranda warnings required)

Suspect in custody?

  • formal arrest
  • movement restricted
No
Not
required
Yes

Suspect interrogated?

  • police words/actions likely to
    elicit incriminating response
No
Not
required
Required

To comply with the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination, police must give suspects Miranda warnings before a custodial interrogation. Statements taken without the issuance of Miranda warnings cannot be used directly in deciding ultimate issues of guilt or innocence. However, such statements can be used for the limited purpose of impeaching the criminal defendant's inconsistent testimony if they were voluntary and trustworthy.*

Here, the wife's previous statement—that she shot her husband—contradicts her present testimony denying that she did so. The wife voluntarily gave the statement, and there is no indication that the statement was coerced or otherwise untrustworthy. Therefore, the wife's previous statement is admissible to impeach her credibility even though the statement was taken in violation of her Miranda rights (Choice B).

*This ensures that the government's use of unlawfully obtained evidence remains limited, while also preventing the defendant from using the government's mistake as a shield against untruthful testimony.

(Choice A) Although the wife had been questioned for a number of hours, there is no indication that she was exhausted or that her statement about shooting her husband was coerced.

(Choice B) The fact that the wife's statement was recorded has no bearing on its admissibility and therefore is not relevant to the analysis at hand.

📌 Educational Objective

Statements taken in violation of Miranda cannot be used directly in deciding ultimate issues of guilt or innocence. However, such a statement can be used for the limited purpose of impeaching the criminal defendant's inconsistent testimony if the statement was voluntary and trustworthy.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Harris v. New York, 401 U.S. 222, 224–25 (1971) (discussing the use of statements taken in violation of Miranda for impeachment purposes).
  • Miranda v. Arizona, 384 U.S. 436, 468–70 (1966) (listing Miranda warnings).

一名妻子是其丈夫谋杀案的主要嫌疑人。该妻子曾拨打911报警，称其丈夫在半夜发现一名闯入者闯入家中，丈夫与闯入者搏斗，闯入者开枪射杀了丈夫。然而，警方未能在丈夫身上发现任何强行闯入的证据或防御性伤口。因此，一名警探将该妻子带到警察局的审讯室，并对她进行了数小时的讯问。审讯过程被录音录像。在声称自己没有谋杀丈夫后，从未收到任何Miranda警告的妻子最终自愿承认是她开枪射杀了丈夫。该妻子随后被控犯有谋杀罪。

在庭审中，该妻子出庭作证，否认开枪射杀其丈夫。为了弹劾该妻子的可信度，控方现在试图引入她先前向警探作出的承认开枪射杀丈夫的陈述。该妻子的律师提出了反对。

该妻子先前的陈述是否具有可采性？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该陈述是在妻子被讯问数小时后作出的。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为获取该陈述违反了妻子的Miranda权利。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为该陈述被录音录像。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该陈述是自愿作出的。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - The Privilege Against Compulsory Self-Incrimination

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：米兰达警告（Miranda warnings） 被违反后，自愿且可信（voluntary and trustworthy） 的供述能不能拿来弹劾被告自己出庭时的相反说法。

三秒认题路径：

羁押盘问 → 无警告 → 供述自愿 → 被告反口 → 先弹劾后说

核心法律规则

一眼就能用的规则

羁押性讯问（custodial interrogation） 里，警察先给 米兰达警告（Miranda warnings），否则该供述一般不能直接拿来证明有罪。可是一旦被告自己上庭说了相反版本，检方仍可用这份未警告供述来弹劾，只要它是 自愿（voluntary） 且 可信（trustworthy） 的。

考场意思：这不是在问“能不能定罪用”，而是在问“能不能拿来拆被告自己的说法”。

核心判例： Harris v. New York - 未给 Miranda 的陈述通常不能直接定罪，但若自愿可信，可以用来弹劾被告的相反证词。

思维导图

先看：这份陈述是“直接定罪用”，还是“拿来弹劾”用？
1是否为 羁押性讯问（custodial interrogation）？本题是，嫌疑人被带去警局问了几个小时。
有无 米兰达警告（Miranda warnings）？
NO → 不能直接拿去证明有罪。
但被告自己上庭后是否说了相反版本？
YES → 进入弹劾用途审查。
卡死点：只要陈述是 voluntary and trustworthy，就能用来打脸被告；“问了很久” 本身不等于强迫。
结论：选 D，因为自愿供述可用于弹劾。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：问了好几个小时，还没给 Miranda，所以这份口供应该完全不能用。

但考试真正问的是：它能不能用来 弹劾（impeach） 被告的相反证词，而不是能不能直接当主证据定罪。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的关键事实是：她是 自愿承认自己开枪，且后来在法庭上当场翻供，所以这份未给 Miranda 的陈述可用来弹劾。

❌ 事实误判 | 时长夸大

✕ A: 只盯着 questioned for hours，忽略了题干没说她被逼供。

❌ 法律适用 | 用途混淆

✕ B: 把 Miranda rights 违反直接等同于“任何用途都不能用”。

❌ 概念混淆 | 录音无关化

✕ C: 看到 recorded 就以为录音能补救，题干根本没给这个效果。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“定罪用”还是“弹劾用”，再问陈述是不是自愿可信。

考场速记

记住一句：没给 Miranda 不等于 完全作废；被告自己上庭反说时，自愿且可信 的旧口供还能回头打他脸。

速记：Harris 口诀就是“先看能不能弹劾，再看能不能定罪”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was charged with armed robbery. The defendant had only an eighth-grade education and no legal knowledge.
At a pretrial hearing, the defendant told the judge that he was unhappy with the public defender who had been appointed to represent him and that he wanted the judge to appoint another lawyer. The judge refused to appoint another lawyer, telling the defendant, with no further explanation, that his only other choice was to represent himself. The defendant said that he would represent himself at trial then, as "anything [was] better than having this lawyer."
The defendant did not raise the subject again, and he represented himself at trial. After hearing overwhelming evidence of the defendant's guilt, the jury convicted him of armed robbery. On appeal, the defendant has requested a new trial on the ground that he was deprived of his right to counsel.
Should the appellate court grant the defendant's request?

choices.A: No, because the defendant voluntarily waived his right to counsel.
choices.B: No, because the trial court's error was harmless in light of the overwhelming evidence.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant was not capable of effectively representing himself.
choices.D: Yes, because the record does not establish a valid waiver of the right to counsel.

questions.explanation:
Waiver of Sixth Amendment right to counsel
Knowing
  • Aware of right to counsel
Intelligent
  • Understands nature of charges
  • Knows range of punishment
  • Recognizes disadvantages of self-representation
Voluntary
  • Waiver is given freely
  • Not choosing self-representation over incompetent counsel

In Faretta v. California, the Supreme Court held that a criminal defendant may only waive his/her Sixth Amendment right to counsel and engage in self-representation if the waiver is made knowingly, intelligently, and voluntarily. To ensure that this standard is met, a judge must confirm on the record that the defendant is both:

  • aware of the nature of the charges, the range of punishment, and the disadvantages of self-representation and
  • not being forced to choose between incompetent counsel and self-representation.

Here, the defendant told the judge he was unhappy with his public defender and wanted another lawyer. The judge then forced the defendant to keep his current counsel or represent himself. Therefore, the defendant's waiver and subsequent trial were invalid, and a new trial should be granted.

(Choice A) The defendant did not voluntarily waive his right to counsel since the judge forced the defendant to choose between his existing counsel and self-representation.

(Choice B) Most trial court errors are reviewed on appeal for harmless error—ie, whether the error was so damaging that it caused an incorrect judgment. But structural errors (eg, deprivation of the right to counsel) are never harmless since they affect the entire framework of a trial and render it fundamentally unfair. Therefore, they require automatic reversal on appeal.

(Choice C) The defendant likely was not capable of effectively representing himself since he has an eighth-grade education and no legal knowledge. But a defendant has the right to engage in self-representation even if he/she cannot do so effectively, so this is not a basis for granting a new trial.

📌 Educational Objective

A defendant can only waive his/her Sixth Amendment right to counsel and engage in self-representation if the trial court confirms that the defendant (1) knows the nature of the charges, range of punishment, and disadvantages of self-representation and (2) is not being forced to choose between incompetent counsel and self-representation.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to assistance of counsel).
  • Faretta v. California, 422 U.S. 806, 834–35 (1975) (holding that right to self-representation is implicit in the Sixth Amendment but waiver of counsel must be knowing, intelligent and voluntary).
  • Johnson v. Zerbst, 304 U.S. 458, 465 (1938) ("[The Sixth Amendment] imposes the serious and weighty responsibility upon the trial judge of determining whether there is an intelligent and competent waiver by the accused").
questions.zh-question:
一名被告被指控犯有持械抢劫罪。该被告仅有八年级教育水平，且不具备任何法律知识。

在一次审前听证会上，被告告诉法官，他对被指派为他辩护的公设辩护人不满意，并希望法官另行指派一名律师。法官拒绝另行指派律师，并在没有进一步解释的情况下告诉被告，他唯一的其他选择就是自我辩护。被告于是说他将在审判中自我辩护，因为“任何事都比让这位律师代理要好”。

被告没有再提起此事，并在审判中进行了自我辩护。在听取了证明被告有罪的压倒性证据后，陪审团裁定他犯有持械抢劫罪。在上诉中，被告以其辩护权被剥夺为由请求重新审判。

上诉法院应否批准被告的请求？

zh-choices.A: 不应批准，因为被告自愿放弃了他的辩护权。
zh-choices.B: 不应批准，因为鉴于存在压倒性证据，初审法院的错误是无害的。
zh-choices.C: 应该批准，因为被告没有能力进行有效的自我辩护。
zh-choices.D: 应该批准，因为案卷记录未能证实被告有效放弃了辩护权。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Right to counsel

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告想放弃第六修正案律师权（Sixth Amendment right to counsel）时，记录里有没有证明这次放弃是知情、明智、出于自愿（knowing, intelligent, and voluntary）。

三秒认题路径：

想换律师 → 被逼二选一 → 自己上庭 → 记录不全 → 放弃无效

核心法律规则

被告有自我辩护权（self-representation），但前提是他真的完成了对律师权（right to counsel）的有效放弃。考场上要看三件事：知道自己有这项权利，知道指控、可能刑罚和自己上庭的坏处，而且不是被迫在无能律师（incompetent counsel）和自己上庭之间硬选。

只要法官没有把这些内容在记录里确认清楚，这个 waiver 就不成立，后面的自我辩护也救不回来。Faretta v. California 和 Johnson v. Zerbst 都锁定这一点：不是“他会不会打官司”，而是“他有没有真的、自由地放弃律师”。

核心判例： Faretta v. California - 只有在知情、明智、自愿的前提下，才可以放弃律师权并自己辩护。

思维导图

先问：被告有没有有效放弃律师权？
1.是否知道有权找律师？
题干里：被告知道自己不满意公设辩护人，但记录没有法官确认他理解放弃后果。
2.是否知道指控、刑罚、自己上庭的坏处？
题干里：只说“想换律师”，没有说明法官告知了指控范围、刑罚范围和自辩风险。
3.是否是自由选择？
卡死点：法官让他在“继续用这个律师”和“自己上庭”之间二选一，not voluntary。
结论：放弃无效 → 右侧答案选 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他教育程度低、又没法律知识，肯定自己辩护很吃亏，所以应选能看出“他不适合自辩”的选项。

但考试真正问的是：法官有没有确认这次放弃真的成立；不是他打得好不好，而是他有没有合法放弃律师权。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干最关键的 法官没有在记录中确认知情、自愿放弃，而是直接逼他在旧律师和自辩之间二选一，所以 waiver 无效。

❌ 概念混淆 | 自辩标准误判

✕ A: 把“不想用这个律师”偷换成有效放弃。

❌ 法律适用 | 无害错误误判

✕ B: 律师权缺失属结构性错误，不能靠 harmless 兜住。

❌ 事实误判 | 自辩能力偷换

✕ C: 把“不会打官司”当成能否自辩的门槛。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看记录里有没有有效 waiver，再看法官有没有把被告逼进“律师 or 自辩”的错误二选一。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先看记录，后看选择；知情、明智、自愿，少一个都不行。 这类题先抓 waiver 是否成立，不要被被告学历低、法官偏不偏、案子证据强不强带跑。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
After a defendant was indicted on federal bank fraud charges and released on bail, his attorney filed notice of the defendant's intent to offer an insanity defense. The prosecutor then enlisted the help of a forensic psychologist who was willing to participate in an "undercover" mental examination of the defendant. The psychologist contacted the defendant and pretended to represent an executive personnel agency. She told the defendant about an attractive employment opportunity and invited him to a "preliminary screening interview" to determine his qualifications for the job. As part of the purported screening process, the psychologist gave the defendant psychological tests that enabled her to form a reliable opinion about his mental state at the time of the alleged offense.
What is the strongest basis for a defense objection to the psychologist's testimony regarding the defendant's mental state?

choices.A: The federal common law privilege for confidential communications between psychotherapist and patient.
choices.B: The Fourth Amendment prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures.
choices.C: The Fifth Amendment privilege against compelled self-incrimination.
choices.D: The Sixth Amendment right to the assistance of counsel.

6th Amendment right to counsel
5th Amendment privilege against self-incrimination

A court should sustain a defendant's objection to testimony based on evidence obtained in violation of his/her constitutional rights, including the Sixth Amendment right to counsel. This right:

  • automatically attaches once judicial proceedings commence (eg, filing of formal charges, indictment)
    and
  • guarantees a criminal defendant assistance of counsel at all critical stages of prosecution—any event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial.

An interrogation is a critical stage of prosecution because the government (eg, prosecutor, undercover government informant) engages in conduct that is reasonably likely to elicit an incriminating response that can be used against the defendant at trial. Therefore, a defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel is violated when the government interrogates him/her post-indictment without counsel present.

Here, the defendant's right to counsel automatically attached once he was indicted (judicial proceedings commenced). The prosecutor then enlisted the forensic psychologist to interrogate the defendant by conducting an "undercover" examination of his mental state at the time of the alleged offense (critical stage). And since the defendant did not have access to counsel during that interrogation, the strongest basis for an objection is that the psychologist's testimony is based on evidence obtained in violation of his Sixth Amendment right to counsel.

(Choice A) Under the federal psychotherapist-patient privilege, a patient can prevent the disclosure of confidential communications with his/her psychotherapist that were made for the purpose of diagnosis or treatment. But this privilege does not apply here since the defendant spoke with the undercover psychologist for a preliminary employment screening—not for diagnosis or treatment.

(Choice B) The Fourth Amendment is inapplicable since no Fourth Amendment search occurred: (1) the defendant had no reasonable expectation of privacy in the information he freely disclosed to the psychologist and (2) the psychologist did not invade a constitutionally protected area. And no Fourth Amendment seizure occurred since the psychologist did not confiscate the defendant's property or restrict his freedom of movement.

(Choice C) The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination applies when a suspect is compelled to make a self-incriminating statement while he/she is in custody or testifying in court. This privilege does not apply here since the psychologist questioned the defendant while he was released on bail (not in custody) and outside the courtroom (not testifying in court).

📌 Educational Objective

The Sixth Amendment right to counsel automatically attaches once judicial proceedings commence and requires the presence of counsel during all critical stages of prosecution—including interrogations conducted by undercover government agents.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to counsel).
  • Massiah v. United States, 377 U.S. 201, 206 (1964) (holding that deliberately eliciting statements from defendant in the absence of counsel violates defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel).

一名被告因联邦银行欺诈罪名被起诉并获得保释后，其律师提交了被告意图提出精神错乱抗辩的通知。随后，检察官寻求了一位法医心理学家的帮助，该心理学家愿意对被告进行一次“卧底”精神状况检查。该心理学家联系了被告，并伪装自己代表一家高管人事代理机构。她告诉被告有一个颇具吸引力的工作机会，并邀请他参加“初步筛选面试”，以确定其工作资格。作为所谓的筛选过程的一部分，该心理学家对被告进行了心理测试，这使她能够对被告在被指控的罪行发生时的精神状态形成可靠的意见。

辩方反对该心理学家就其对被告精神状态的证词，最有力的依据是什么？

zh-choices.A: 联邦普通法上关于心理治疗师与患者之间保密通信的特免权。
zh-choices.B: Fourth Amendment 禁止不合理搜查和扣押的规定。
zh-choices.C: Fifth Amendment 反对强迫自证其罪的特免权。
zh-choices.D: Sixth Amendment 获得律师协助的权利。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Right to counsel

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：正式起诉后（post-indictment），政府用“假身份”去套话，是否侵犯了第六修正案的律师帮助权（right to counsel）。

三秒认题路径：

已起诉 → 假身份问话 → 关键阶段 → 没律师在场 → 选第六修正案

核心法律规则

抓住这条线就够了

第六修正案律师帮助权（Sixth Amendment right to counsel）一旦司法程序启动就自动附着，最典型的起点就是正式指控或起诉书（indictment）。

只要进入关键阶段（critical stage），政府就不能在没有律师在场时去故意引出陈述（deliberately elicit statements）；考试上这句话的意思就是：这类供述不能拿来打你。

本题里，检察官让心理学家假扮招聘人员去做“筛查”，本质上是在起诉后对被告做秘密问讯，所以最强异议就是证据来自违反第六修正案的取证。

核心判例： Massiah v. United States — 起诉后在律师不在场时故意套话，得到的陈述通常不能用于控诉被告。

思维导图

先看：是不是已经进入刑事司法程序？
是已被起诉（indicted）后，律师帮助权自动附着。
再看：政府是不是在“秘密套话”式问讯？
是假扮招聘筛查，实质是对被告做讯问（interrogation）。
再看：这是不是关键阶段？
是会影响辩护、会被拿去当庭使用，属于critical stage。
卡死点：没有律师在场 + 故意引出陈述 → 第六修正案被违反
结论
答心理学家证言的最强攻击点 = D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这是“心理治疗谈话”，所以先想到psychotherapist-patient privilege，或者觉得被告没被关押就不算数。

但考试真正问的是：政府能不能在起诉后、律师不在场时，用假身份去套出能上庭用的内容。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「被告有没有真的被吓到」或「信息有没有看起来像就业筛查」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的关键点是：已经被起诉后，政府又用假招聘面试去问精神状态，这就是第六修正案的关键阶段套话。

❌ 概念混淆 | 特权场景错认

✕ A: 把diagnosis or treatment看错了，这里不是治疗关系。

❌ 事实误判 | 搜查概念偷换

✕ B: 把freely disclosed当成搜查对象，方向错了。

❌ 法律适用 | 供述场景错套

✕ C: 看到custody就硬套第五修正案，但这题不是羁押讯问。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓程序节点，再看政府是否故意引出陈述；只要已起诉且无律师在场，先想到第六修正案。

考场速记

再记一句：indictment 后先问第六修正案，deliberately elicit 一出现，就别被“不是拘押”带跑。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
An indigent defendant was tried for misdemeanor assault. The defendant did not request that a lawyer be appointed to represent him, and the court did not appoint one. The crime carries a maximum punishment of one year in prison and a $2,000 fine. The defendant was found guilty, and the court imposed a fine on him.
Has the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel been violated?

choices.A: No, because the defendant did not request a lawyer.
choices.B: No, because the defendant was not sentenced to incarceration.
choices.C: Yes, because the defendant was charged with a misdemeanor.
choices.D: Yes, because the defendant was indigent.

questions.explanation:
The Sixth Amendment right to counsel applies in any case (felony or misdemeanor) in which a defendant has been sentenced to incarceration—even if that sentence has been suspended (Choice C). This means that in any case in which only a fine is imposed, the Sixth Amendment right to counsel does not apply and thus cannot be violated.

Here, the defendant was tried for misdemeanor assault—which carries a maximum punishment of one year in prison and a $2,000 fine—without being represented by an attorney. Although the defendant could have been sentenced to incarceration, the court imposed only a fine. Therefore, the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel was not implicated or violated.*

*Note that the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel would have been violated had the defendant been sentenced to incarceration because there is no indication that this right was waived.

(Choice A) Unlike the Fifth Amendment right to counsel, a defendant need not invoke the Sixth Amendment right to counsel by requesting a lawyer. Instead, the Sixth Amendment right to counsel automatically attaches when formal judicial proceedings begin and applies at all critical stages of prosecution.

(Choice D) Indigent defendants are entitled to the appointment of counsel only when the Sixth Amendment right to counsel exists. Here, this right did not exist because the defendant was merely fined.

📌 Educational Objective

The Sixth Amendment provides the right to counsel in any case in which a defendant has been sentenced to incarceration—even if that sentence has been suspended. However, this right does not apply in cases in which only a fine is imposed.

📚 References
  • Scott v. Illinois, 440 U.S. 367, 373–74 (1979) (holding that the Sixth Amendment right to counsel applies only in cases in which the court imposes a sentence of incarceration, even if the sentence is suspended).

被告的第六修正案律师权（Sixth Amendment right to counsel）是否受到了侵犯？

zh-choices.B: 否，因为被告未被判处监禁（incarceration）。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为被告被控轻罪（misdemeanor）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为被告是贫困的（indigent）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Right to counsel

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第六修正案的 律师帮助权（right to counsel） 只有在法院实际判了监禁时才会被触发；只罚款，不算侵犯。

三秒认题路径：

没请律师 → 只罚款 → 没判监禁 → 权利未触发 → 选 B

核心法律规则

考场上直接背这句

第六修正案律师帮助权（Sixth Amendment right to counsel） 会在正式刑事程序开始后自动出现，考场意思：不用先开口要律师。监禁（incarceration） 才是触发点，考场意思：法院真的判了你坐牢，哪怕是缓刑监禁，也要有律师。

如果最后只判 罚金（fine），考场意思：这案子没有触发第六修正案律师权，所以也谈不上“被侵犯”。

核心判例： Scott v. Illinois —— 只有在法院实际判处监禁时，才有第六修正案律师帮助权。

思维导图

先问：这案子是不是“只罚款”还是“判了监禁”？
Step 1如果法院实际判了 监禁（incarceration），即使缓刑，也会触发第六修正案律师权。
Step 2如果只是 罚金（fine），就直接卡死：律师权根本没启动。
本题卡点：没有监禁，只有罚金，所以不能说 Sixth Amendment 被违反。
结论题目虽然写了 indigent，但穷不穷不是第一关；先看有没有监禁，再决定要不要 appoint counsel。
答案因此选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想： 被告是 indigent，而且又没律师，听起来应该违反第六修正案。

但考试真正问的是： 不是“有没有贫穷、有没有律师”本身，而是“法院最后有没有判监禁”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这题同样是看 法律后果（legal consequence），不是看题干故事有多不公平。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干只判了 罚金，没有 监禁（incarceration），所以第六修正案律师权根本没被触发。

❌ 概念混淆 | 先要申请误判

✕ A: 以为没提 request a lawyer 就输，但第六修正案不是先申请才生效。

❌ 法律适用 | 罪名宽泛误判

✕ C: 把“被控轻罪”当成自动触发点，忽略了真正关键是最后判了什么。

❌ 事实误判 | 贫困即权利误判

✕ D: 看到 indigent 就直接联想到 appointed counsel，但贫困本身不会单独启动第六修正案。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看最终刑罚：只罚款就直接排除，第六修正案律师权没有被触发。

考场速记

记忆口诀：“先看有没有监禁，只有罚金就没有 Sixth Amendment counsel。”

补一刀：律师帮助权（right to counsel） 看的是法院有没有判 incarceration，不是被告有没有穷、有没有开口要。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant, a 14-year-old male, was tried as an adult for an armed robbery and was convicted. No one had been physically harmed during the robbery. In light of the defendant's lengthy juvenile criminal history, which included violent offenses, and the fact that armed robbery is a crime of violence, he was sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole.
Did the life-without-parole sentence violate the Eighth Amendment ban on cruel and unusual punishment?

choices.A: No, because a juvenile may be sentenced to life without parole if release would pose a danger to the community.
choices.B: No, because the Eighth Amendment does not apply outside the context of capital punishment.
choices.C: Yes, because a life-without-parole sentence is not permissible for a juvenile defendant convicted of a nonhomicide offense.
choices.D: Yes, because a life-without-parole sentence is not permissible for an adult or juvenile defendant convicted of a nonviolent offense.

questions.explanation:
Eighth Amendment cruel & unusual punishment
  • No death penalty for:
    • juveniles
    • intellectually deficient persons
    • adults convicted of nonhomicide offenses
  • No life-without-parole for juveniles convicted of nonhomicide offenses
  • No mandatory life-without-parole for juveniles convicted of homicide

The Eighth Amendment prohibits cruel and unusual punishments—punishments that are inherently barbaric (eg, torture) and those that are disproportionate to the crime. A punishment is disproportionate if:

  • the sentence imposed grossly exceeds the nature of the crime (eg, defendant sentenced to life in prison for shoplifting) or
  • the punishment violates a categorical rule based on the defendant's characteristics (eg, a juvenile) and/or the nature of the crime (eg, a nonhomicide offense).

Therefore, if the defendant was a juvenile (under the age of 18) when the crime was committed, the Eighth Amendment prohibits the imposition of: (1) the death penalty, (2) mandatory life without parole for any offense, and (3) life without parole for nonhomicide offenses.

Here, the 14-year-old defendant (juvenile) was convicted of armed robbery (nonhomicide offense) and sentenced to life in prison without the possibility of parole. Therefore, this sentence violated the Eighth Amendment's ban on cruel and unusual punishment.

(Choice A) Due to their age, juveniles convicted of nonhomicide offenses cannot be sentenced to life without parole for any reason. Therefore, the defendant's sentence violated the Eighth Amendment even if his release from prison would pose a danger to the community.

(Choice B) The Eighth Amendment applies to capital punishment (death penalty)—eg, juveniles cannot be sentenced to death. However, it also applies to noncapital punishment (non-death penalty)—eg, juveniles cannot be sentenced to life without parole for nonhomicide offenses.

(Choice D) Although a juvenile cannot be sentenced to life without parole for a nonviolent offense, an adult can (though most courts would likely consider it excessive).

📌 Educational Objective

The Eighth Amendment's prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment forbids imposing a sentence of life in prison without the possibility of parole on a juvenile defendant convicted of a nonhomicide offense.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VIII (prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment).
  • Graham v. Florida, 560 U.S. 48, 74 (2010) (recognizing that juveniles cannot be sentenced to life without parole for nonhomicide offenses).
questions.zh-question:
一名14岁的男性被告因持械抢劫罪作为成年人受审并被定罪。抢劫过程中无人受到身体伤害。鉴于该被告有包括暴力犯罪在内的长期未成年人犯罪史，且持械抢劫属于暴力犯罪，他被判处不得假释的无期徒刑。

这项不得假释的无期徒刑判决是否违反了第八修正案禁止残酷和不寻常惩罚的规定？

zh-choices.A: 不违反，因为如果释放未成年人会对社区构成危险，则可以判处其不得假释的无期徒刑。
zh-choices.B: 不违反，因为第八修正案不适用于死刑之外的情形。
zh-choices.C: 是的，因为对于因非杀人罪被定罪的未成年被告，不得判处不得假释的无期徒刑。
zh-choices.D: 是的，因为对于因非暴力犯罪被定罪的成年或未成年被告，不得判处不得假释的无期徒刑。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Cruel and Unusual Punishment

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：未成年人（juvenile）因非杀人罪（nonhomicide offense）被判无期不得假释（life without parole）时，第八修正案（Eighth Amendment）是否直接禁止。

三秒认题路径：

14岁 → 少年犯 → 非杀人罪 → LWOP → 直接违宪

核心法律规则

残酷且异常惩罚（cruel and unusual punishment）不只是死刑问题；它也管非死刑刑罚。对 未成年人（juvenile），考试上最重要的线是：非杀人罪（nonhomicide offense）不能判 无期不得假释（life without parole）。

这里的关键不是被告“会不会很危险”，而是法院能不能直接给这种少年犯下这么重的终局刑。Graham v. Florida 把这条线锁死了：少年非杀人案，LWOP 通常不行。

核心判例： Graham v. Florida - 少年犯因非杀人罪被判无期不得假释，属于第八修正案禁止的过重惩罚。

思维导图

先看刑罚是不是可立即被第八修正案拦下？
1. 被告是 14岁未成年人（juvenile），不是普通成人。
2. 罪名是 armed robbery，但它属于 非杀人罪（nonhomicide offense）。
3. 题干给的是 无期不得假释（life without parole），正撞上 Graham 规则。
卡死点：不是“危险不危险”，而是“少年 + 非杀人罪 + LWOP”这一组合本身就禁。
结论： 这道题应选 C，因为这种量刑对少年非杀人犯通常违宪。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他有暴力前科、又是 armed robbery，法官是不是就能觉得“放出去很危险”，所以 LWOP 可以。

但考试真正问的是：司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。 这里同理，关键不是“危险感”，而是第八修正案对少年非杀人罪 LWOP 的硬性限制。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干的 14岁少年 + nonhomicide offense + life without parole 正中 Graham 规则，所以这项量刑违宪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 危险性当豁免

✕ A: 把“放出去危险”当成少年 LWOP 的通行证，但 danger to the community 不能推翻这条硬规则。

❌ 法律适用 | 误当只管死刑

✕ B: 以为第八修正案只管死刑，忽略它也管 noncapital punishment。

❌ 事实误判 | 偷换非暴力

✕ D: 把题干的 armed robbery 偷换成非暴力犯罪，事实就走偏了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓年龄，再看是否杀人，再一眼锁定有没有直接撞上少年 LWOP 禁区。

考场速记

记住这句：少年 + 非杀人罪 + 无期不得假释，先想到 Graham v. Florida，结论通常就是违宪。

速记法：“少年非杀人，LWOP 先别判；能判死刑的门槛更高，非死刑也会被第八修正案拦下。”

questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
A marijuana farmer had been missing for several months. The sheriff's department received an anonymous tip that a woman, the farmer's business rival, had buried the farmer in a hillside about 200 yards from the woman's farmhouse. Sheriff's deputies went to the woman's farm. They cut the barbed wire that surrounded the hillside and entered, looking for the grave. They also searched the adjacent fields on the woman's farm that were within the area enclosed by the barbed wire and discovered clothing that belonged to the farmer hanging on a scarecrow.
The woman observed their discovery and began shooting. The deputies returned the fire. The woman dashed to her pickup truck to escape. Unable to start the truck, she fled across a field toward the barn. A deputy tackled her just as she entered the barn. As the woman attempted to get up, the deputy pinned her arms behind her back. Another deputy threatened, "Tell us what you did with the farmer or we will shut you down and see your family on relief." The woman responded that she had killed the farmer in a fight but did not report the incident because she did not want authorities to enter her land and discover her marijuana crop. Instead, she buried the farmer behind the barn. The woman was thereafter charged with murder.
If the woman moves to suppress her admission about killing the farmer, how will the court likely rule on her motion?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the deputy was in hot pursuit when he questioned the woman.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because the woman was questioned during an emergency police search.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the statement was the product of the warrantless entry and search of the woman's farm.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the woman did not voluntarily waive her right to silence.
