questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was indicted and arrested for bank robbery. The defendant had an initial appearance before a magistrate judge in which he was notified of the charges and told that counsel would be appointed for him the next day. The police then required the defendant to participate with other prisoners in a lineup in which each person had to wear a white T-shirt and say, "Put your hands in the air." At the lineup, witnesses to the bank robbery identified the defendant as the bank robber. The next day, counsel was provided and the defendant was arraigned on the charges.
The defendant argues that his Sixth Amendment right to counsel was violated when he was denied counsel at two critical stages of the proceeding: his initial appearance in court before the magistrate judge and the lineup identification.
Was the defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel violated?

choices.A: No.
choices.B: Yes, based only on the denial of counsel at the initial appearance.
choices.C: Yes, based only on the denial of counsel at the lineup.
choices.D: Yes, based on the denial of counsel at both stages of the proceeding.

questions.explanation:
Sixth Amendment right to counsel

(critical stages after prosecution has commenced)

  • Interrogations & lineups
  • Preliminary hearings & arraignments
  • Plea negotiations & hearings
  • Trial & sentencing
  • Appeals

The Sixth Amendment right to counsel:

• automatically attaches once judicial proceedings commence (eg, indictment, filing of formal charges, preliminary hearing, arraignment) and

• guarantees that criminal defendants will have the assistance of counsel during all critical stages of prosecution—any event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial.

An indictment is a judicial proceeding that triggers a defendant's Sixth Amendment right to counsel. And a post-indictment lineup is a critical stage of prosecution because suggestive lineup procedures can lead to an unreliable and prejudicial identification. Since an attorney would have helped to ensure that the lineup was conducted fairly and protected the defendant's right to a fair trial, the denial of counsel violated his Sixth Amendment right.

In contrast, an initial appearance is not a critical stage if the judge merely conducts administrative tasks like notifying the defendant of the charges and explaining that an attorney will be appointed the next day. As a result, the defendant did not have a Sixth Amendment right to counsel during his initial appearance (Choices A, B & D). But had the defendant been required to make decisions that might adversely affect the outcome of his trial (eg, deciding whether to enter an affirmative defense), then his initial appearance would have been a critical stage.

📌 Educational Objective

The Sixth Amendment right to counsel automatically attaches once judicial proceedings begin and applies to all critical stages of prosecution. A critical stage is any event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to assistance of counsel).
  • Rothgery v. Gillespie County, 554 U.S. 191, 198 (2008) (explaining that right to counsel attaches at commencement of judicial proceedings).
  • United States v. Wade, 388 U.S. 218, 237 (1967) (recognizing that post-indictment lineup is a critical stage of prosecution).
questions.zh-question:
一名被告因银行抢劫被起诉并逮捕。该被告在治安法官面前进行了首次出庭，在庭上他被告知了所控罪名，并被告知第二天将为他指定律师。随后，警方要求该被告与其他囚犯一起参加一个列队指认程序，其中每个人都必须穿白色T恤并说：“把手举起来。”在列队指认中，银行抢劫案的目击者指认该被告为银行劫匪。第二天，律师被提供给了被告，被告就这些指控被传讯。

被告辩称，由于他在两个关键诉讼阶段被拒绝提供律师，即在治安法官面前的首次出庭和列队指认，其第六修正案的律师权受到了侵犯。

被告的第六修正案律师权是否受到了侵犯？

zh-choices.A: 没有。
zh-choices.B: 是，但仅基于在首次出庭时被拒绝提供律师。
zh-choices.C: 是，但仅基于在列队指认时被拒绝提供律师。
zh-choices.D: 是，基于在这两个诉讼阶段均被拒绝提供律师。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Right to counsel

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第六修正案（Sixth Amendment）右到律师何时开始生效，以及“初次出庭”和“列队辨认”里，哪一个才算 critical stage（关键阶段）。

三秒认题路径：

已起诉 → 看是否关键阶段 → 初次出庭多半不是 → 列队辨认通常是 → 只选 C

核心法律规则

只抓住这条就够了

第六修正案右到律师（Sixth Amendment right to counsel）会在司法程序正式开始时自动启动，像 indictment（起诉书）、正式指控、arraignment（传讯/提审） 这种节点都算起点。

启动以后，不是每个场合都要律师，只有 critical stage（关键阶段） 才需要；考场意思：如果没律师会让被告在认罪、辨认、抗辩等事情上吃亏，就要有律师。

post-indictment lineup（起诉后列队辨认） 是经典关键阶段，因为辨认一旦被带偏，后面很难补救。

核心判例： United States v. Wade - 起诉后的列队辨认属于关键阶段，所以被告有权有律师在场；Rothgery v. Gillespie County - 司法程序一开始，右到律师就启动。

思维导图

先问：司法程序开始了吗？（indictment / formal charge / arraignment）
YES右到律师已启动 → 再问这一步是不是 critical stage（关键阶段）
是起诉后列队辨认 → 律师必须在场 → 本题这一步出错
否只是行政通知、告知指控、说明明天派律师 → 初次出庭通常不是关键阶段
结论只看列队辨认这一步 → 选 C

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然被告一到法庭就还没律师，那 initial appearance（初次出庭） 和 lineup（列队辨认） 都该算违规。

但考试真正问的是：哪一步真的会影响定罪结果。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

初次出庭只是通知指控、说明会指派律师，没让他做会伤到案件的决定，所以不是关键阶段。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干 起诉后列队辨认 属于 critical stage（关键阶段），律师缺席会影响辨认可靠性，所以这里只在这一步违反第六修正案。

❌ 概念混淆 | 起点认错

✕ A: 把“已起诉”误当成“每一步都要律师”。

❌ 事实误判 | 夸大初次出庭

✕ B: 把 initial appearance 说成要做实质抗辩的场合。

❌ 法律适用 | 双重违规误套

✕ D: 以为两步都算关键阶段，但初次出庭只是行政通知。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“司法程序已启动”，再逐步筛掉不算关键阶段的行政性程序。

考场速记

记住这句：先看司法程序是否开始，再看是不是关键阶段；post-indictment lineup 常考，initial appearance（初次出庭） 若只是通知和指派律师，通常不算。

再背一句：Rothgery 管“何时启动”，Wade 管“列队辨认要不要律师”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Without a warrant, police officers searched the garbage cans in the alley behind a man's house and discovered chemicals used to make methamphetamine, as well as cooking utensils and containers with the man's fingerprints on them. The alley was a public thoroughfare maintained by the city, and the garbage was picked up once a week by a private sanitation company. The items were found inside the garbage cans in plastic bags that had been tied closed and further secured with tape. The man was charged in federal court with the manufacture of methamphetamine.
Did the search of the garbage cans violate the Fourth Amendment?

choices.A: No, because the man had no reasonable expectation of privacy in garbage left in the alley.
choices.B: No, because the probative value of the evidence outweighs the man's modest privacy claims in his garbage.
choices.C: Yes, because the alley was within the curtilage of the man's home and entry without a warrant was unconstitutional.
choices.D: Yes, because there is a reasonable expectation of privacy in one's secured garbage containers.

questions.explanation:
The Fourth Amendment is violated when the government conducts an unreasonable search or seizure—ie, when police act without a warrant and no exception applies. A Fourth Amendment search occurs if one of the following tests is met:

  • Physical trespass test – the government physically intruded upon a constitutionally protected area to obtain information (eg, an intrusion upon the curtilage—the area immediately surrounding and commonly associated with a person's dwelling).
  • Reasonable expectation of privacy test – the government invaded a person's subjective expectation of privacy that society would find objectively reasonable.

In California v. Greenwood, the Supreme Court held that (1) public areas are not constitutionally protected and (2) persons have no reasonable expectation of privacy in items that are accessible or visible to anyone (including police). Therefore, police may freely inspect items left in a public area or exposed to the public.

Here, the officers did not conduct a search under the physical trespass test since the garbage cans were in a public thoroughfare located behind the man's house—not a constitutionally protected area (Choice C). Additionally, there was no search under the reasonable expectation of privacy test since the man had no objectively reasonable expectation of privacy in garbage cans that were readily accessible in a public alley (Choice D). Therefore, the officers did not violate the Fourth Amendment when they rummaged through the garbage cans.

(Choice B) The probative value of the evidence sought (ie, its tendency to make a fact more or less probable) cannot justify a violation of the defendant's Fourth Amendment right to privacy—no matter how modest. Instead, probative value is used to determine whether the evidence is relevant and admissible at trial.

📌 Educational Objective

The government does not need a warrant to inspect items left in a public area or exposed to the public since (1) public areas are not constitutionally protected and (2) persons have no reasonable expectation of privacy in such items.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • California v. Greenwood, 486 U.S. 35, 40–41 (1988) (recognizing that individuals do not have a reasonable expectation of privacy in garbage placed on a public street).
questions.zh-question:
在没有搜查令的情况下，警察搜查了一名男子房屋后的小巷里的垃圾桶，发现了用于制造甲基苯丙胺的化学品，以及带有该男子指纹的炊具和容器。该小巷是由市政府维护的公共通道，垃圾每周由一家私营环卫公司收走一次。这些物品是在垃圾桶内的塑料袋中发现的，袋子被扎紧并用胶带进一步加固。该男子在联邦法院被控制造甲基苯丙胺。

对垃圾桶的搜查是否违反了第四修正案？

zh-choices.A: 否，因为该男子对遗留在小巷里的垃圾没有合理的隐私期待。
zh-choices.B: 否，因为证据的证明价值超过了该男子对其垃圾的有限隐私主张。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为小巷位于该男子住宅的庭园范围内，无证进入是违宪的。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为个人对已加固的垃圾容器存在合理的隐私期待。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Search and seizure

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：警察在公用小巷里翻看垃圾桶，算不算第四修正案意义上的搜索。

三秒认题路径：

无令状 → 垃圾桶 → 公共小巷 → 无隐私期待 → 不构成搜索

核心法律规则

第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）只管政府做了不合理的搜索或扣押；先问有没有 搜索（search），再问有没有例外。

这里最关键的是两个门槛：一是 受保护区域（constitutionally protected area），二是 合理隐私期待（reasonable expectation of privacy）。放在公开可接触的地方、任何人都能看到或拿到的东西，通常就不算受保护。

California v. Greenwood 的考场意思：放在公共巷道里的垃圾，哪怕扎紧、封胶带，也没有可让你马上拦下警方的隐私保护。

核心判例： California v. Greenwood - 公共街道或公共巷道中的垃圾，没有客观合理的隐私期待，所以警方无需先拿令状。

思维导图

先问：这是不是第四修正案的“搜索”?
门槛 1：有没有进入受保护区域？
不是：垃圾桶在公共小巷，属于公开可接触区域。
门槛 2：有没有合理隐私期待？
没有：丢在公共巷道里的垃圾，社会不会保护你把它当秘密。
结论：两道门都没过 → 不是第四修正案搜索 → 选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：垃圾袋被扎紧、又用胶带封好，看起来很私密。

但考试真正问的是：这些垃圾放在 公共小巷 里后，法律上还能不能算“你能排除他人进入”的隐私空间。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以别被“封得严”带偏；决定答案的不是你主观上想保密，而是社会是否承认你在这个地点还有隐私期待。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的 public thoroughfare 说明垃圾在公共小巷里，依 Greenwood，这里没有客观合理的隐私期待，所以不构成第四修正案搜索。

❌ 概念混淆 | 证据价值误判

✕ B: 把 probative value 当成第四修正案理由了。

❌ 法律适用 | 侵入区域误套

✕ C: 把公共小巷硬说成 curtilage，题干事实撑不住。

❌ 事实误判 | 封装即保密

✕ D: 以为 secured garbage 就自动有隐私期待。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看地点是不是公开区域，再用 Greenwood 快速切掉“看起来很私密”的错觉。

考场速记

记忆口诀：California v. Greenwood - public place, no privacy。看到公共街道、公共小巷、可自由接触的垃圾，先默认“不用令状”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
FBI agents, without a warrant and without the permission of foreign law enforcement or judicial officers, entered a foreign country, kidnapped a businessman—a U.S. citizen wanted in the United States for drug-smuggling violations—on the street, and forcibly drove him back to State A. Thereafter, the agents, again without a warrant, broke into the State A home of the businessman's girlfriend and arrested her.
The businessman and his girlfriend were both indicted for narcotics violations. Both moved to dismiss the indictment on the ground that their arrests violated the Fourth Amendment.
How should the court rule on their motions to dismiss?

choices.A: Deny both motions.
choices.B: Grant the businessman's motion but deny the girlfriend's motion.
choices.C: Grant the girlfriend's motion but deny the businessman's motion.
choices.D: Grant both motions.

questions.explanation:
Grounds for dismissing indictment
Deficient indictment
  • Fails to charge actual crime
  • Omits elements of crime
  • Statute of limitations has run
  • Improper venue or jurisdiction
Defective grand jury
proceedings
  • Admission of unqualified grand juror
  • Exclusion of grand juror based on race/gender
  • Prosecutorial misconduct
Constitutional violation
  • Fifth Amendment double jeopardy clause
  • Sixth Amendment right to speedy trial
  • Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment due process clauses

An indictment is a written statement by a grand jury that formally charges a person with a criminal offense after a finding of probable cause. It can be dismissed for (1) defective grand jury proceedings, (2) deficiencies in the indictment, or (3) violations of certain constitutional rights. Here, both defendants moved to dismiss the indictment on the ground that their arrests violated the Fourth Amendment. But since a Fourth Amendment violation is not a proper basis to dismiss an indictment, both motions should be denied (Choices B, C, & D).

And even if an indictment could be dismissed based on a Fourth Amendment violation, the businessman's arrest was proper. Police can lawfully arrest persons:

  • outside their home if police have probable cause to believe that they committed a felony or
  • inside their home if police have a valid warrant authorizing their arrest.

Here, FBI agents kidnapped the businessman in a foreign country and drove him back to State A to face charges for narcotics violations. This arrest was valid since (1) it occurred on the street (outside his home) and (2) the police had probable cause to believe that he had committed a felony (drug smuggling). And under the Ker/Frisbie doctrine, a defendant can be prosecuted in the United States even if he/she was forcibly abducted from another country without a warrant or the other country's permission. Therefore, the businessman was properly indicted.

In contrast, the girlfriend's arrest was invalid since (1) it occurred inside her State A home but (2) the police had no arrest warrant. And though the court will not dismiss the indictment on this basis, she can move to suppress any evidence discovered from that illegal arrest at trial.

📌 Educational Objective

An illegal Fourth Amendment arrest is not a valid basis to dismiss an indictment, but evidence obtained from an illegal arrest can be suppressed at trial.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Crews, 445 U.S. 463, 474 (1980) ("An illegal arrest, without more, has never been viewed as a bar to subsequent prosecution . . . .")
  • Ker v. Illinois, 119 U.S. 436, 444 (1886); Frisbie v. Collins, 342 U.S. 519, 522 (1952) (holding that a forcible abduction does not preclude prosecution).

法院应如何裁定他们驳回起诉的动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回两项动议。
zh-choices.B: 批准商人的动议，但驳回女友的动议。
zh-choices.C: 批准女友的动议，但驳回商人的动议。
zh-choices.D: 批准两项动议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Arrest: unreasonable seizure of persons

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：非法逮捕（illegal arrest）能不能直接用来撤销起诉书（dismiss indictment），以及 第四修正案（Fourth Amendment） 受害后该走排除证据（suppression）还是直接打掉起诉。

三秒认题路径：

先看撤诉 → 再看逮捕 → 不看起诉书本身 → 只能排除证据 → 不能撤销

核心法律规则

起诉书（indictment）只会因为起诉书本身有缺陷、大陪审团程序（grand jury proceedings）有瑕疵，或少数明确的宪法问题而被撤销；第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）逮捕违法，通常不是撤销起诉书的理由。

考场意思：就算抓人方式不漂亮，案件也不自动消失；被告更常见的救济，是在审判里去压掉因此拿到的证据，而不是让法官把整个案子先删掉。

对本题来说，Ker/Frisbie doctrine 还会再补一刀：就算人是被强行带回美国，管辖与起诉（prosecution）通常仍然有效。

核心判例： United States v. Crews、Ker v. Illinois、Frisbie v. Collins —— 违法逮捕不等于不能继续起诉；强行绑回美国也不自动挡住 prosecution。

思维导图

题干先问：能不能因 Fourth Amendment 逮捕违法，直接把 indictment 挖掉？
第1关：是不是 起诉书自身缺陷 或 大陪审团程序瑕疵？
不是。这里只是抓人方式有问题，不是起诉书写错。
第2关：有没有能直接撤销起诉书的 宪法类别？
通常是极少数明确情形；第四修正案逮捕违法 不在这里。
卡死点：违法逮捕 ≠ 撤诉理由。
第3关：那救济去哪？
去审判里打 suppression，不是现在把整个案子撤掉。
加一刀：外国街头绑回美国的 businessman 还能起诉吗？
能。Ker/Frisbie 告诉你：强行带回，不会自动掀翻 prosecution。
结论：两人的撤诉动议都应被拒绝，对应答案 A。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然两个人都是被 warrantless arrest 抓的，那就应该都能把起诉撤掉。

但考试真正问的是：第四修正案 逮捕违法，能不能直接打掉 indictment；答案是不能，最多去争 suppression。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

另一个坑是把 businessman 的外国绑架写成致命漏洞；其实 Ker/Frisbie 逻辑正好反过来，强行带回通常不阻断起诉。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干争点是 Fourth Amendment arrest，但这类问题通常不能直接撤销 indictment；被告要找的是审判中的 suppression，不是先把案子掀掉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 撤诉救济误判

✕ B: 把 illegal arrest 误当成只撤 businessman、不撤 girlfriend 的理由。

❌ 法律适用 | 外国绑回误判

✕ C: 看到 forcibly abducted 就想当然判 businessman 赢，但 Ker/Frisbie 不给这个结果。

❌ 事实误判 | 两人同错偷换

✕ D: 把两次抓捕都当成能直接撤诉的同一种后果，忽略了本题根本没有这种救济。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“逮捕违法”与“起诉书缺陷”，再看能不能走 suppression，不要把救济层级看错。

考场速记

记住一句：illegal arrest 通常只管证据，不管起诉书；Ker/Frisbie 还会告诉你，强行带回美国也通常不挡 prosecution。

这类题先问“能不能撤诉”，再问“有没有 suppression”；不要把抓人程序问题直接升级成整个案件失效。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
A man was in jail after being arrested for burglary. When the police attempted to question him, the man invoked his Miranda rights and refused to answer any questions. The man was subsequently tried, convicted, and sentenced to a prison term for the burglary. Three years later, while the man was serving his prison sentence for the burglary, a police detective from a nearby town questioned him about an unsolved homicide. The detective did not know that the man had invoked Miranda at an earlier time. The man waived his Miranda rights and made several incriminating statements to the detective. When he was later charged with the homicide, the man moved to suppress these statements, claiming that his earlier refusal to waive his Miranda rights should have been honored.
Should the court suppress the statements?

choices.A: No, because the detective was unaware that the man had originally invoked his Miranda rights.
choices.B: No, because the man's prior invocation of his Miranda rights did not preclude the later interrogation.
choices.C: Yes, because the man had earlier invoked his Miranda rights, and the police were not permitted to resume questioning, even after a time lapse of years.
choices.D: Yes, because the man was incarcerated, and his earlier invocation of his Miranda rights shielded him from further questioning until he was released.

questions.explanation:
Fifth Amendment
privilege against self-incrimination
Custodial interrogation
Testimony under oath
Miranda warnings required
Rights invoked
(explicit & unambiguous)
remain silent
attorney
Rights waived
Privilege invoked
Privilege waived
Immunity granted
Honor request until:
  • attorney present
  • suspect resumes
  • 14 days (no custody)
Interrogate
Honor request
Question
Question

A motion to suppress should be granted if the defendant's statement was taken in violation of his/her Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination. To comply with this privilege, police must give a suspect Miranda warnings (eg, the right to speak to an attorney) before conducting a custodial interrogation. If the suspect invokes his/her right to counsel, any custodial interrogation must stop until:

  • the suspect's attorney is present
  • the suspect voluntarily reinitiates the interrogation or
  • 14 days have passed since the suspect was released from police custody OR was no longer subject to coercive pressures associated with police custody (Choices C & D).

Here, the man invoked his Miranda right to counsel during a prior custodial interrogation, after which he was convicted and sent to prison (released from police custody). Three years later, a detective interrogated the man about a homicide. Since more than 14 days had passed since the man was released from police custody, the detective was free to question him after he waived his Miranda rights. Therefore, the man's motion to suppress should be denied.

(Choice A) An invocation of the right to counsel is valid against all police officers—including subsequent interrogators who are unaware of the invocation. Therefore, the court would not deny the man's motion to suppress merely because the detective did not know that the man had invoked his Miranda rights in a prior interrogation.

📌 Educational Objective

When a suspect invokes his/her Miranda right to counsel, all police interrogation must stop until (1) the suspect's attorney is present, (2) the suspect voluntarily reinitiates the questioning, or (3) fourteen days have passed since the suspect was released from custody or free of coercive pressures associated with police custody.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • Arizona v. Roberson, 486 U.S. 675, 682–85 (1988) (recognizing that the invocation of Miranda rights extends to interrogations about other crimes).
  • Maryland v. Shatzer, 559 U.S. 98, 110 (2010) (holding that a break in the chain of custody ends Miranda protection).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子因入室盗窃被捕后入狱。当警方试图审问他时，该男子援引其米兰达权利，拒绝回答任何问题。该男子随后因入室盗窃罪被审判、定罪并被判处有期徒刑。三年后，当该男子因入室盗窃罪服刑期间，一名来自邻近城镇的警探就一宗未决的凶杀案对他进行了审问。该警探并不知道该男子早前曾援引过米兰达权利。该男子放弃了他的米兰达权利，并向警探作出了几项对其不利的陈述。当他后来被指控犯有凶杀罪时，该男子动议排除这些陈述，声称他早前拒绝放弃米兰达权利的决定应得到尊重。

法院是否应该排除这些陈述？

zh-choices.A: 不应排除，因为警探不知道该男子最初曾援引其米兰达权利。
zh-choices.B: 不应排除，因为该男子先前援引其米兰达权利并不妨碍后来的审讯。
zh-choices.C: 应排除，因为该男子早前已援引其米兰达权利，即使时隔数年，警方也不得恢复审问。
zh-choices.D: 应排除，因为该男子被监禁，他早前援引米兰达权利保护他免于进一步审问，直到他被释放为止。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：Miranda（米兰达警告）下，先前在别案里已经主张过律师权，不会自动把多年后的新一轮讯问永远挡死；14天离开羁押后，警察可以重新问。

三秒认题路径：

先前援引权利 → 后来新讯问 → 已离开羁押 → 超过14天 → 可再问

核心法律规则

只抓这条规则就够了

当嫌疑人在custodial interrogation（羁押性讯问）中明确要求律师，警方必须停问；但这个保护不是永久封死，Maryland v. Shatzer 说只要他已经离开警方羁押满14 days（14天），就可以重新开始问。

这里的关键是：考场看的是这次讯问前，前一次“援引律师权”有没有还在有效冷却期里；超过14天后，新的 Miranda waiver 一般有效。

核心判例： Maryland v. Shatzer — 只要离开警方羁押满14天，之前的 Miranda 律师请求不再挡住后来的讯问。

思维导图

先问：这次供述能不能压掉？
1. 先看是不是 custodial interrogation（羁押性讯问），是的话先有 Miranda 保护。
2. 他以前确实说过“我要律师” → 旧案里要停问。
3. 但他后来已被定罪入狱，等于离开原来的警方羁押环境。
卡死点：离开羁押满 14 天后，旧的律师请求不再继续拦住新案件讯问。
4. 三年后才问新 homicide，早就过了 14 天 → 新 Miranda waiver 有效。
结论： 不能压掉，答案选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然他以前已经喊过律师，那警察以后就再也不能碰他了。

但考试真正问的是：旧的援引有没有在 14天 内、还处在同一套羁押压力里；这题已经过了三年，早就断了。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键是：他在前一次案件里虽已主张律师权，但后来已离开原羁押状态三年，超过 14 天 后可以重新讯问，所以这次口供不用压掉。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“后来的警察不知道”当成关键点了。

❌ 法律适用 | 永久禁止误判

✕ C: 把旧的 Miranda 当成终身封锁。

❌ 事实误判 | 在押状态偷换

✕ D: 误以为“还在坐牢”就一定不能再问。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看是否还在 Miranda 冷却期，再查是否已离开羁押满 14 天。

考场速记

记忆口诀：先看 Miranda（米兰达警告），再看有没有 break in custody（脱离羁押）；满 14 days，旧请求就不再挡新问。

这题就是：先前援引律师权 ≠ 永久免问；Shatzer 让你记住“14-day break 后可重启”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Apply the Miranda break in custody rule

reason.en: Initiates Fifth Amendment interrogation protections under Miranda.
reason.zh: 在米兰达规则下开启第五修正案的审讯保护。

label.zh: 脱离羁押后流逝的时间

reason.en: Exceeds the 14-day window required to dissipate police coercion presumption.
reason.zh: 超出了消除警察强迫性推定所需的14天窗口期。

label.en: return to normal life in prison

reason.en: Under Shatzer, return to the general prison population is a break in custody.
reason.zh: 根据 Shatzer 判例，回到普通监狱服刑人员群体中构成了羁押的中断。

reason.en: Allows police to obtain admissible statements since custody was broken.
reason.zh: 由于羁押已被中断，此举允许警察获取具有可采性的供述。

reason.en: The procedural remedy requested by the defense to exclude the confessions.
reason.zh: 辩方请求排除口供的程序性救济。

reason.en: A subsequent officer's lack of knowledge does not validate an otherwise prohibited interrogation.
reason.zh: 后续审讯警员的不知情并不能使本应禁止的审讯变得合法。

B.text: did not preclude the later interrogation

reason.en: Correctly states the legal effect of the break in custody on the original invocation.
reason.zh: 正确阐述了羁押中断对最初权利主张的法律效果。

reason.en: Incorrectly asserts that the prohibition on questioning remains indefinite despite the break in custody.
reason.zh: 错误地声称尽管羁押已被中断，但对审讯的禁止依然无限期存在。

reason.en: Incorrectly assumes incarceration equals continuous interrogation custody for Miranda.
reason.zh: 错误地认为在监狱服刑等同于米兰达规则下的持续审讯羁押。

highlights.text: invoked his Miranda rights and refused to answer

reason.en: Sets the baseline protection that would normally prevent police from initiating further questioning.
reason.zh: 设定了通常会阻止警察主动发起进一步审讯的基准保护。

highlights.text: Three years later

reason.en: Indicates a lapse of time far exceeding the 14-day break-in-custody threshold.
reason.zh: 表明时间间隔已远远超过14天的羁押中断阈值。

highlights.text: serving his prison sentence for the burglary

label.en: prison environment as break in custody
label.zh: 在监狱服刑构成了羁押中断

reason.en: Establishes that the suspect was returned to his normal prison routine, which ends interrogation custody.
reason.zh: 确立了嫌疑人已回到正常的监狱生活，从而结束了审讯意义上的羁押。

highlights.text: waived his Miranda rights and made several incriminating statements

label.en: valid waiver following break in custody
label.zh: 羁押中断后的有效放弃

reason.en: Shows the defendant voluntarily waived his rights after custody was broken, making the statements admissible.
reason.zh: 表明被告在羁押中断后自愿放弃权利，使得该供述具备可采性。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A woman who is a computer expert decided to dedicate herself to exposing persons who trafficked in child pornography. She posted a number of sexually oriented photographs on her website. The file for each photograph contained an embedded Trojan horse program (a program that would allow the woman to enter the computer of anyone who downloaded the photograph). A man downloaded one of those photographs onto his personal computer. Using the embedded program, the woman entered the man's computer and found a file containing a pornographic photograph of a child. She copied the file and turned it over to a federal law enforcement agency. A federal agent told her that a successful prosecution would require more than one photograph and offered her a monetary reward for additional photographs leading to the man's conviction. The woman entered the man's computer again, and this time she found hundreds of child pornography photographs, which she turned over to the federal agency.
The man was charged with multiple counts of violating federal child pornography statutes. He has moved to suppress the photographs that the woman discovered on his computer. The motion is based on both the Fourth Amendment and a federal statute forbidding interception of electronic communication without permission. The parties have stipulated that the woman's conduct in downloading photographs from the man's computer violated the interception statute.
How should the court rule on the defendant's motion to suppress?

choices.A: Deny the motion as to all photographs.
choices.B: Grant the motion as to all photographs, because the woman acted without probable cause.
choices.C: Grant the motion as to all photographs, because the woman violated the federal interception statute.
choices.D: Grant the motion only as to the second set of photographs.

questions.explanation:
4th Amendment right to be free from unreasonable searches
Did government act?
  • government agent
  • private individual working on
    government’s behalf
No
No
violation
Yes
Was action a search?
  • physical trespass test
  • reasonable expectation of privacy test
No
No
violation
Yes
Was search unreasonable?
  • conducted without a valid warrant and
    no exception applies
No
No
violation
Yes
Violation

The exclusionary rule requires the suppression of evidence obtained in violation of the law or a defendant's constitutional rights (eg, from a warrantless search). Since this rule seeks to deter government misconduct, it only applies to the actions of government agents (eg, government employees, persons working on the government's behalf). Therefore, evidence is admissible if it was obtained by a private individual acting on his/her own behalf, without the government's knowledge or participation (eg, concerned citizens, vigilantes).

Here, the woman used an embedded Trojan horse program to conduct two searches of the man's computer. During the first search, the woman discovered a child pornography photograph. Since that search was motivated by her personal desire to expose persons who trafficked in child pornography, she was acting as a private individual without the government's knowledge or participation. Therefore, the exclusionary rule does not apply, and the court should deny the man's motion to suppress the first photograph.

Once the woman gave that photograph to the federal law enforcement agency, a federal agent offered her a monetary reward for additional photographs leading to the man's conviction. The woman then conducted a second search of the man's computer on the agency's behalf. Therefore, she was acting as a government agent during that search. And since the search violated the Fourth Amendment (no warrant) and the federal interception statute, the court should grant the man's motion to suppress the second set of photographs (Choice D).

(Choice A) Government agents generally need a warrant based on probable cause to conduct a Fourth Amendment search, but private individuals do not. Therefore, the fact that the woman acted without probable cause would only support the suppression of photographs obtained during her second (government) search—not her first (private) search.

(Choice B) Government agents generally need a warrant based on probable cause to conduct a Fourth Amendment search, but private individuals do not. Therefore, the fact that the woman acted without probable cause would only support the suppression of photographs obtained during her second (government) search—not her first (private) search.

(Choice C) Although the parties stipulated that the woman's conduct violated the federal interception statute, that stipulation only supports the exclusion of the second set of photographs (government search).

📌 Educational Objective

The exclusionary rule requires suppression of evidence that was illegally or unconstitutionally obtained by government agents—not private individuals acting without the government's knowledge or participation.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Jacobsen, 466 U.S. 109, 113 (1984) (finding that the Fourth Amendment applies to searches conducted by the government and individuals working on its behalf, but not private individuals).
  • Nardone v. United States, 308 U.S. 338, 340–41 (1939) (explaining that evidence obtained in violation of a federal statute is subject to the exclusionary rule).
questions.zh-question:
一名女性计算机专家决定致力于揭露贩卖儿童色情制品的人。她在自己的网站上发布了多张性导向的照片。每张照片的文件都含有一个嵌入的木马程序（一种允许该女子进入任何下载该照片者电脑的程序）。一名男子将其中一张照片下载到了他的个人电脑上。利用这个嵌入的程序，该女子进入了该男子的电脑，并发现了一个包含儿童色情照片的文件。她复制了该文件并将其交给了联邦执法机构。一名联邦探员告诉她，成功的起诉需要不止一张照片，并向她提供了金钱奖励，以换取能导致该男子定罪的更多照片。该女子再次进入该男子的电脑，这一次她发现了数百张儿童色情照片，并将它们交给了联邦机构。

该男子被控多项违反联邦儿童色情法规的罪名。他已提出动议，要求排除（suppress）该女子在其电脑上发现的照片作为证据。该动议的依据是《Fourth Amendment》和一项禁止未经许可（permission）截取电子通信的联邦法规。双方当事人已约定（stipulated），该女子从该男子电脑下载照片的行为违反了该截取法规。

法院应如何裁定被告的排除证据动议？

zh-choices.A: 驳回针对所有照片的动议。
zh-choices.B: 批准针对所有照片的动议，因为该女子在没有“合理理由”（probable cause）的情况下行事。
zh-choices.C: 批准针对所有照片的动议，因为该女子违反了联邦截取法规。
zh-choices.D: 仅批准针对第二组照片的动议。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Search and seizure

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：第四修正案（Fourth Amendment）只管政府行为；第一次搜电脑是私人行为，第二次搜电脑因政府奖励和指示变成政府代理搜查，才可能压证据。

三秒认题路径：

先看谁搜 → 再看政府代理 → 第一次私搜无排除 → 第二次公搜看压制

核心法律规则

排除规则（exclusionary rule）只压制政府违反宪法或法律取得的证据，考场意思：私人自己偷看、自己取证，通常不会因为第四修正案被排除。

政府代理（government agent）不是看名字，是看有没有替政府办事、政府知情参与或给出奖励指挥；一旦私人是替政府做搜查，就按政府搜查算。

无令状搜查（warrantless search）如果是政府搜查而且没有例外，就会触发压制；但私人的第一次搜查不触发第四修正案。

核心判例： United States v. Jacobsen - 说明第四修正案只管政府及其代理人的搜查，不管纯私人自行取证。
核心判例： Nardone v. United States - 说明违反联邦法取得的证据，也可能被排除。

思维导图

先问：是谁在搜？
NO只是私人自己找线索
第一次搜：私人动机，政府没参与 → 第四修正案不管 → 不压制
YES政府知情、奖励、指挥，私人替政府办事
再问：这次搜查是否无令状且无例外？
YES政府代理 + 无令状
第二次搜：替联邦办案 → 搜查违法 → 照第四修正案和联邦窃听法压制
NO有令状或例外
证据可能保留，关键不在“坏不坏”，而在“是不是政府搜查”
结论：第一次不压，第二次压

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然女方没有概率基础、还违反了联邦窃听法，那两次拿到的照片都该删掉。

但考试真正问的是：第四修正案和排除规则先看是不是政府搜查，不是先看她主观上有没有“抓坏人”的正义感，也不是先把所有照片一锅端。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

第一次搜查时她只是私人行动，第二次在联邦奖励和配合下变成政府代理；所以只压第二组照片。

❌ 事实误判 | 混成一锅端

✕ A: 把两次搜查都当成同一种身份，忽略第一次是私人取证。

❌ 法律适用 | 只盯概率

✕ B: 盯着probable cause不放，却没先问第一步是不是政府行为。

❌ 概念混淆 | 违法即全排

✕ C: 把interception statute一违就全删，忘了只压政府代理那次。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分身份，再看搜查性质；先切开私人和政府代理，答案就不会被情绪化事实带偏。

考场速记

记住一句：先看是不是政府搜查，再看有没有令状或例外；私人自己找出来的东西，通常不走第四修正案排除。

做题口诀：Government first, remedy second。先抓“谁在搜”，再抓“能不能压制”。

question_analysis.skill_tested: distinguish private searches from government searches

reason.en: Serves as the constitutional basis for suppressing evidence from unreasonable searches.
reason.zh: 作为排除通过无理搜查所获证据的宪法依据。

label.zh: 政府代理人关系触发物

reason.en: Converts the private individual's subsequent actions into state action.
reason.zh: 将私人的后续行为转化为政府行为（国家行为）。

reason.en: The procedural mechanism used to request the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence.
reason.zh: 请求排除非法获取证据的程序机制。

reason.en: Indicates the involvement of a government entity capable of state action.
reason.zh: 表明存在能够构成国家行为的政府主体的参与。

reason.en: The statutory basis for the suppression motion, stipulated to be violated.
reason.zh: 压制证据动议的成文法依据，双方约定已违反该法。

reason.en: Incorrectly assumes the second search remains private and unaffected by the government reward.
reason.zh: 错误地认为第二次搜查依然是私人搜查，不受政府奖励影响。

reason.en: Incorrectly applies the probable cause standard to the first search, which was purely private.
reason.zh: 将合理依据标准错误地应用到纯属私人的第一次搜查中。

reason.en: Incorrectly assumes a statutory violation by a private citizen triggers the constitutional exclusionary rule for the first search.
reason.zh: 错误地认为私人违反成文法会触发第一次搜查的宪法排除规则。

D.text: only as to the second set of photographs

reason.en: Correctly distinguishes the private first search from the government-sponsored second search.
reason.zh: 正确区分了私人的第一次搜查与政府资助的第二次搜查。

highlights.text: Using the embedded program, the woman entered the man's computer and found a file containing a pornographic photograph of a child.

reason.en: Establishes that the initial search was conducted purely by a private individual prior to government contact.
reason.zh: 确立了最初的搜查纯粹是由私人在与政府接触前进行的。

highlights.text: offered her a monetary reward for additional photographs leading to the man's conviction.

reason.en: Triggers state action by making the woman an instrument or agent of the government.
reason.zh: 通过使该女子成为政府的工具或代理人，触发了国家行为（政府行为）。

highlights.text: The woman entered the man's computer again

label.zh: 作为政府代理人的后续搜查

reason.en: Identifies the second search, which is subject to Fourth Amendment constraints due to the agency relationship.
reason.zh: 识别出第二次搜查，由于代理关系的存在，该搜查受到第四修正案的约束。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A federal grand jury that was investigating drug trafficking in the jurisdiction subpoenaed a witness to testify. The prosecutor advised the witness that he had a Fifth Amendment privilege not to testify if he so chose. The witness asked that his attorney be allowed to advise him inside the grand jury room, but the prosecutor refused to allow the attorney inside. After speaking with his attorney outside the grand jury room, the witness decided to testify. During his testimony, he made self-incriminating statements.
The witness was subsequently indicted for drug crimes. The indictment was based on the witness's grand jury testimony and on evidence seized in an unconstitutional search of the witness's home.
The witness has moved to dismiss the indictment.
Should the court dismiss the indictment?

choices.A: No, because the witness had no right to counsel inside the grand jury room and the illegally seized evidence did not affect the validity of the indictment.
choices.B: No, because the witness waived his constitutional rights by testifying.
choices.C: Yes, because the indictment was based upon illegally seized evidence.
choices.D: Yes, because the witness was denied his constitutional right to advice of counsel.

questions.explanation:
Rights & privileges that may be invoked at grand jury proceedings
Constitutional
rights
  • Privilege against self-incrimination (Fifth Amendment)
  • Equal protection (Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment)
  • Congressmen's privilege not to be questioned about legislative activities (speech or debate clause)
Privileges
  • Attorney-client privilege
  • Spousal privilege
  • Marital communications privilege
  • Psychotherapist-patient privilege

An indictment is a written statement by a grand jury that formally charges a person with a crime after a finding of probable cause. But since a grand jury only has the investigatory power to indict (not the judicial power to convict), a witness may only invoke certain constitutional rights during grand jury proceedings.

A witness may consult with an attorney outside the grand jury room (as seen here). But since a witness has no Sixth Amendment right to have counsel inside the grand jury room, the prosecutor had the right to refuse the witness's request to have his attorney inside. Therefore, the witness's self-incriminating testimony before the grand jury did not violate the Sixth Amendment, and the subsequent indictment should not be dismissed on this basis (Choice D).

The indictment was also based on evidence seized during an unconstitutional Fourth Amendment search of the witness's home. Pursuant to the exclusionary rule, illegally seized evidence should be suppressed at trial to discourage unconstitutional police conduct. However, the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings since the grand jury is an investigatory body—not a judicial one. Therefore, the illegally seized evidence does not affect the validity of the indictment, and it should not be dismissed (Choice C).

(Choice B) Though the witness waived his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination by testifying, he did not waive his Fourth or Sixth Amendment rights because they do not apply during grand jury proceedings. And since witnesses can only waive rights they possess, this is not a basis to deny the motion.

📌 Educational Objective

Since grand jury proceedings are investigatory in nature, only certain constitutional protections apply. A grand jury witness can consult with an attorney outside the grand jury room but has no Sixth Amendment right to counsel inside that room. And the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VI (right to counsel).
  • United States v. Mandujano, 425 U.S. 564, 581 (1976) (finding that a witness has no right to counsel inside the grand jury room).
  • U.S. Const. amend. IV (prohibition against unreasonable searches and seizures).
  • United States v. Calandra, 414 U.S. 338, 351–52 (1974) (holding that the exclusionary rule does not apply to grand jury proceedings).
questions.zh-question:
一个正在调查该司法管辖区内毒品贩运的联邦大陪审团传唤了一名证人作证。检察官告知该证人，如果他选择不作证，他拥有 Fifth Amendment 规定的不作证特权。该证人请求允许其律师在大陪审团室内为他提供建议，但检察官拒绝让律师进入。在与律师在大陪审团室外商谈后，该证人决定作证。在他的证词中，他做出了自证其罪的陈述。

该证人随后因毒品犯罪被起诉。该起诉是基于该证人向大陪审团提供的证词，以及通过对证人住宅的违宪搜查所扣押的证据。

该证人已动议驳回该起诉。

法院应否驳回该起诉？

zh-choices.A: 不应，因为证人在大陪审团室内没有获得律师帮助的权利，且非法扣押的证据不影响起诉的有效性。
zh-choices.B: 不应，因为证人通过作证放弃了他的宪法权利。
zh-choices.C: 应，因为该起诉是基于非法扣押的证据。
zh-choices.D: 应，因为证人被剥夺了其获得律师建议的宪法权利。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Right to counsel

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：大陪审团（grand jury）里，证人能不能因为“没让律师进陪审团室”或“材料来自非法搜查”就把起诉书打掉。

三秒认题路径：

grand jury → 律师进室内？ → 第六修正案 → 非法搜查证据 → 能否撤诉

核心法律规则

这题只看两条

大陪审团（grand jury）是调查程序，不是审判程序，所以很多审判阶段的保护不会自动搬进来。证人可以在室外咨询律师，但没有第六修正案（Sixth Amendment）要求律师必须坐进陪审团室；考试意思是：不能因为法官/检察官拒绝“律师进室内”就直接撤销起诉书。

另外，排除规则（exclusionary rule）主要是为了审判时排除非法证据，不是为了打散大陪审团的起诉决定；所以就算证据来自非法搜查，也通常不影响起诉书有效性。

核心判例： United States v. Mandujano + United States v. Calandra —— 前者锁定“律师不能进大陪审团室”，后者锁定“非法搜查证据通常不能用来撤起诉书”。

思维导图

先问：这是终局判决（final judgment）吗？
NO：现在只是大陪审团阶段的起诉问题。
再问：有没有法定中间上诉（statutory interlocutory appeal）？
再问：能不能走附带命令原则（collateral-order doctrine）？
三个关口：
1. 重要且独立？
2. 与实体争点分离？
3. 以后还能有效救济吗？这里会失败
结论：律师不准进陪审团室 + 非法搜查证据，都不是立刻撤起诉书的理由。
答案：A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然证人被迫在没有律师陪同下说了自我归罪的话，而且起诉材料里还有非法搜查来的东西，那起诉书应该不干净。

但考试真正问的是：能不能用这些瑕疵直接打掉大陪审团的起诉，而不是这些证据/陈述“看起来脏不脏”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的关键事实是 grand jury 里拒绝律师进室内、以及起诉依据含非法搜查证据；这两点都不足以撤销起诉书。

❌ 概念混淆 | 放弃范围误判

✕ B: 把自愿作证当成放弃所有权利，waived his constitutional rights 说大了。

❌ 法律适用 | 排除规则误套

✕ C: 只看到 illegally seized 就想撤起诉，忽略大陪审团阶段不吃这套。

❌ 事实误判 | 第六修正案偷换

✕ D: 把“可在外面咨询律师”偷换成“必须进室内陪同”，advice of counsel 不是这个意思。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定程序场景是大陪审团，再逐个排除“第六修正案”和“排除规则”的审判阶段思路。

考场速记

记住一句：grand jury 先看它是不是审判程序；不是的话，很多“看着很严重”的宪法错误也不一定能撤起诉书。

口诀：“In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely” 只记中间上诉例外；本题不是例外，本题是大陪审团调查程序，别把审判规则直接搬进来。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
Police officers received a report that someone had been murdered. Upon arriving at the scene, a police detective interviewed the only eyewitness to the event. The detective's report, which was delivered to the prosecutor, stated that the eyewitness could not identify the perpetrator of the crime.
A man was subsequently charged with murder. His attorney requested that the prosecution turn over all evidence favorable to the defense. The prosecutor substantially complied with the request but inadvertently failed to disclose the detective's report. At trial, the eyewitness identified the man as the murderer.
The man's attorney learned of the report after the man was convicted. On appeal, the man's attorney argued that the prosecutor's failure to turn over the detective's report violated the man's constitutional rights. He further argued that there was a reasonable probability of a different outcome had the report been disclosed to the defense.
Should the appellate court reverse the man's conviction?

choices.A: No, because the evidence impeached the eyewitness's testimony but did not exonerate the man.
choices.B: No, because the prosecutor did not intentionally withhold the detective's report.
choices.C: Yes, because the man was prejudiced by the prosecutor's failure to disclose the detective's report.
choices.D: Yes, because the man's attorney requested that the prosecution turn over all favorable evidence.

©UWorld

In Brady v. Maryland, the Supreme Court held that a defendant's due process rights are violated when the prosecution prejudices the defendant by failing to timely disclose evidence that is both:

  • favorable to the defendant – evidence used to negate a defendant's guilt or mitigate punishment (exculpatory evidence) or to discredit the prosecution's witness (impeachment evidence) and
  • material to guilt or punishment – there is a reasonable probability that, had the evidence been disclosed, the result of the proceeding would have been different.

Here, the prosecutor failed to turn over the detective's report, which stated that the sole eyewitness could not identify the perpetrator of the crime. This report was favorable to the man because it contradicted the eyewitness's in-court identification of the man. It was also material to the man's guilt because there was a reasonable probability that the result of the proceeding would have been different had the detective's report been disclosed. Because the man was prejudiced by the failure to disclose the report, the appellate court should reverse his conviction.

(Choice A) Evidence must be favorable and material to—but need not exonerate—the defendant to trigger the prosecution's duty to disclose. Here, the undisclosed report could have been used to impeach the eyewitness, and if it had, there is a reasonable probability that the man would have been acquitted. Therefore, the man's due process rights were violated.

(Choice B) Whether the prosecution intentionally withheld favorable and material evidence is irrelevant. What matters is whether the prosecutor's conduct (intentional or not) prejudiced the defendant.

(Choice D) Prosecutors have an affirmative duty to disclose favorable and material evidence to the defense—even if the defendant does not request it.

📌 Educational Objective

In Brady v. Maryland, the Supreme Court held that a defendant's due process rights are violated when the prosecution prejudices the defendant by failing to timely disclose evidence that is both (1) favorable to the defendant and (2) material to guilt or punishment.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV (due process clause as applicable to states).
  • Brady v. Maryland, 373 U.S. 83, 87 (1963) (recognizing that prosecution's withholding of favorable and material evidence violated due process).
  • United States v. Bagley, 473 U.S. 667, 682 (1985) (discussing when a failure to disclose evidence favorable to the defendant is material).

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Fair trial & guilty pleas

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：Brady 规则（Brady rule）下，检方漏交有利且重要的证据，是否足以让定罪被撤销。

三秒认题路径：

漏交证据 → 有利被告 → 重要证据 → 合理概率改判 → 可撤销

核心法律规则

考场上直接套的规则

Brady v. Maryland 的意思很直接：检方不能把对被告有利（favorable）且重要（material）的证据拖着不交。这里的“有利”既包括能削弱定罪的开脱证据（exculpatory evidence），也包括能打击控方证人的弹劾证据（impeachment evidence），考试意思：能不能让陪审团不信那个关键证人。重要（material）的意思不是“有点用”，而是如果交出来，reasonable probability 会改变结果。

核心判例： Brady v. Maryland - 只要漏交的是有利且重要的证据，即使不是故意的，也可能违反正当程序。

思维导图

先看：这是不是 Brady 型漏交证据？
① 有利吗？ 能否削弱控方证人
本题报告说唯一目击者“认不出凶手”，这正好能打脸庭审中的指认。
② 重要吗？ 是否可能改判
如果这份报告给了辩方，陪审团很可能不采信该目击者，结果就可能变。
③ 关键卡点 不是看检方有没有故意，而是看被告有没有被 prejudice（受损）
结论 满足 Brady → 可撤销定罪

考点陷阱

你可能会想：这份报告只是用来 impeachment，又不是直接证明他无罪，所以不算。

但考试真正问的是：它有没有同时满足“有利 + 重要”，而不是看它能不能单独把人洗白。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 C？

题干里的 sole eyewitness could not identify 直接削弱唯一指认证人，又有合理概率改判，所以属于 Brady 违宪漏交。

❌ 概念混淆 | 弹劾证据误读

✕ A: 把 impeached 误当成“没用”，其实它照样是有利证据。

❌ 法律适用 | 故意要件误判

✕ B: 你被 intentionally 带偏了；Brady 重点不是故意。

❌ 事实误判 | 请求条件偷换

✕ D: 以为“被告要过才算”，但检方本来就有主动披露义务。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“有利 + 重要”两把钥匙，再看是否存在合理概率改判。

考场速记

记忆口诀：Brady 只看“有利 + 重要”，不看检方是不是故意；能削弱关键证人的 impeachment evidence 也算。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A 17-year-old high school student decided to rob a convenience store. The student entered the store, brandished a pistol, and threatened to shoot the clerk unless she placed the contents of the cash register into a bag. After the clerk emptied the cash register, the student ordered her to lie on the floor and count to 500. To discourage the clerk from moving, the student fired the pistol at the floor immediately beside the clerk. The bullet ricocheted off the floor and struck the clerk in the head, killing her.
The student is now 18 years old and on trial for felony murder.
Can the state constitutionally seek the death penalty?

choices.A: No, because the death penalty cannot be imposed in felony-murder cases.
choices.B: No, because the student was under 18 years of age when he committed the crime.
choices.C: Yes, because the homicide occurred during the commission of an inherently dangerous felony.
choices.D: Yes, because the punishment is not disproportionately excessive in relation to the crime committed.

questions.explanation:
Eighth Amendment cruel & unusual punishment
  • No death penalty for:
    • juveniles
    • intellectually deficient persons
    • adults convicted of nonhomicide offenses
  • No life-without-parole for juveniles convicted of nonhomicide offenses
  • No mandatory life-without-parole for juveniles convicted of homicide

The Eighth Amendment prohibits the imposition of cruel and unusual punishments, including punishments that are inherently barbaric (e.g., torture) or disproportionate to the crime. It also prohibits imposing a death sentence on a defendant who was younger than 18 years of age when the crime was committed.

Here, the student is currently 18 years old, but he was 17 years old when the felony murder was committed. Therefore, the state cannot constitutionally seek the death penalty.

(Choices A and C) Felony murder is an unintended killing proximately caused by and during the commission or attempted commission of an inherently dangerous felony. If a felony-murder defendant is over 18 years of age, then the death penalty can generally be imposed so long as the defendant was not acting as an accomplice and did not kill, attempt to kill, or intend to kill the victim (not seen here).

(Choice D) The Eighth Amendment bars punishments that are so disproportionate to the offense as to shock the moral sense of the community. In Roper v. Simmons, the U.S. Supreme Court determined that imposing the death penalty for any crime committed by a defendant who was under 18 years of age meets this criteria. Thus, the state cannot seek the death penalty against the defendant here.

📌 Educational Objective

The Eighth Amendment's prohibition against cruel and unusual punishment forbids imposing a death sentence on a defendant who was under 18 years of age when the crime was committed.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. VIII (prohibiting cruel and unusual punishment).
  • Roper v. Simmons, 543 U.S. 551, 578 (2005) (holding that the death penalty cannot be imposed on a defendant who was a juvenile under eighteen when the crime was committed).
questions.zh-question:
一名17岁的高中生决定抢劫一家便利店。该学生进入商店，挥舞手枪，并威胁店员，除非她将收银机里的钱放入袋中，否则就开枪。店员清空收银机后，学生命令她躺在地板上数到500。为阻止店员移动，学生朝店员身旁的地板开了一枪。子弹从地板反弹，击中店员头部，致其死亡。
该学生现年18岁，正因重罪谋杀（felony murder）受审。
州能否在宪法上寻求判处死刑？

zh-choices.A: 不能，因为在重罪谋杀（felony-murder）案件中不能判处死刑。
zh-choices.B: 不能，因为该学生在犯罪时未满18岁。
zh-choices.C: 能，因为该杀人行为发生在一个本质危险的重罪（inherently dangerous felony）实施过程中。
zh-choices.D: 能，因为该惩罚与所犯罪行相比并非不成比例地过重。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Cruel & unusual punishment

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：死刑能不能对犯罪发生时未满18岁的人（juvenile）适用。

三秒认题路径：

未满18岁 → 罪时年龄 → 死刑限制 → Roper → 选 No

核心法律规则

先抓住规则，再看题干

第八修正案（Eighth Amendment）禁止残酷且异常的处罚（cruel and unusual punishment），包括对某些人群不能用的死刑。对犯罪发生时未满18岁的人（juvenile），州不能判死刑（death penalty）。

考场意思：他现在已经18岁不重要，关键看犯罪那一刻是不是未满18岁。只要是，死刑这条路就被堵死了。

核心判例：Roper v. Simmons - 罪行发生时未满18岁，不能判死刑。

思维导图

先问：这是不是终局判决？
YES终局后再谈上诉，不是本题路径。
NO继续看是否存在立即可救济的例外。
本题关卡：罪时年龄是否低于18岁？
是触发 Roper v. Simmons。
卡死点：未满18岁时犯案 → death penalty 不能用。
否才可能再看是否属于一般死刑规则。
结论：州不能合宪地寻求死刑。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他抢劫时开枪、又造成死亡，像极了felony murder，所以死刑应该可以。

但考试真正问的是：死刑能不能给“罪时未满18岁的人”，不是这次犯罪听起来有多恶劣。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以别被“他现在已经18岁”带跑，关键是犯罪发生时的年龄。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键点是：他在实施该起抢劫并导致死亡时只有17岁，而Roper直接禁止对罪时未满18岁者判死刑。

❌ 概念混淆 | 死刑绝对化

✕ A: 把 felony-murder 误当成死刑禁区，本题真正卡住的是年龄。

❌ 法律适用 | 只看危险性

✕ C: 只看到抢劫时开枪致死，就忽略了罪时未满18岁的死刑禁令。

❌ 事实误判 | 过度强调恶性

✕ D: 题目再恶劣，也不能把 disproportionately excessive 当成可以绕过 Roper 的借口。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定“罪时年龄”这个硬门槛，再判断死刑能否进入。

考场速记

记住一句：死刑看罪时年龄，不看现在年龄。如果犯罪发生时未满18岁，直接排除死刑。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man decided to rob a grocery store. During the robbery, he held a store clerk at gunpoint and hit the clerk in the face with the gun before fleeing the store. The police located the store clerk in the hospital the following day. While at the store clerk's bedside, the police officers presented a photo array of possible suspects to the store clerk and went through each photo without making any statements or gestures to him. The store clerk identified the man as the robber, and the man was subsequently arrested. Immediately after his arrest, the man was informed of his Miranda rights. He immediately invoked his right to counsel.
The man has been formally charged with armed robbery. Before trial, the man's attorney filed a motion to exclude the store clerk's identification.
How should the court rule?

choices.A: Deny the motion, because the man had not been formally charged when the identification was made.
choices.B: Deny the motion, because there is no right to counsel at a photo array.
choices.C: Grant the motion, because the man did not have the opportunity to select or object to the photos in advance.
choices.D: Grant the motion, because the man invoked his right to counsel.

questions.explanation:
Sixth Amendment right to counsel
Critical
stages
  • Post-indictment: lineups, in-person identifications, interrogations
  • Arraignments, preliminary hearings, bail hearings, pretrial motions
  • Plea negotiations & hearings
  • Trial & sentencing
Noncritical
stages
  • Pre-charge lineups
  • Photo-array identification
  • Fingerprinting, handwriting & voice exemplars, blood samples
  • Initial appearances, hearings to determine probable cause to detain defendant
  • Discretionary appeals
  • Post-conviction proceedings (eg, parole or probation hearing)

The right to counsel arises under the Fifth Amendment and the Sixth Amendment. The Fifth Amendment right to counsel arises when (1) a suspect is subject to a custodial interrogation and (2) the suspect makes a specific, unambiguous statement asserting his desire to have counsel present. Here, the man is challenging the store clerk's identification—not an interrogation of the man. Therefore, the Fifth Amendment right to counsel does not apply.

In contrast, the Sixth Amendment right to counsel:

• automatically attaches once formal judicial proceedings commence (e.g., indictment, filing of formal charges, preliminary hearing, arraignment) and

• applies during all critical stages of prosecution (i.e., any event where the absence of counsel may prejudice the defendant's right to a fair trial).

However, a photo array is not considered a "critical stage of prosecution" to which the Sixth Amendment right to counsel applies (even if the Fifth Amendment right to counsel is invoked). Therefore, the fact that the identification was made before the man was formally charged does not affect its admissibility (Choices A and D). Accordingly, the man had no right to counsel at the photo array.

(Choice C) The defense has no right to select or object to photos in a photo array before a witness sees it.

📌 Educational Objective

A suspect has no right to have his counsel present when a witness is shown a photo array that includes the suspect, regardless of when the photo array is conducted.

📚 References
  • United States v. Ash, 413 U.S. 300, 321 (1973) (holding that the Sixth Amendment does not require that defense counsel be present when a witness views police or prosecution photo arrays).
questions.zh-question:
一名男子决定抢劫一家杂货店。抢劫过程中，他用枪指着一名店员，并在逃离商店前用枪打了店员的脸。次日，警方在医院找到了该店员。在店员床边，警官向店员展示了一组嫌疑人照片（photo array），并逐一查看每张照片，期间没有对店员发表任何言论或做出任何手势。店员指认该男子为抢劫犯，该男子随后被捕。逮捕后，该男子立即被告知其米兰达权利（Miranda rights）。他立即援引了其律师权（right to counsel）。
该男子已被正式指控武装抢劫。庭审前，该男子的律师提交了一份动议，要求排除店员的指认（identification）。
法院应如何裁决？

zh-choices.A: 驳回动议，因为在指认发生时，该男子尚未被正式指控。
zh-choices.B: 驳回动议，因为在照片指认（photo array）中没有律师权（right to counsel）。
zh-choices.C: 批准动议，因为该男子没有机会事先选择或反对这些照片。
zh-choices.D: 批准动议，因为该男子援引了其律师权（right to counsel）。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Right to counsel

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：照片辨认（photo array）里，第六修正案律师权（Sixth Amendment right to counsel）通常不跟进，所以不能因为这里没律师就排除辨认。

三秒认题路径：

照片辨认 → 先看律师权 → 非关键阶段 → 不能排除 → 选 B

核心法律规则

第六修正案律师权（Sixth Amendment right to counsel）只有在正式司法程序开始后才自动附着，比如起诉、正式指控、预审或传讯；而且只覆盖 关键阶段（critical stage），考场意思：这一步缺律师会伤到公平审判。

照片辨认（photo array）不算关键阶段，所以被害人看照片时，辩方通常没有权利要求律师在场。这里的关键不是“嫌疑人后来有没有被捕”，而是“这个程序本身要不要律师”。

核心判例： United States v. Ash - 最高法院明确说，证人看警方或检方照片阵列时，辩方律师通常不必在场。

思维导图

先问：这是不是 终局判决（final judgment） 后的普通上诉问题？
不是。 题干是要不要排除辨认，不是判决已经结束后的上诉。
再问：第六修正案律师权是否已经进入这个程序？
不会。 照片辨认本身通常不是 关键阶段（critical stage）。
卡死点：没有“关键阶段”，就没有这一步的律师到场权。
最后落点：题干在考什么？
结论：即使之后正式起诉，先前的照片辨认也通常不因缺律师而失效。
答案：B，拒绝排除该辨认。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：人已经被正式起诉了，怎么还能说没有律师权？

但考试真正问的是：照片阵列当时是不是 关键阶段（critical stage），不是事后能不能补救。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的 photo array 不是 关键阶段（critical stage），所以就算后来正式起诉，也没有这一步的律师在场权。

❌ 概念混淆 | 事前起诉误判

✕ A: 把“是否已起诉”当成决定因素，忽略了照片辨认本身的阶段属性。

❌ 事实误判 | 事先选择错想

✕ C: 题干没给你先选或先反对照片的权利，object to the photos 不是规则。

❌ 法律适用 | 米兰达外推误判

✕ D: 把 Miranda 的认律师，硬套到证人看照片阵列上了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清是“审讯嫌疑人”还是“证人辨认”，再看有没有进入第六修正案的关键阶段。

考场速记

记住一句：照片辨认（photo array）通常没有 律师在场权（right to counsel）；先看是不是关键阶段，再决定能不能排除。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉记忆法，但本题不是上诉题，核心还是 关键阶段（critical stage）。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man was arrested and charged with arson. The indictment alleges that the man committed the crime three years ago. The defense has learned that the prosecutor had enough evidence to prosecute the man several months after the arson but made a good-faith decision to delay bringing charges to investigate whether others were involved in the crime. The man contends that the delay has prejudiced his defense because a friend who could have provided the man with an alibi has recently died.
The applicable jurisdiction does not have a statute of limitations regarding arson.
Has the prosecutor's delay violated the man's constitutional rights?

choices.A: No, because the Constitution does not protect a defendant from pre-accusation delay.
choices.B: No, because the delay was attributable to the prosecution's good-faith investigation of the crime.
choices.C: Yes, because the delay violated the man's right to a speedy trial under the Sixth Amendment.
choices.D: Yes, because the man's case was prejudiced by the delay.

questions.explanation:
The due process clause, along with state and federal statutes of limitations, protects criminal defendants from intentional and prejudicial pre-accusation delay. The defendant's due process rights may have been violated if a delay was used to obtain a tactical advantage for the prosecution or to harass the defendant. But there is no due process violation when delay results from an investigation conducted in good faith.

Here, the man was indicted for arson three years after the crime occurred. The man argued that this delay prejudiced his defense because an alibi witness has since died. However, the delay resulted from the prosecution's good-faith investigation of the crime—not from an attempt to gain a tactical advantage or harass the defendant. Therefore, the prosecutor's delay did not violate the man's constitutional rights.

(Choice A) The Constitution, by virtue of the due process clause, does protect defendants from pre-accusation delay.

(Choice B) The delay was attributable to the prosecution's good-faith investigation of the crime.

(Choice C) The Sixth Amendment right to a speedy trial protects defendants from post-accusation delay. Here, the man experienced a pre-accusation delay, so his Sixth Amendment rights were not violated.

(Choice D) Prejudice suffered by a defendant from a pre-accusation delay is one element of establishing a due process violation, but there must also be a showing that the prosecutor's delay was made in bad faith.

📌 Educational Objective

The due process clause protects defendants from intentional and prejudicial pre-accusation delay. However, delay due to an investigation conducted in good faith does not violate a defendant's due process rights.

📚 References
  • United States v. Lovasco, 431 U.S. 783 (1977) (holding that a pre-accusation delay does not violate a defendant's due process rights if the delay is the result of a good-faith investigation).
questions.zh-question: 一个男人因纵火罪被捕并被起诉。起诉书指控该男子在三年前犯下了此罪。辩方了解到，检察官在纵火案发生几个月后就有足够的证据起诉该男子，但出于善意决定延迟提起指控，以调查是否有其他人参与了该罪行。该男子声称，延迟损害了他的辩护，因为一位本可以为他提供不在场证明的朋友最近去世了。适用司法管辖区对纵火罪没有诉讼时效。检察官的延迟是否侵犯了该男子的宪法权利？

zh-choices.A: 不，因为宪法不保护被告免受起诉前延迟（pre-accusation delay）的影响。
zh-choices.B: 不，因为延迟是由于检察机关对犯罪的善意调查造成的。
zh-choices.C: 是，因为延迟侵犯了该男子根据第六修正案（Sixth Amendment）享有的快速审判权（speedy trial）。
zh-choices.D: 是，因为该男子的案件因延迟而受到损害。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Fair trial & guilty pleas

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：起诉前延迟（pre-accusation delay）有没有因为检方善意调查（good-faith investigation）而不构成宪法性侵犯。

三秒认题路径：

未起诉前 → 三年延迟 → 有善意调查 → 不是拖垮辩护就赢 → 选 B

核心法律规则

只看这条规则就够了

正当程序条款（due process clause）会保护被告免受故意、带有偏害的起诉前延迟（pre-accusation delay），考场意思：检方不能故意拖着不告来赚战术优势或骚扰你。

但如果延迟是为了善意调查（good-faith investigation），即使被告后来觉得自己吃亏，也通常不算违宪；这题里关键就是检方在查是否还有其他共犯，不是为了偷袭被告。

核心判例： United States v. Lovasco — 预起诉延迟只要来自善意调查，通常不违反正当程序。

思维导图

先看是不是 起诉前延迟（pre-accusation delay）？
YES三年后才起诉，属于起诉前，不走第六修正案迅速审判权（Sixth Amendment speedy trial）。
再看检方延迟原因：善意调查（good-faith investigation）还是恶意拖延？
善意卡死点：不是为了战术优势，也不是为了骚扰被告
虽然被告说alibi witness死了，辩护受损，但“受损”本身不够。
结论：正当程序（due process）未被违反 → 选 B

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然证人死了，辩护确实更难了，那就应该直接判被告赢。

但考试真正问的是：检方有没有用这段时间去偷战术优势，还是在认真查案。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，不是「物理上的证据有没有变少」。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的关键事实是检方在三年内一直做善意调查，所以这类起诉前延迟（pre-accusation delay）通常不构成宪法侵害。

❌ 概念混淆 | 权利来源误判

✕ A: 把due process当成完全不管起诉前延迟了。

❌ 法律适用 | 迅速审判错位

✕ C: 把speedy trial套到起诉前阶段。

❌ 事实误判 | 只看损害忽略原因

✕ D: 只盯着证人已死，却漏掉检方是good-faith调查。

这题建议用什么方法？

先锁定是起诉前还是起诉后，再看延迟有没有恶意或战术目的。

考场速记

记住：起诉前延迟（pre-accusation delay）看的是检方动机，不是被告有没有真实受损；Lovasco 这类题一见“善意调查”，优先选“没有违宪”。

口诀：In Certain Circumstances, An Appeal Can Be Made Prematurely 是中间上诉口诀，这题不靠它，别把“上诉例外”混进来。

question_analysis.skill_tested: Applying due process standards to pre-accusation delay

reason.en: Demonstrates the prosecutor's non-tactical, legitimate reason for delaying the indictment.
reason.zh: 表明检察官延迟起诉是出于合法的非战术性原因。

reason.en: Represents the required harm to the defense, though insufficient on its own without bad faith.
reason.zh: 代表对辩护造成的必要损害，但在没有检方恶意的情况下单凭此项不足以构成违宪。

reason.en: The primary defense against untimely prosecution, which is absent for arson here.
reason.zh: 应对不及时起诉的主要抗辩，但在本案放火罪中不存在。

reason.en: Incorrectly asserts that the Constitution offers no protection during this period.
reason.zh: 错误地声称宪法在控诉前阶段不提供任何保护。

reason.en: Defeats a due process violation claim since the delay was not for bad-faith tactical advantage.
reason.zh: 否定了违反正当程序的指控，因为延迟并非为了获取恶意战术优势。

C.text: speedy trial under the Sixth Amendment

label.zh: 第六修正案快速审判权

reason.en: Swaps post-accusation speedy trial rights with pre-accusation due process standards.
reason.zh: 将控告后的快速审判权与控告前的正当程序标准混淆。

reason.en: Fails to recognize that prejudice alone, without prosecutorial bad faith, does not violate due process.
reason.zh: 未能认识到仅有实际损害而无检察官恶意并不构成违反正当程序。

highlights.text: good-faith decision to delay bringing charges

reason.en: Establishes that the delay was not for tactical advantage or harassment.
reason.zh: 确定延迟起诉并非为了获取诉讼优势或骚扰被告人。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A defendant was tried for armed robbery. The state introduced evidence that a man, identified by witnesses as the defendant, entered a convenience store at 11:00 p.m. on March 5, threatened the clerk with a gun, and took $75 from the cash register.
The defendant did not testify, but his sister did. She testified that on March 5, at the time of the robbery, the defendant was with her in a city 300 miles away. On cross-examination, the sister admitted having given a statement to the police in which she had said that the defendant was not with her on March 5, but she claimed that the earlier statement was mistaken.
The court instructed the jurors that in order to convict the defendant, they had to find all of the elements of the crime beyond a reasonable doubt.
As to the defendant's claim of alibi, which of the following additional instructions would be proper?

choices.A: Alibi is a matter of defense and so must be established by the defendant; however, the burden of persuasion is by a preponderance of the evidence, not beyond a reasonable doubt.
choices.B: Before you may consider the defendant's claim of alibi, you must decide whether he has produced sufficient evidence to raise the issue.
choices.C: If the defendant's evidence has caused you to have a reasonable doubt as to whether he was the robber, you must find him not guilty.
choices.D: If you have a reasonable doubt as to whether the defendant was present at the convenience store at about 11:00 p.m. on March 5, you must find him not guilty.

questions.explanation:
Criminal defenses:  burdens & standards of proof
Negation
defense
  • Challenges element of crime (eg, alibi, lack of intent)
  • Fifth Amendment assigns burden to prosecution to prove element beyond a reasonable doubt
Affirmative
defense
  • Justifies or excuses criminal conduct, but does not challenge element of crime (eg, entrapment, self-defense, duress)
  • Statute assigns burden (prosecution or defense) & standard of proof (eg, preponderance, clear & convincing, beyond a reasonable doubt)

Due process requires that the prosecution prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, when a defendant asserts a defense that negates an element of the crime (eg, an alibi defense), the prosecution bears the burden of proof—not the defendant. However, the prosecution is not required to disprove an affirmative defense (eg, self-defense, duress) since it justifies or excuses the defendant's criminal conduct but does not negate an element of the crime.

Here, the defendant was on trial for armed robbery, which requires proof that he was at the convenience store at about 11:00 p.m. on March 5. Since the defendant's sister testified that he was with her 300 miles away when the crime occurred, her alibi testimony challenges an element of the crime that the prosecution must prove beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, the trial court should instruct the jury that if it has a reasonable doubt as to whether the defendant was at the convenience store, it must find him not guilty.

(Choice A) The burden of proof can be placed on the defendant only for affirmative defenses—not for defenses that challenge an element of the criminal offense (eg, alibi, lack of intent). Additionally, any level of proof can be imposed—eg, preponderance of the evidence, clear and convincing evidence, beyond a reasonable doubt.

(Choice B) A defendant must produce sufficient evidence to raise an affirmative defense, but not to raise an alibi defense since it negates an element of the charged crime. Instead, the prosecution must produce sufficient evidence to establish all elements of the criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt.

(Choice C) Although the jury must find the defendant not guilty if it has a reasonable doubt as to whether he was the robber, this jury instruction wrongfully places the burden of proof for an element of the crime on the defendant.

📌 Educational Objective

The prosecution must prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt. Therefore, the prosecution bears the burden of proof when a defendant raises a defense that challenges an element of the offense.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. XIV § 1 (due process clause).
  • In re Winship, 397 U.S. 358, 364 (1970) (stating that the prosecution must prove every element of a criminal offense beyond a reasonable doubt).

一名被告因持械抢劫罪受审。控方（州政府）出示证据，证明一名被证人指认为被告的男子，于3月5日晚11时进入一家便利店，用枪威胁店员，并从收银机中取走75美元。

被告没有作证，但他的姐姐作证了。她作证称，在3月5日抢劫案发生时，被告正和她在一起，身处300英里外的一座城市。在交叉询问中，姐姐承认曾向警方提供过一份陈述，其中她称被告在3月5日并未与她在一起，但她声称之前的陈述是错误的。

法庭指示陪审员，若要裁定被告有罪，他们必须毫无合理疑点地认定犯罪的所有要素。

关于被告的不在场证明主张，以下哪项附加指示是恰当的？

zh-choices.A: 不在场证明属于抗辩事由，因此必须由被告来确立；然而，其说服责任的标准是优势证据，而非毫无合理疑点。
zh-choices.B: 在你们可以考虑被告的不在场证明主张之前，你们必须判断他是否已提出充分证据来引出此争议点。
zh-choices.C: 如果被告的证据已使你们对他是否是抢劫犯产生合理怀疑，你们必须裁定他无罪。
zh-choices.D: 如果你们对于被告是否于3月5日晚11时左右在便利店现场存有合理怀疑，你们必须裁定他无罪。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Due process

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：被告拿出 不在场辩护（alibi defense） 时，检方是否仍要自己证明“人就在现场”这一构成要件，而不是让被告先把不在场证明到某个标准。

三秒认题路径：

不在场辩护 → 否认到场 → 检方担责 → 合理怀疑 → 无罪

核心法律规则

正当程序（due process）要求检方把犯罪的每个要件都证明到 beyond a reasonable doubt，所以凡是否认构成要件的辩护，举证责任都在检方。不在场辩护（alibi defense）就是在说“我不在案发现场”，它直接打掉的是“被告在便利店抢劫时就在场”这个要件。相反，积极抗辩（affirmative defense）只是承认行为发生了，再去解释“为什么不该罚”，这类才可能由法条分配被告去证明。

核心判例： In re Winship — 检方必须把刑事犯罪的每个要件证明到排除合理怀疑；所以本题不能把“在场”这个要件倒给被告证明。

思维导图

先问：这道题是在问“能不能把证明责任转给被告”吗？
是。 被告提出的是 不在场辩护（alibi），它否认的是“是否在抢劫现场”这个构成要件。
规则。 只要辩护在打构成要件，检方就必须继续证明；被告只要制造出合理怀疑即可。
卡死点：不能要求被告先“证明自己不在场”到某种程度；那会把要件证明责任倒置。
区分。 若是 积极抗辩（affirmative defense），才可能由法定规则要求被告承担某种举证负担。
结论。 只要你对“被告是否在便利店”有合理怀疑，就必须判 not guilty，对应正确选项 D。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然被告拿出的是“我当时在别的城市”的说法，那他是不是应该先把这个说法证明出来，法官才让陪审团考虑？

但考试真正问的是：这个辩护有没有打到犯罪要件本身。司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的不在场有没有先被被告证明」。

换句话说，alibi 不是让被告“额外拿分”的独立抗辩，而是直接告诉陪审团：检方还没有证明你要相信的那个关键事实。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 D？

题干的 不在场辩护 直接冲击“被告是否在便利店作案”这个要件；所以只要你对在场有合理怀疑，就必须无罪。

❌ 概念混淆 | 责任倒置误判

✕ A: 把 burden of persuasion 错放给被告了。

❌ 法律适用 | 先行证明误判

✕ B: 以为 sufficient evidence 是不在场的门槛，其实这里不是。

❌ 事实误判 | 责任主体偷换

✕ C: 看似对，实际把“有合理怀疑”这件事说成是被告去证明了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先看辩护是在否认要件还是在主张积极抗辩，再决定证明责任归谁。

考场速记

记住一句：alibi 不是“我来举证”的积极抗辩，而是“检方还没证明人就在现场”的要件攻击；所以只要对在场有合理怀疑，就直接判无罪。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.topic: The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context
questions.question:
A state grand jury investigating a murder learned that the key suspect might have kept a diary. The grand jury issued a subpoena duces tecum requiring the suspect to produce any diary. The subpoena made clear that the grand jury was seeking only the diary and not any testimony from the suspect. The suspect refused to produce the diary, citing his Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination.
Under what circumstances, if any, may the grand jury compel production of the diary over the suspect's assertion of his Fifth Amendment privilege?

choices.A: It may compel production without granting immunity, because the suspect was not compelled to write a diary.
choices.B: It may compel production if the suspect is granted use and derivative use immunity from the act of production.
choices.C: It may compel production only if the suspect is granted transactional immunity.
choices.D: It may not compel production of a private diary under any circumstances.

privilege against self-incrimination
Custodial interrogation
Miranda warnings required

Question

  • testimonial communication
    • oral testimony
    • act of producing document

Question
Question

The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination protects suspects from being compelled to provide self-incriminating evidence that is testimonial or communicative in nature (ie, testimonial communications). For example, the compelled act of producing a document is privileged if that act would prove that:

  • the document exists
  • the suspect possesses the document or
  • the document is authentic (ie, was created or written by the suspect).

However, the contents of a document are not protected by this privilege since the suspect was not compelled to create that content (Choice A).

Here, the grand jury compelled the suspect to produce any diary when it issued a subpoena duces tecum.
The grand jury believed that the suspect might have kept a diary, so the suspect's act of production would prove that the diary exists, that he possesses it, and that it is authentic (self-incriminating evidence). As a result, the act of production is a privileged testimonial communication.

But the grand jury can still compel production of the diary over the suspect's assertion of this privilege if the suspect is granted either:

  • use and derivative use immunity – prevents the government from using self-incriminating testimonial communications (and any evidence derived from them) against the suspect in any way that could lead to a criminal prosecution (eg, to obtain a grand jury indictment, at trial) or
  • transactional immunity – protects the suspect from being prosecuted for any crimes associated with self-incriminating testimonial communications.

While testimony can be compelled by granting the suspect full transactional immunity, it is not necessary because the narrower use and derivative use immunity is the minimum grant of immunity required to comply with the Fifth Amendment (Choice C). Therefore, the grand jury can compel production of the diary if the suspect is granted use and derivative use immunity (Choice D).

📌 Educational Objective

The Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination protects suspects from compelled testimonial communications—eg, the act of producing a document that would prove its existence, possession, and/or authenticity. However, self-incriminating testimony can still be compelled if the government grants use and derivative use immunity.

📚 References
  • U.S. Const. amend. V (privilege against self-incrimination).
  • United States v. Hubbell, 530 U.S. 27, 43–44 (2000) (finding that the act of producing documents is a testimonial communication that can only be compelled by a grant of immunity).
  • Kastigar v. United States, 406 U.S. 441, 452–53 (1972) (holding that use and derivative use immunity is the minimum grant of immunity required to comply with the Fifth Amendment).

一个正在调查谋杀案的州大陪审团得知，关键嫌疑人可能写有日记。大陪审团签发了一份携带物证传票（subpoena duces tecum），要求嫌疑人交出任何日记。该传票明确指出，大陪审团只寻求日记，而非嫌疑人的任何证词。嫌疑人以其根据 Fifth Amendment（第五修正案）享有的反对自证其罪的特权为由，拒绝交出日记。

在何种情况下（若有），大陪审团可以不顾嫌疑人主张的 Fifth Amendment 特权，强制其交出日记？

zh-choices.A: 可以强制其交出而无需授予豁免权，因为嫌疑人并非被强迫写日记。
zh-choices.B: 如果嫌疑人因其交出行为而获得使用及派生使用豁免权，则可以强制其交出。
zh-choices.C: 只有在嫌疑人被授予交易豁免权（transactional immunity）的情况下，才能强制其交出。
zh-choices.D: 在任何情况下都不得强制交出私人日记。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - The Fifth Amendment in a Police Interrogation Context

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：强制提交文件（compelled production of a document）时，第五修正案（Fifth Amendment）保护的是“交出这一步”本身，不是日记内容；若要强制交出，通常要给使用及衍生使用豁免（use and derivative use immunity）。

三秒认题路径：

传票要日记 → 不是作证内容 → 看交出动作 → 触发特权 → 先问豁免

核心法律规则

自证其罪特权（privilege against self-incrimination）只挡证言性（testimonial）或沟通性（communicative）的强制自证。考场意思：如果强迫你“说出”或“用动作承认”某件会指向你的事实，才会踩到第五修正案。

这里的提交文件的动作（act of production）本身可能在证明“文件存在、你持有、文件是真的”。考场意思：所以真正在自证的，不是日记里写了什么，而是你把日记拿出来这一下。

政府若给使用及衍生使用豁免（use and derivative use immunity），就能强制这类证言性动作；不需要一定给更重的交易性豁免（transactional immunity）。考场意思：最低门槛是前者，后者是更宽但不是本题必须。

核心判例： United States v. Hubbell - 认定文件提交的动作本身可能是证言性沟通；Kastigar v. United States - 说明用及衍生使用豁免已经够用。

思维导图

题干：大陪审团要你交出日记，先看“交出动作”是不是第五修正案问题。
第一层：内容本身？不是。日记内容不是你被迫“写出来”的，所以内容不受这道题直接保护。
第二层：提交动作？是。交出动作会承认日记存在、你占有、且可能是你写的。
卡死点：这一步是 testimonial，不能直接硬要，除非先给 use and derivative use immunity。
结论：不给豁免时，拒绝交出有理；给了最低限度豁免后，可以强制提交。
答案：选 B。

考点陷阱

你可能会想：既然日记内容可能很不利，那当然谁都不能碰。
但考试真正问的是：强迫交出这一动作有没有在替政府“证明事实”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以别把“没写成口供”误当成“完全没有第五修正案问题”；本题真正触发点是act of production，不是日记文字本身。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 B？

题干的subpoena duces tecum逼的是“交出动作”，这一步会暴露存在、持有和真实性；给use and derivative use immunity后，才可强制生产。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则渊源误判

✕ A: 把“没被迫写”当成“交出也没特权”，漏看了act of production。

❌ 法律适用 | 豁免层级误判

✕ C: 把更重的transactional immunity当成唯一门槛了。

❌ 事实误判 | 绝对禁止偷换

✕ D: 题干没说“绝对不能强制”，是忽略了可用豁免这条路。

这题建议用什么方法？

先抓“交出动作”是否证言性，再看政府有没有给最低限度豁免。

考场速记

记忆口诀：提交文件的动作（act of production）可能受第五修正案保护；要强制，就先找使用及衍生使用豁免（use and derivative use immunity）。Hubbell 记“动作有证言性”，Kastigar 记“最低豁免够用”。

questions.subject: Criminal Law and Procedure
questions.question:
A man sought medical assistance for a gunshot wound to his leg in a hospital emergency room. He told a police officer at the hospital that he had been shot. The officer interviewed the man about the incident while the man was receiving medical treatment. At first, the man stated that he had been shot while attempting to buy drugs on a street corner. However, the discrepancies between the man's wound and his description of the shooting made the officer doubt the veracity of the man's story. The officer knew that the man was unable to leave the hospital due to his injuries, so the officer reminded the man that he did not have to talk with the officer. In response to further questioning, the man revealed that he had shot himself with his own gun.
The man had previously been convicted of a felony, so he was arrested and charged with illegal possession of a firearm by a felon. The man moved to suppress the statement that he had shot himself because he had not been provided with Miranda warnings.
Which of the following standards should the court apply to determine whether the man was in custody for Fifth Amendment purposes?

choices.A: Whether a reasonable person would have believed that he could terminate the interview.
choices.B: Whether it was reasonable for the police officer to believe that the man had shot himself.
choices.C: Whether the man believed that he could leave the hospital.
choices.D: Whether the police officer had probable cause to arrest the man.

(Terry stop)

In accordance with the Fifth Amendment privilege against self-incrimination, police must Mirandaize a suspect before a custodial interrogation. A custodial interrogation is questioning initiated by a known (as opposed to undercover) law enforcement officer after a person is in custody. A person is in custody for Miranda purposes when the person is (1) placed under formal arrest or (2) restrained in his freedom of movement to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to leave.

Here, the man was confined to the hospital due to medical necessity and had not been placed under formal arrest at the time of questioning. This means that the man would have been in custody only if his freedom of movement was restrained to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to leave. Accordingly, the court should determine whether the man was in custody for Fifth Amendment purposes by considering whether a reasonable person would have believed that he could terminate the officer's interview.

(Choices B and D) The determination of whether an individual was in custody does not turn on whether it was reasonable for police to believe the individual's account of relevant events, nor does it turn on whether the information possessed by the police was sufficient to arrest the individual.

(Choice C) The test for determining whether an individual is in custody is an objective one that focuses on what a reasonable person faced with similar circumstances would have believed—not on what the individual subjectively believed.

📌 Educational Objective

A person is in custody for Miranda purposes when the person is (1) placed under formal arrest or (2) restrained in his freedom of movement to such a degree that a reasonable person would not feel free to leave.

📚 References
  • Thompson v. Keohane, 516 U.S. 99, 112 (1995) (providing that, if there has been no formal arrest, an "in custody" determination turns on whether a reasonable person would have believed that he could leave, given the totality of the circumstances).

一名男子因腿部枪伤在医院急诊室寻求医疗救助。他告诉医院里的一名警官他中枪了。警官在该男子接受医疗救治期间就该事件对他进行了询问。起初，该男子声称他是在街角试图购买毒品时中枪的。然而，该男子的伤口与他对枪击事件的描述之间的不符之处，使警官怀疑其说法的真实性。警官知道该男子因伤无法离开医院，因此提醒该男子他没有义务与警官交谈。在进一步的询问下，该男子透露他用自己的枪打伤了自己。
该男子此前曾被判犯有重罪（felony），因此他被捕并被控犯有重罪犯非法持有枪支罪。该男子动议排除（suppress）他自称打伤自己的陈述，理由是他未被告知 Miranda 警告。
法院应适用以下哪种标准来确定该男子是否为第五修正案目的而言处于羁押（custody）状态？

zh-choices.A: 合理的人是否会相信他可以终止询问。
zh-choices.B: 警官相信该男子打伤自己是否合理。
zh-choices.C: 该男子是否相信他可以离开医院。
zh-choices.D: 警官是否有合理根据（probable cause）逮捕该男子。

questions.zh-explanation:
MBE 考点解析

Criminal Law and Procedure: Constitutional Protections - Confessions & self-incrimination

本题真正考的是

一句话定位考点

本题真正考的是：米兰达拘押（Miranda custody）到底看客观合理人会不会觉得自己能结束讯问，而不是看病人主观想法或警察手里有没有足够逮捕证据。

三秒认题路径：

没被正式逮捕 → 看是否被拘押 → 客观合理人标准 → 能否结束讯问 → 选 A

核心法律规则

米兰达警告（Miranda warnings）只在拘押讯问（custodial interrogation）前才需要。拘押（custody）有两种：正式逮捕（formal arrest），或者自由被限制到合理人不会觉得自己能离开。这里的判断是客观的，问的是“同样处境下的合理人会怎么想”，不是“这名被问的人自己怎么想”。

所以这题只要盯住一个点：他虽然在医院里不能随便走，但那是医疗原因，不等于已经被警察拘押；因此标准是看合理人会不会觉得自己能terminate the interview，也就是能不能结束这次谈话。

核心判例： Thompson v. Keohane — 没有正式逮捕时，是否“in custody”看合理人在整体情境下会不会觉得能离开。

思维导图

先问：这人有没有被正式逮捕？
YES 直接进入 拘押（custody），再看是否存在 讯问（interrogation），米兰达问题通常成立。
NO 继续看：自由是否被压到reasonable person不会觉得能走。
卡死点：不是看他能不能离开医院，而是看他能不能结束警官的问话。
本题事实 医院里受伤 → 警官提醒可以不说 → 合理人仍会觉得可终止访谈 → 无米兰达拘押 → 选 A

考点陷阱

你可能会想：他已经因为枪伤待在医院、又被警察单独问话，所以一定算“被控制住”了。

但考试真正问的是：米兰达意义上的拘押不是“人能不能走出医院”，而是“合理人会不会觉得自己能结束这场问话”。

司法考试看的是「法律程序上能不能救济」，而不是「物理上的秘密有没有泄露」。

所以“我主观上觉得走不了”或“警察觉得他很可疑”，都不是标准。

正确答案与干扰项排除

为什么选 A？

题干的关键点是他没有被正式逮捕，且警官还提醒他可以不必说话；因此要看合理人是否会觉得能终止访谈，这就是Miranda custody标准。

❌ 概念混淆 | 规则源头误判

✕ B: 把believe the man当拘押标准了。

❌ 事实误判 | 主观感受偷换

✕ C: 只看他自己觉得能不能离开医院，漏掉了客观合理人标准。

❌ 法律适用 | 逮捕门槛错位

✕ D: 把probable cause硬塞进拘押判断了。

这题建议用什么方法？

先分清“医疗不能离开”和“米兰达意义上的拘押”是两回事，再套客观合理人标准。

考场速记

记住一句：Miranda custody看的是reasonable person会不会觉得自己能结束警察问话，不是看病人能不能走出医院。

以后见到“在医院、在车里、在路边”这类场景，先问有没有正式逮捕；没有的话，再问合理人会不会觉得可终止讯问。
